drills.name: Stork turns
drills.summary: Linked round turns on easy to moderate terrain, balanced on the outside ski. After a pole touch, the inside ski's tail lifts through the middle of initiation while its tip stays on the snow, and it comes back down through the middle of the finish. A tail that touches early shows balance drifting inside or back.
drills.terrain: Easy to moderate groomed slopes with smooth, edgeable snow, dynamic on a steeper blue; not ice, slush or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. More lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee; a deeper sidecut tightens the turn.
cautions: Never land the lifted ski in a wedge; set it down parallel, at hip width, on its little-toe edge.
Stop the drill when tired; a tired set-down is the risky one.

drills.name: Javelin turns
drills.summary: Linked medium-radius turns balanced on the outside ski with the inside ski lifted and crossed over it. The edges change on two feet; once the new outside ski holds, the inside ski comes off the snow and stays about level, pointing where the countered pelvis and chest face. The outside leg turns its ski underneath in the hip socket, so the lifted tip ends up across the stance ski's forebody from the fall line through the finish. In the transition the lifted ski is uncrossed and set down parallel, and becomes the new outside ski. The crossing must come from the stance leg turning, not from twisting the free leg across.
drills.terrain: Green to gentle blue groomed slopes with smooth snow; not ice, slush or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. More lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee; a deeper sidecut tightens the turn.
cautions: Uncross the lifted ski before setting it down, and set it down parallel at hip width; never land it crossed or in a wedge.
Keep the stance knee bent and over the foot while the thigh turns in; don't push the hips back to make room for the crossed ski.
Stop the drill when tired; a tired set-down is the risky one.

drills.name: Outside-ski turns
drills.summary: Linked medium-radius turns on the outside ski alone. The new inside ski comes off the snow before the edge change, so the stance foot rolls its ski from the little-toe edge to the big-toe edge on its own, and the lifted ski stays about level and parallel through every phase. At the end of the turn it is set down at hip width, takes the weight and becomes the next stance ski. The stance ski bends and leaves a round, brushed track; balance comes from angulation over one edge and fore-aft control along one ski.
drills.terrain: Blue to gentle black groomed runs with smooth, edgeable snow, softened rather than hard morning groom; not ice, slush or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. More lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee; a deeper sidecut tightens the turn. On one ski, canting and boot fit matter more, because one edge carries the whole lateral force.
cautions: Build up to it. Lift only the tail at first, as in stork turns, then the whole ski, and practise on easier terrain before blue to black.
Set the lifted ski down parallel, at hip width, on its little-toe edge; never in a wedge.
Stop the drill when tired; a tired set-down is the risky one.

drills.name: Thousand steps
drills.summary: Linked large turns made while stepping continuously from ski to ski. Each ski is lifted a little, kept about parallel to the snow, and placed back on its edge, so the skis leave narrow edged tracks and stay nearly parallel after the first diverging step into the turn. The stepping carries on through the edge change. Each leg flexes and extends on its own to move the weight across, under a quiet, stable torso, with the weight on the outside ski for more of each step.
drills.terrain: Green to gentle blue groomed slopes with smooth snow; not ice, slush or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. More lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee; a deeper sidecut tightens the turn.
cautions: Keep the steps small and the skis parallel; a diverging step that lands tip out can catch an edge.
Step with the legs, not by swaying the upper body.

drills.name: Extension transitions
drills.summary: Linked carved turns where the edge change happens high. As a turn ends both legs push the body up and forward across the skis; the skis go light at the top of the rise, the edges change, and the new outside leg meets the turn long and then flexes as the load builds. Compare with flexion transitions, where the skis cross under a body that stays low.
drills.terrain: Groomed blue runs with room for medium turns; dynamic on a steeper blue
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 14-17 m sidecut and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. Too little forward lean lets the rise go up and back; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Rise forward over the feet, not up and back; starting the new turn in the back seat is the knee injury pattern.
A hard push makes a hard landing; the turn must absorb what the rise took away.

drills.name: Flexion transitions
drills.summary: Linked carved turns where the edge change happens low. As a turn ends the legs keep folding, and the old outside leg is pulled up and under the body, so the skis cross under a body that barely rises and the new edges engage while the skier is still low. The legs then reach out to the side into the new turn. Compare with extension transitions, where the body rises over the skis instead.
drills.terrain: Groomed blue runs with room for medium turns; dynamic on a steeper blue
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 14-17 m sidecut and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. Too little forward lean turns the deep switch into a back-seat position; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Fold at the hips and knees with the shins on the tongues; folding at the waist or sitting back at the switch is the back-seat knee injury pattern.
Holding the low switch tires the thighs fast; rest before the burn sets in.

drills.name: Short-radius turns
drills.summary: Linked, rhythmic turns in a corridor about one groomer track wide. The pelvis and chest keep facing down the hill while both legs turn underneath them, so the skis swing from side to side below a quiet upper body. Each turn ends in a short edge set timed with a pole plant, and the rebound from it starts the next turn. Skied brushed or carved, at any setting.
drills.terrain: Groomed blue runs in a corridor about one groomer track wide; dynamic on a steeper blue or an easy black
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 12-15 m sidecut and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A shorter sidecut lets the skis carve a short turn at lower speed; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Stay over the feet at the edge set; a hard set from the back seat is the slip-catch knee injury pattern.
Hold the speed with turn shape, not by skidding harder and harder; stop when the legs burn.

drills.name: Long-radius carved turns
drills.summary: Linked, round turns across a wide corridor, carved arc to arc. The edges change before the skis turn, both skis tip together onto similar edge angles, and the tails follow the tips in two thin tracks. The edge builds steadily from the edge change to its most in late shaping, then lets go. The outside leg lengthens a little into the turn, stays long and steady through shaping, and flexes to absorb the load that peaks below the fall line; the inside leg shortens, its hip held up and its foot a little ahead.
drills.terrain: Smooth groomed blue to steeper blue with room for turns about three groomer widths across; firm, edgeable snow, not ice; a quiet slope with a clear view
drills.equipment: Efforts assume a long-turn carving ski of about 20 m sidecut radius, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A shorter-radius ski carves these speeds only in tighter turns; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Speed builds quickly in carved turns; ski them only where you can see the whole turn and the slope below is clear.
If the outside ski slips, don't straighten the leg hard to catch the edge; stay forward and flexed and let it grip again.
Stop when the legs tire; knee injuries cluster late in runs.

drills.name: One-footed railroad-track turns
drills.summary: Railroad-track turns on one ski for a whole run, then on the other. The stance ski is rolled from edge to edge with no steering and leaves a thin carved track, while the lifted ski is held quiet, parallel to the snow, and tipped in step as if it were on the snow. The turns alternate between the stance ski's big-toe edge, as the outside ski, and its harder little-toe edge, as the inside ski; balance on the one edge comes from the ankle and foot under a quiet upper body, helped by a little upper-body angulation, never by leaning on the poles.
drills.terrain: Gentle green groomed slopes, flat enough to stay near the fall line without gaining speed; smooth, edgeable snow
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 15 m sidecut radius, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A snug, well-canted boot matters more on one ski, and the little-toe-edge turns need it most.
cautions: Learn it with about 90 % of the weight on one foot before lifting the other ski fully.
If you lose balance, put the lifted ski down parallel and at hip width, not wide in a wedge.
Ski both legs; the little-toe-edge turns are harder, so expect one direction to feel weaker.

drills.name: Railroad-track turns
drills.summary: Linked shallow turns down a narrow corridor on gentle terrain, made only by rolling both skis from one pair of edges, through flat, onto the other, with no steering. The inside foot leads the roll, both skis tip at the same rate, and the tails follow the tips in two thin tracks. The edge stays small, building to its most at the fall line and rolling back to flat, while the trunk stays quiet over the skis. One-footed railroad tracks are a separate drill.
drills.terrain: Gentle green groomed slopes with smooth, edgeable snow and a run-out; a corridor about one groomer width wide
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 15 m sidecut radius, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A deeper sidecut makes a rounder track at the same small edge; a stiff or upright cuff makes the small roll inside the boot harder to feel.
cautions: Choose a slope gentle enough that speed stays low without steering; on steeper terrain the drill turns into skidded turns or a runaway.
Roll the inside foot first; putting the new outside ski on its big-toe edge first is the habit the drill is meant to break.

drills.name: Falling leaf
drills.summary: A sideslip down a corridor that drifts forward, then backward, like a leaf falling, with the same ski downhill the whole way. Moving the pressure toward the balls of the feet with the ankles, and letting the tips steer slightly down, takes the skis forward; easing it toward the heels takes them backward. The body keeps facing down the hill and the edges keep the slide steady.
drills.terrain: Smooth groomed slopes steep enough to slide sideways, from a blue when gentle to a steep blue when dynamic; firm snow, not ice or deep snow
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis with normally tuned edges, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp and about 42 mm stand height. A boot too stiff in front makes the forward segment hard to start; too little forward lean puts the backward segment on the tails.
cautions: Go backward with the ankles, not by sitting back; leaning on the back of the boots is the backward-fall position that loads the knee.
Keep the slide in a corridor; drifting into a traverse means the upper body is steering.

drills.name: Hockey stops
drills.summary: From a straight run down the fall line, both skis are pivoted quickly and together across the hill under a body that keeps facing down it, then edged progressively into a braking skid to a full stop. The legs turn at the same rate; angulation over the downhill ski holds the edges as the skis slow.
drills.terrain: Smooth groomed slopes with room to run straight, from a green when gentle to a blue when dynamic; firm, edgeable snow, not ice or deep snow
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis with normally tuned edges, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp and about 42 mm stand height. Sharp edges, a high stand height or hard snow make the edges bite sooner and harder; shorter skis pivot more easily.
cautions: Build the edge progressively; an abrupt edge set with the weight back can catch the downhill ski and twist the knee.
Pivot the legs, not the shoulders; throwing the upper body around spins the skier to face across the hill.
Stop well clear of other skiers and check uphill before starting again.

drills.name: Pivot slips
drills.summary: Down a corridor little wider than the skis are long, the skier sideslips, flattens the skis and pivots them a half circle under the feet, through the fall line, into a sideslip facing the other way, again and again. The pelvis and chest keep facing down the hill the whole time; the thighs turn in the hip sockets, the skis stay flat and parallel, and the pivot point stays under the middle of the feet.
drills.terrain: Smooth groomed slopes, from an easy blue when gentle to a steeper blue when dynamic, in a narrow corridor; firm snow that lets flat skis turn, not ice or deep snow
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis with normally tuned edges, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp and about 42 mm stand height. Shorter, lighter skis pivot more easily; sharp edges, a high stand height or hard snow make an edge catch sooner.
cautions: Flatten the skis before turning them; an edge that catches mid-pivot twists the knee.
Turn the legs, not the shoulders; a rotating upper body spins the whole skier and leaves the trunk muscles idle.

drills.name: Sideslips
drills.summary: Skis parallel and across the hill, the body facing down it. Rolling the knees and ankles down the hill flattens the skis so they slide sideways down a narrow corridor at a steady rate; rolling them back into the hill sets the edges and stops. In the diagonal version the skis slide forward and down along a steady line. The edges, not the upper body, set the speed.
drills.terrain: Smooth groomed slopes steep enough to slide sideways, from a blue when gentle to a steep blue or easy black when dynamic; firm snow, not ice or deep snow
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis with normally tuned edges, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp and about 42 mm stand height. Sharp edges, a high stand height or hard snow make the slip grabby and the edge set sudden; wide or detuned skis slide more easily.
cautions: Set the edges progressively; an abrupt edge set with the weight back can catch the downhill ski and twist the knee.
Lean out over the downhill ski, not into the hill; leaning in locks the edges or lets the feet slide out.

drills.name: Carved J-turns
drills.summary: A single carved arc, then the same the other way. From a run in or near the fall line, both skis are tipped onto their edges from the feet, ankles and knees, early and progressively, so they bend from the centre and leave two clean parallel lines. The arc leaves the fall line, crosses the hill and climbs until the skier stops in balance, with angulation growing as speed falls. Skidded tails or a lean into the hill show the edge came from the body, not the legs.
drills.terrain: Gentle green to easy blue groomed slopes with a clear run-out across the hill; smooth, edgeable snow, not ice
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 15 m sidecut radius and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. The arc's radius comes from the edge angle and the sidecut, so a deeper sidecut carves a tighter arc at the same edge; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Pick a slope with an empty run-out across and above you; the arc ends up the hill and other skiers come from above.
Stop by holding the edge and letting the arc climb, not by sitting back; a back-weighted stop loads the knee through the boot.
Keep both skis tipped; an uphill ski that catches and drifts out into a wedge twists the knee.

drills.name: Crab wedge turns
drills.summary: Linked wedge turns on gentle terrain where only the outside ski's edge angle rises. The wedge keeps its size; the outside ski is tipped up from the ankle and by turning the thigh in, bends and leaves a thin carved line, so the ski's sidecut makes the turn, while the flatter inside ski brushes. The upper body stays over the outside ski. There is no edge change; each ski stays on its big-toe edge and only its edge angle rises and falls.
drills.terrain: Gentle green groomed slopes with smooth, edgeable snow; not ice or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 13-15 m sidecut radius and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. The carved radius is set by sidecut and edge angle, so a deeper sidecut needs less edge for the same turn and a straighter ski needs more; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee.
cautions: Tip the outside ski with the ankle and by turning the thigh in; never by letting the knee cave in over the foot.
Keep the inside ski flat enough to brush. An inside edge that catches twists the knee inward, the classic wedge injury.
Keep it slow and the wedge small; a wide wedge with the weight back loads the knees most.

drills.name: Dolphin turns
drills.summary: Linked medium-radius turns that work the fore-aft range. Through the finish the ankles open and the feet slide ahead, so the pressure runs back to the tails; the tails bend and the tips lift off the snow. In the transition both legs pull up under the hips and the toes pull up, so the tips point down and land first on their new edges, and the new turn grips and bends from the forebody. Aft is a short moment at the end of each turn, never a position.
drills.terrain: Groomed blue slopes with smooth, edgeable snow; not ice, ruts or crowded pistes, where a tail-heavy finish is hard to recover
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis of about 15 m sidecut with a little tip rocker, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, a firm but progressive rear spoiler, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A stiffer tail or a forward mount lifts the tips sooner; a centre mount or a short ski makes the fore-aft range harder to use; a very stiff spoiler hardens the push at the finish. More lean or ramp deepens the knee.
cautions: Aft is a moment at the end of the turn, not a stance; if the hips stay behind the feet into the next turn, stop and start again from a centred straight run.
Never land on the tails with straight legs; point the tips down and land on them with the legs bent.
Keep the hips above the knees as the tails load; sitting low and back is the knee-injury position.
Learn it slowly on a gentle blue with small tip lifts before adding speed.

drills.name: Straight run on one ski
drills.summary: A straight glide down the fall line on gentle terrain, balanced on one flat ski. The other ski's tail is held off the snow at a steady height with its tip resting on the snow and the ski parallel to the stance ski; some associations simply lift the foot. The stance ski stays flat, rolled onto neither edge, while the body stays centred over the middle of the foot and faces down the run. Repeat on the other leg.
drills.terrain: Gentle, smooth groomed green terrain with a flat run-out; not ice or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. Boot canting matters most in this drill, because a badly canted boot sets a flat ski on an edge that the ankle must then fight; more lean or ramp deepens the knee, and a higher stand height gives a tipped ski more leverage on the ankle.
cautions: Choose a slope with a flat run-out; on one flat ski, a fall sideways comes quickly.
Set the lifted ski down flat, parallel and at hip width, never angled into a wedge.
Stop the drill when tired; balance corrections get late and large with fatigue.

drills.name: Tic-tac turns
drills.summary: Short linked turns where the edge change is stepped. After a pole plant, the new outside ski is lifted and reached down onto its new edge a little out from under the body (tic), then the new inside ski is lifted and set on its new edge at hip width, not under the body (tac); both skis then finish the turn on their edges. Done slowly the two steps are separate; as the tempo rises they overlap until both skis are briefly in the air. Stepping onto the new edges lets the body fall into the turn and grip early, above the fall line.
drills.terrain: A very gentle groomed slope to start, then easy to moderate groomed pistes; firm, smooth snow, not ice, slush or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational carving skis with a short-turn sidecut and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. More lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds edge leverage but loads the knee; a deeper sidecut tightens the turn. A soft boot cuff lets a landing fall back onto the tails.
cautions: Land each ski with the shin on the tongue and the knee bent, never back on the tail with the leg straight.
Set the inside ski down on its little-toe edge at hip width; a ski set wide on its big-toe edge can catch in a wedge and twist the knee.
Leave the airborne version until the separate steps are clean and the pitch allows it; stop when tired.

drills.name: Wedge turns
drills.summary: Linked medium-radius turns in a gliding wedge, tips closer than tails, slow enough that a parallel turn would not come easily. Both legs turn in the hip sockets to steer, pivoting the skis under the feet rather than pushing the tails out. Both skis stay on their big-toe edges with no edge change; the outside ski is edged more and carries more weight, the inside ski goes a little flatter so it can steer. The body moves toward each new outside ski but stays between the feet, and the wedge keeps the same size all the way.
drills.terrain: Easy groomed green slopes, gentle enough to glide at a steady slow speed; not steep enough to force a big braking wedge
drills.equipment: Efforts assume recreational skis of any sidecut, since the wedge is steered rather than carved, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A boot with too little lean, or too stiff to flex, lets the shin stand upright and the skier sit back in the wedge, which loads the quadriceps and the knee.
cautions: Keep the wedge small and the speed slow; a big wedge on steeper snow grips at the tails, stops the steering and invites sitting back.
A caught inside edge twists the knee inward; keep the skis gliding on low edges and the knees over the feet.

drills.name: Whitepass turns
drills.summary: Linked medium-to-large carved turns skied mostly on one ski at a time. Out of each turn the inside ski is lifted and the outside ski alone finishes the turn, then changes edges on its own and starts the next turn as the inside ski, on its little-toe edge, with the new outside ski held up level beside it. Near the fall line the outside leg extends to set its ski down, both skis share the snow for a moment, and angulation hands the load to the outside ski. The body must commit inside the new turn; staying over a flat ski is the common failure.
drills.terrain: Blue to gentle black groomed slopes with smooth, edgeable snow; not ice or ruts
drills.equipment: Efforts assume carving skis with a sidecut radius of about 16-20 m, and boots with about 15° of cuff lean, about 0.9° of binding ramp (4.7 mm) and about 42 mm stand height. A shorter sidecut tightens the arcs at the same speed; more lean or ramp deepens the knee; a higher stand height adds the edge leverage the little-toe edge needs but loads the knee.
cautions: Learn it in parts on easy terrain first, one-ski traverses on either ski, then uphill arcs on the outside ski and downhill arcs on the inside ski, before linking turns.
Set the outside ski down parallel, at hip width, already on its big-toe edge and with the leg bent; a wide, tip-out or straight-legged landing can catch.
Stop the drill when tired; the single-leg finish is its highest load.

stork-turn.name: Turn balanced on the outside ski, inside tail held up

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the feet are drawn back and the shin presses into the tongue while the body crosses over; flexed about as far as it goes in the turn
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and the feet back

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load to the fall line, then opens a little as the foot starts forward; a little more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves toward the heel
finish.cue: Let the foot slide ahead as the turn ends

initiation.action: Flexed with the shin in the tongue as the tail lifts, so the ski pitches tip down
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the tip resting on the snow; the ski's longer, heavier forebody and the snow under the tip balance it, so little ankle effort is needed
shaping.cue: Tip resting on the snow, not pressed

finish.action: Stays closed, shin on the tongue, while the tail comes down by knee and hip extension, ready to become the new outside ski
finish.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the tail comes down

initiation.action: Begins to evert inside the boot, rolling the ski onto its big-toe edge
initiation.cue: Roll onto the big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, below the fall line, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski, with constant small corrections on the one edge
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line; the edge angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Holds, then releases toward flat through the finish into the transition
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends

initiation.action: Inverts so the lifted ski tips onto its little-toe edge with the stance ski
initiation.cue: Tip the lifted ski the same way as the stance ski

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the stance ski's edge
shaping.cue: Keep the lifted ski tilted with the stance ski

finish.action: Tilt held as the ski is set down on its little-toe edge, ready for the edge change
finish.cue: Set it down parallel, at hip width, on its little-toe edge alongside the stance ski

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the whole load
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

shaping.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

finish.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the new turn loads
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds; deeper the harder the turn, about 60° gentle, 65° moderate, 71° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long, strong and steady on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 68° gentle, 74° moderate, 81° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends

initiation.action: Flexes to raise the tail just after the pole touch, once the body has tipped into the turn and the new outside ski holds; knee flexion gives the tail-up pitch
initiation.cue: Touch, tip in, then lift the inside heel toward your seat

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee, heel drawn toward the seat
shaping.cue: Heel toward your seat; the tip stays on the snow

finish.action: Lengthens with the hip to set the tail down through the middle of the finish
finish.cue: Lower the tail, don't drop it

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

shaping.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Set the ski down straight

initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

shaping.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Set the ski down without the knee caving in

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens into the new turn
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip with the pelvis countered, about 48° gentle, 55° moderate, 63° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist; deeper with speed and pitch

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the transition, about 62° gentle, 70° moderate, 78° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to finish

initiation.action: Flexes to hold the thigh up while the knee bends to lift the tail; hip flexion shortens the leg as a whole
initiation.cue: Bring the inside thigh up a little; the tip stays on the snow

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip, the hip flexors holding the thigh up
shaping.cue: Inside thigh held up a little, tip on the snow

finish.action: Lowered to set the tail down
finish.cue: Lower the leg under control

initiation.action: The pelvis tips over the stance thigh as the legs tilt in, so the inside half rises; the outside abductors hike it, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up

shaping.action: Hip angulation keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, the outside hip carrying the unsupported inside half of the pelvis
shaping.moment: Abduction
shaping.cue: Stay strong over the outside hip; the angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases through the finish as the legs come upright and the inside ski returns to the snow
finish.cue: Level the hips as the tail comes down

initiation.action: Kept at hip width as the tail lifts, neither drawn in nor out; the net moment is near zero
initiation.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

shaping.action: Held at hip width beside the stance leg
shaping.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

finish.action: Held, then the foot is set down at hip width
finish.cue: Set the foot down at hip width, not wide

initiation.action: Turns inward a little, the thigh rotating under the pelvis to steer and tip the ski
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh in the hip socket

shaping.action: Held turned in as the ski turns
shaping.moment: Small; internal (steering) in a brushed turn, external (braking) if carved, extrapolated from a modelled carved GS turn
shaping.cue: Keep the knee over the foot as the ski turns

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the release
finish.cue: Let the thigh unwind with the release

initiation.action: Turns outward with the turn so the lifted ski stays parallel
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted ski parallel

shaping.action: Held turned out; the external rotators resist tip drag, the inside tip being pulled toward the stance ski until the tips cross
shaping.cue: Keep the lifted tip from drifting toward the stance ski

finish.action: Held until the ski is set down
finish.cue: Set it down parallel

initiation.action: Comes up from the transition's deep hip hinge as the legs lengthen, moving with the thighs; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open over the long legs, more tilted the harder the turn, never standing tall. Tilting it further forward than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half rises against the balance axis as the inside foot unloads, hiked by the outside hip abductors
initiation.cue: Inside hip up

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, with no support from the inside ski
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Held up under the late load, then lowers through the finish as the tail is set down
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Quiet in space while the femurs rotate under it
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Slight counter held
shaping.cue: Belt buckle a little toward the outside of the turn

finish.action: Square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load, never arched or slumped; a harder turn folds more at the hips, not the low back
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Tip the upper body over the outside ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out; more as speed and pitch build

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Straighten up as the turn ends

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-33° from vertical through the turn, a little more the harder the turn; it rises a little with the hips as the legs lengthen
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Quiet in space with the pelvis while the femurs rotate under
initiation.cue: Chest a little toward the outside of the turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the legs turn

finish.action: Square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward, ready
shaping.cue: Keep the outside hand ready

finish.action: Swings forward to ready the next pole touch
finish.cue: Swing the next pole forward

initiation.action: Swings the pole forward to touch just before the tail lifts
initiation.cue: Touch, then lift

shaping.action: Hand held forward, leading
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward, not dropped

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides, hands wide for balance
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the touching arm reaches forward from the shoulder to the snow
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip; the touching wrist flicks the pole tip forward
initiation.cue: Touch with the wrist, not the arm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes ahead down the hill
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level, or tipped slightly toward the outside with the shoulders
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head turns against the countered chest so the eyes stay on the path
initiation.cue: Look where you are going

shaping.action: Held against the counter
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Lengthens the knee into the turn, holds it against the whole turn force with no help from the inside leg, then lets it flex under the late load
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. Here one leg carries the whole load, about body weight when gentle and up to 1.3 times it when dynamic, peaking below the fall line, at a deeper bend as the turn gets harder; the per-setting values are our inference from that load and bend. At initiation the load is nearly the same at every setting, so gentle 1 against moderate 2 reflects the knee depth, not the load

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the stance leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the load, sharing the work with the hamstrings and adductor magnus
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared with the hamstrings and adductor magnus. Scaled like the vasti, with the load and the depth of the fold; the per-setting values are inference. At initiation gentle 1 against moderate 2, at almost the same load, reflects the depth of the fold

activations.role: Hikes the unsupported inside half of the pelvis from the stance hip as the edge builds, holds it, and lets it down as the tail comes down
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the one-leg pelvic hold follows from mechanics and single-leg exercise data. Highest from late shaping into the finish, where the angulation peaks and the pelvis is still held up under the peak load until the tail comes down

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to steer and edge, then brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the steering role is mechanics of the bent leg

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and shares the hip extension moment
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance; modelled hip extension share. Scaled with the load like adductor magnus

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the hip joint and brake the thigh's inward turn when the ski carves
activations.basis: The hip rotation moment is small and its sign depends on whether the ski carves or brushes; extrapolated from a model of a carved GS turn. Their action also shifts with hip flexion

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the feet back into the new turn; once the turn loads, only co-contracts, as the net ankle moment is plantarflexion
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where it is highly active; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the flexed ankle against the rising load to the fall line, sharing the plantarflexion moment with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus, not the gastrocnemius, does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the big-toe edge and build it into late shaping, make the constant small balance corrections on one edge, then let it go
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; balancing on one ski adds continuous co-contraction. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals for balance on one edge
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the stance hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The stance hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Holds the inside thigh up while the knee lifts the tail
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow, and only rectus femoris has been measured as an inside-leg hip flexor. Holding up the leg, boot and ski, about 16 kg, is a moderate hip-flexor effort; their effective weight grows with the load factor, about 6-21 % at the fall line, too little to move a level

activations.role: Works as a hip flexor on the inside leg, not as a knee extensor
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns; changes little with intensity

activations.role: Nearly idle while the leg is lifted; take the load again at set-down
activations.basis: Measured low on the inside leg in normal turns; lower still with no load

activations.role: Bends the knee to raise the tail, then holds the heel toward the seat; its short head is a pure knee bender
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics. Holding the lower leg and ski up is a light effort

activations.role: Help bend the knee and hold the tail up
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Bends the knee and keeps the lifted leg at hip width
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Flexes the hip, turns the thigh out and bends the knee together, which is the stork posture
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps hold the thigh up
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Keep the lifted thigh at hip width; pectineus also lifts it
activations.basis: Modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Turn the lifted thigh out so the ski stays parallel, and resist the tip drag that would cross the tips
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. With the hip deeply flexed their external rotation moment arm shrinks, and piriformis flips to an internal rotator, so gluteus maximus and sartorius share the work

activations.role: Helps turn the lifted thigh out so the ski stays parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the free thigh from falling inward
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns; its role here is mechanics

activations.role: Keeps the shin on the tongue and tips the lifted ski, and keeps the ankle closed as the tail comes down so the ski is ready to take the next turn; light, because the resting tip balances the ski
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns; low here by mechanics

activations.role: Tips the lifted ski onto its new edge and holds it there for the set-down
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it at the finish; the pelvic hike itself is the outside hip abductors' work
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The side bend grows with the edge angle, so its effort rises with intensity by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the counter against the legs' turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics, and a light one

activations.role: Steadies the trunk's side bend by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Balances the back extensors and the outside hip flexors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the skier stays off the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the low back carries a large combined load. Rises when dynamic, with the deeper fold and the higher load from the fall line on

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes steady while the chest counters
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Swings the pole for the touch and keeps the inside hand up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Brings the pole tip down for the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Works with latissimus dorsi in the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the elbow against the pole as it touches the snow
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles and flick the tip for the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier falls back and the outside ski catches its inner edge while the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries
Loaded if the lifted ski lands wide and catches, so the leg re-engages in a wedge, tip out, twisting the knee inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Our inference from the same wedge catch, which the sources describe without naming this ligament; the knee caving in opens its inner side
Pulled hard through long quadriceps holds at a deep knee bend, more so at higher intensity
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load

javelin-turn.name: Turn on the outside ski with the lifted inside ski crossed over it

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the feet are drawn back and the shin presses into the tongue while the body crosses over; flexed about as far as it goes in the turn
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and the feet back

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load to the fall line, then opens a little as the foot starts forward; pushing the hips back to make room for the crossed ski opens it too far, which is a fault
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue while the ski turns under you

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves toward the heel
finish.cue: Let the foot slide ahead as the turn ends

initiation.action: Flexed with the shin in the tongue through the edge change and as the ski lifts, so it comes up level rather than tip down
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the lifted ski about parallel to the snow; the ski's longer forebody pitches it tip down, and the shin and cuff hold it level with a little ankle effort
shaping.moment: Small dorsiflexion, against the forebody's weight
shaping.cue: Lifted ski level, tip just above the stance ski

finish.action: Stays closed, shin on the tongue, through the finish and as the ski is set down, ready to become the new outside ski
finish.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as you set the ski down

initiation.action: Begins to evert inside the boot, rolling the ski onto its big-toe edge with the other ski
initiation.cue: Roll onto the big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, below the fall line, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski, with constant small corrections on the one edge while the ski is steered
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep the edge building as the ski turns under you

finish.action: Holds, then releases toward flat through the finish into the transition
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends

initiation.action: Inverts so the inside ski tips onto its little-toe edge with the outside ski through the edge change, before it lifts
initiation.cue: Tip the inside ski the same way as the outside ski

shaping.action: Tilt held loosely; the lifted ski only needs to clear the stance ski
shaping.cue: Lifted ski quiet, just above the stance ski

finish.action: Tilt held as the ski is uncrossed and set down on its little-toe edge alongside the stance ski
finish.cue: Set it down parallel, at hip width, on its little-toe edge

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the load, all of it once the other ski lifts
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held under a light load, then quiet once the ski lifts
initiation.cue: A quiet foot

shaping.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

finish.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the new turn loads
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds and the leg turns its ski; about 58° gentle, 62° moderate, 66° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long and steady on the outside leg while it turns

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 66° gentle, 70° moderate, 75° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends

initiation.action: Shortens with the hip through the edge change, then flexes further to lift the whole ski once the new outside ski holds
initiation.cue: Change edges, then pick the inside ski up

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee, heel up, so the lifted ski rides level above the stance ski
shaping.cue: Heel up, ski level

finish.action: Held through the finish, then lengthens with the hip to set the ski down in the transition
finish.cue: Lower the ski, don't drop it

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

shaping.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Set the ski down straight

initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites, more so as the thigh turns in
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh in, but keep the knee over the foot

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

shaping.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Set the ski down without the knee caving in

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens into the new turn
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip over a strongly countered pelvis, about 46° gentle, 51° moderate, 56° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°); the counter lets the trunk fold forward rather than sideways
shaping.moment: Extension, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the transition, about 58° gentle, 64° moderate, 70° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to finish

initiation.action: Flexes more than the outside hip through the edge change, then lifts the thigh and the whole ski once the new edges hold
initiation.cue: Bring the inside thigh up after the edges change

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip, the hip flexors carrying the whole leg, boot and ski above the stance ski's forebody
shaping.moment: Flexion, about 0.6 Nm/kg with nothing resting on the snow (our estimate)
shaping.cue: Inside thigh up, lifted ski level

finish.action: Held through the finish, then lowered to set the ski down parallel in the transition
finish.cue: Lower the leg under control

initiation.action: The pelvis tips over the stance thigh as the legs tilt in; once the inside ski lifts, the outside abductors hold up the inside half alone, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up as the ski lifts

shaping.action: Hip angulation keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, the outside hip carrying the unsupported inside half of the pelvis; lifting the inside leg helps the hips move inside
shaping.moment: Abduction
shaping.cue: Hips in, over the outside hip

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases as the legs come upright and the lifted ski comes down
finish.cue: Level the hips as the ski comes down

initiation.action: Kept at hip width through the edge change and the lift
initiation.cue: Inside boot at hip width

shaping.action: Adducts a little so the lifted boot rides close beside the stance boot and the lifted tip passes over the stance ski's forebody; with the pelvis listed, the leg's own weight draws it in and the abductors control how far
shaping.moment: Small abduction
shaping.cue: Lifted tip over the stance ski, boots close

finish.action: Held crossed, then abducts back to hip width as the ski is uncrossed and set down
finish.cue: Uncross and set the ski down at hip width

initiation.action: Turns inward, the thigh rotating under a pelvis that keeps facing down the hill, to steer and tip the ski
initiation.cue: Turn the outside thigh under a still pelvis

shaping.action: Keeps turning inward, far more than in a normal turn, as the stance ski is steered under the lifted one; the brushed track shows the steering
shaping.moment: Internal, driving the steering against the snow
shaping.cue: Steer the outside ski under the lifted one

finish.action: Held at its most turned-in, then unwinds as the skis come together in the transition
finish.cue: Keep the separation through the finish

initiation.action: Turns outward a little with the skis through the edge change, as in a normal turn; the pelvis is already countered, so it is small
initiation.cue: Both skis turn together at first

shaping.action: Held near neutral to the pelvis, so the lifted ski points where the pelvis and chest face; the leg is not twisted across
shaping.cue: Lifted ski points where your belly button points

finish.action: Held near neutral to the pelvis until the ski is set down parallel to the stance ski
finish.cue: Keep the lifted ski with the upper body

initiation.action: Comes up from the transition's deep hip hinge as the legs lengthen, moving with the thighs; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open over the long stance leg, never standing tall. Pushing the hips back to make room for the crossed ski, so the low back arches and the weight goes to the tail, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half rises against the balance axis as the inside ski unloads and lifts, hiked by the outside hip abductors
initiation.cue: Inside hip up

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, with no support from the inside ski
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Held up under the late load, then lowers as the lifted ski is set down
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Stays facing down the hill while the skis turn under it, so the counter starts to build
initiation.cue: Belly button down the hill while the skis turn

shaping.action: Strong counter held, the pelvis facing well outside the stance ski, of the order of 30-50° by the end of shaping (our estimate), almost all of it from the stance femur turning in under it
shaping.moment: Held against the reaction of the stance leg's turning
shaping.cue: Pelvis and chest face where the lifted ski points

finish.action: Counter held through the finish; it unwinds as the skis release and turn under it into the next turn
finish.cue: Keep the separation through the finish

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load, never arched or slumped; the counter lets the trunk fold forward at the hips rather than bend at the low back
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Tip the upper body over the outside ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Straighten up as the turn ends

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.moment: Small, about a twelfth of the extension moment in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Even this much counter comes from the hips, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-33° from vertical through the turn; it rises a little with the hips as the legs lengthen
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Faces down the hill with the pelvis while the skis turn under; the shoulders counter slightly more than the pelvis
initiation.cue: Chest down the hill

shaping.action: Strong counter held with the pelvis against the stance leg's turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the outside leg turns

finish.action: Held with the pelvis; it unwinds as the skis release and turn under it
finish.cue: Keep the upper body facing down the hill

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view, facing down the hill with the chest
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward
shaping.cue: Both hands in front of the chest

finish.action: Arm held forward
finish.cue: Keep the outside hand forward

initiation.action: Arm held forward; the task pages ask for no pole touch
initiation.cue: Inside hand forward

shaping.action: Hand held up and forward, not dropped, which would pull the balance off the stance ski
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward, not dropped

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides, hands wide for balance
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75° and held
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip held
initiation.cue: Hold the poles lightly

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes ahead down the hill
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level, or tipped slightly toward the outside with the shoulders
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head faces down the hill with the chest
initiation.cue: Look down the hill

shaping.action: Head held with the countered chest; the eyes stay on the path
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Lengthens the knee into the turn, holds it against the whole turn force once the inside ski lifts, then lets it flex under the late load
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. Here one leg carries the whole load from the lift on, about 1.06-1.21 times body weight at the slow speeds of a brushed drill on easy terrain, so it stays at 2 at every setting; the per-setting values are our inference from that load and the knee bend. At initiation the load is still shared and nearly body weight at every setting; dynamic's 2 reflects a deeper bend

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the stance leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the load, sharing the work with the hamstrings and adductor magnus, and steadies the turned-in hip
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared with the hamstrings and adductor magnus. Scaled like the vasti, with the load and the depth of the fold; the per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Holds up the unsupported inside half of the pelvis once the ski lifts, and with its front fibres turns the bent stance thigh inward under the countered pelvis
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the one-leg pelvic hold follows from mechanics and single-leg exercise data. In the flexed hip the front fibres become internal rotators (cadaver moment arms), so here they also drive the steering. The per-setting values are inference, as in stork turns at similar loads

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius, turns the flexed thigh inward and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data and cadaver moment arms; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps turn the thigh inward and hold the pelvis
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: The main drivers of the stance thigh's large inward turn with the leg bent, then brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; with the leg bent the adductors are the strong rotators that turn and edge the ski (LeMaster). The drill asks for far more of this turning than a normal turn, at low loads; the per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee, shares the hip extension moment, and checks the trunk's forward pitch on one ski
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance; modelled hip extension share. A one-legged racer's biceps femoris was much more active in the first half of the turn on his harder side. Scaled with the load by inference

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in while the thigh turns in hard
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the head of the femur and control the thigh's inward turn as they lengthen
activations.basis: In a brushed, steered turn the net hip rotation moment is internal, so these external rotators only co-contract; extrapolated from a model of a carved GS turn and cadaver moment arms, which also shift with hip flexion

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the feet back into the new turn; once the turn loads, only co-contracts, as the net ankle moment is plantarflexion
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where it is highly active; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the flexed ankle against the rising load, sharing the plantarflexion moment with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus, not the gastrocnemius, does the ankle work. Lower loads than a carved turn here; scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the big-toe edge and build it into late shaping, make the constant small balance corrections on one edge, then let it go
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; balancing on one ski adds continuous co-contraction. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals for balance on one edge
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the stance hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The stance hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Lifts the inside thigh and the whole ski once the new edges hold, and holds them above the stance ski to the transition
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow, and only rectus femoris has been measured as an inside-leg hip flexor. Holding up the leg, boot and ski, about 16 kg, with nothing on the snow is about 0.6 Nm/kg of hip flexion moment (our estimate), a moderate effort; the load factor adds 6-21 % at the fall line, too little to move a level

activations.role: Works as a hip flexor on the inside leg, not as a knee extensor
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns; changes little with intensity

activations.role: Hold the lightly loaded inside knee through the edge change, idle while the leg is lifted, and take the load again at set-down
activations.basis: Measured low on the inside leg in normal turns; lower still with no load

activations.role: Bends the knee to lift the ski, then holds the heel up so the lifted ski stays level; its short head is a pure knee bender
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics. Holding the lower leg, boot and ski is a light effort once lifted

activations.role: Help bend the knee and hold the ski up
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Bends the knee and helps draw the lifted thigh in toward the stance leg
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps lift the thigh and bend the knee
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps hold the thigh up, and keeps it from turning out with the turn so the lifted ski stays with the pelvis
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow; the rotation role is moment arms in the flexed hip

activations.role: Co-contract with the abductors to place the lifted boot beside the stance boot, so the lifted tip rides over the stance ski; pectineus also helps lift the thigh
activations.basis: Modelled inside adductor longus in normal turns. Light here, because with the pelvis listed the hanging leg's own weight already draws it toward the stance leg, so the net moment is a small abduction

activations.role: Controls how far the lifted thigh falls in across the stance leg, then brings it back to hip width; its front fibres help keep the lifted ski with the pelvis
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns; its role here is mechanics

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh out with the skis through the edge change, then co-contract to hold the lifted ski in line with the pelvis
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the inside leg's shortening under its light load before the lift
activations.basis: The inside leg needs a hip extension moment while it carries load in a normal turn (modelled); here only until the lift

activations.role: Pulls the foot back and tips the inside ski onto its little-toe edge through the edge change, then keeps the shin on the tongue and the lifted ski level
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns. The forebody's pitch moment on the lifted ski is a few newton-metres, and the cuff carries part of it; low by mechanics

activations.role: Tips the inside ski onto its little-toe edge for the edge change and holds that tilt for the set-down
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the large counter against the stance leg's turning, paired with the inside external oblique, through the finish
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns. The drill holds far more counter than a normal turn, and longer, but the hip rotation moments it resists are small (about 0.2 Nm/kg modelled), so a moderate effort by inference

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; scaled as the outside internal oblique

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it at the finish; the pelvic hike itself is the outside hip abductors' work
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The edge angles at these slow speeds are moderate, so the side bend and its effort stay low

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics, and a light one

activations.role: Steadies the trunk by co-contraction against the counter pair
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing
