activations.role: Balances the back extensors and the outside hip flexors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the hips are not pushed back to make room for the crossed ski
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the low back carries a large combined load. The loads at these slow speeds change little between settings, so it stays at 2

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist, so the counter stays in the hips
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes steady while the chest counters
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the arms forward with the hands in view
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier falls back, often from pushing the hips back to make room for the crossed ski, and the stance ski catches its inner edge while the knee straightens and turns in; the slip-catch seen in racing injuries. The large inward turn of the stance thigh puts the knee nearer that position, so it must stay flexed and over the foot
Loaded if the crossed ski is set down still crossed or wide and catches, so the leg re-engages tip out in a wedge and the knee twists inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Our inference; the sources name valgus on the outside knee as what loads this ligament, and a hard inward turn of the stance thigh can let the knee cave in
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load; the large counter must come from the hips, not from twisting the low back

outside-ski-turn.name: Turn on the outside ski alone, inside ski held off the snow

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the foot is drawn back and the shin presses into the tongue while the body crosses over the one stance ski; flexed about as far as it goes in the turn
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and the foot back as you roll onto the new edge

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load to the fall line, then opens a little as the foot starts forward; a little more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves toward the heel. Fore-aft balance along the one ski is the task's point
finish.cue: Let the foot slide ahead as the turn ends, without sitting back

initiation.action: Flexed with the shin in the tongue as the leg is drawn up, so the lifted ski hangs level rather than tip down
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the stance one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the ski about parallel to the snow; the ski's longer forebody, ahead of the boot, pitches it tip down, and the shin and cuff hold it level with a little ankle effort
shaping.moment: Small dorsiflexion, against the forebody's weight
shaping.cue: Lifted ski level with the snow, tip not dragging

finish.action: Stays closed, shin on the tongue, as the ski is lowered at the end of the finish, so it lands centred and ready to take the weight
finish.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as you set the ski down

initiation.action: The stance foot alone changes the edge. It starts on the little-toe edge, where it took the weight in the transition; the inverters let it go, then the foot everts in the boot and rolls the ski through flat onto its big-toe edge
initiation.moment: Inversion while still on the little-toe edge, then eversion
initiation.cue: Roll the one ski from its little-toe edge onto its big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, below the fall line, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski, with constant small corrections on the one edge
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line; the edge angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Eases as the turn ends; the ski is still on its big-toe edge when the weight moves onto the other ski and this one is lifted
finish.cue: Ease the edge as the turn ends, then step off it

initiation.action: Inverts so the lifted ski tips onto its little-toe edge with the stance ski
initiation.cue: Tip the lifted ski the same way as the stance ski

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the stance ski's edge
shaping.cue: Keep the lifted ski tilted with the stance ski

finish.action: Tilt held as the ski is set down on its little-toe edge, where it takes the whole load for a moment before its own edge change
finish.moment: Inversion once loaded on the little-toe edge
finish.cue: Set it down parallel, at hip width, on its little-toe edge

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the whole load through its own edge change
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

shaping.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the sole as the foot takes the weight

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition, where it took the weight, as the new turn loads
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn on the one leg

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds; deeper the harder the turn, about 62° gentle, 67° moderate, 72° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long, strong and steady on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 70° gentle, 76° moderate, 80° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends

initiation.action: Flexes to draw the whole ski off the snow as the weight moves onto the new outside ski, before its edge change; knee flexion lifts the heel and keeps the ski level
initiation.cue: Pick the ski up before you change edges

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee, with no tip on the snow to help
shaping.cue: Heel up, ski level with the snow

finish.action: Held up through most of the finish, then lengthens with the hip to set the ski down at the end of it
finish.cue: Lower the ski, don't drop it

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

shaping.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Set the ski down straight

initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

shaping.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Set the ski down without the knee caving in

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens into the new turn
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip with the pelvis countered, about 50° gentle, 57° moderate, 64° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist; deeper with speed and pitch

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the transition, about 63° gentle, 71° moderate, 79° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to finish

initiation.action: Flexes to lift the thigh and the whole ski before the edge change; hip flexion does most of the shortening and brings the lifted foot a little ahead
initiation.cue: Bring the inside thigh up; the whole ski comes off the snow

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip, the hip flexors carrying the whole leg, boot and ski
shaping.moment: Flexion, about 0.6 Nm/kg with nothing resting on the snow (our estimate)
shaping.cue: Inside thigh held up, ski level

finish.action: Held through most of the finish, then lowered to set the ski down at hip width just before the edge change
finish.cue: Lower the leg under control

initiation.action: The pelvis tips over the stance thigh as the leg tilts in, so the inside half, unsupported since the transition, rises; the outside abductors hike it, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up from the moment the ski lifts

shaping.action: Hip angulation keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, the outside hip carrying the unsupported inside half of the pelvis
shaping.moment: Abduction
shaping.cue: Stay strong over the outside hip; the angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases as the legs come upright and the other ski is set down
finish.cue: Level the hips as the other ski comes down

initiation.action: Kept at hip width as the ski lifts, neither drawn in nor out; the net moment is near zero
initiation.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

shaping.action: Held at hip width beside the stance leg, the ski parallel to the stance ski
shaping.cue: Lifted ski parallel and at hip width

finish.action: Held, then the foot is set down at hip width
finish.cue: Set the foot down at hip width, not wide

initiation.action: Turns inward, the thigh rotating under the pelvis to steer and tip the one ski through its edge change
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh in the hip socket

shaping.action: Held turned in as the ski turns; the brushed track needs a little steering
shaping.moment: Small; internal (steering) in a brushed turn, external (braking) if carved, extrapolated from a modelled carved GS turn
shaping.cue: Keep the knee over the foot as the ski turns

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral as the turn ends
finish.cue: Let the thigh unwind as the turn ends

initiation.action: Turns outward with the turn so the lifted ski stays parallel to the stance ski
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted ski parallel

shaping.action: Held turned out, keeping the lifted tip from drifting toward the stance ski
shaping.cue: Lifted ski aligned with the stance ski

finish.action: Held until the ski is set down
finish.cue: Set it down parallel

initiation.action: Comes up from the transition's deep hip hinge as the stance leg lengthens, moving with the thigh; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the leg; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open over the long stance leg, more tilted the harder the turn, never standing tall. Tilting it further forward than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half has no support from the transition on; it rises against the balance axis as the stance leg tips in, hiked by the outside hip abductors
initiation.cue: Inside hip up before the edges change

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, with no support from the inside ski
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Held up under the late load, then lowers as the lifted ski is set down
finish.cue: Level the hips as the ski comes down

initiation.action: Quiet in space while the stance femur rotates under it
initiation.cue: Let the leg turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Slight counter held
shaping.cue: Belt buckle a little toward the outside of the turn

finish.action: Square to the ski as it eases off its edge; the new counter forms as the new stance leg turns under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the ski as the turn ends

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load, never arched or slumped; a harder turn folds more at the hips, not the low back
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski as the one ski changes edges; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it. Angulation, not banking, keeps the body over the one edge
initiation.cue: Tip the upper body over the stance ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out; more as speed and pitch build

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Straighten up as the turn ends

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-33° from vertical through the turn, a little more the harder the turn; it rises a little with the hips as the stance leg lengthens
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Quiet in space with the pelvis while the stance femur rotates under
initiation.cue: Chest a little toward the outside of the turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held against the leg's turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the leg turns

finish.action: Square to the ski as it eases off its edge; the new counter forms as the new stance leg turns under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the ski as the turn ends

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward, ready
shaping.cue: Keep the outside hand ready

finish.action: Swings forward to ready the next touch
finish.cue: Swing the next pole forward

initiation.action: Swings the pole forward for a light touch at the edge change, for timing; the task pages ask for no touch, so it is optional
initiation.cue: A light touch as the edges change

shaping.action: Hand held forward, leading
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward, not dropped

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides, hands wide for balance on the one edge
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the touching arm reaches forward from the shoulder
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip; the touching wrist flicks the pole tip forward
initiation.cue: Touch with the wrist, not the arm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes ahead down the hill
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level, or tipped slightly toward the outside with the shoulders
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head turns against the countered chest so the eyes stay on the path
initiation.cue: Look where you are going

shaping.action: Held against the counter
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Lengthens the knee into the turn, holds it against the whole turn force with no help from the inside leg, then lets it flex under the late load
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. Here one leg carries the whole load all turn, about body weight when gentle and up to 1.4 times it when dynamic, peaking below the fall line, at a deeper bend as the turn gets harder; the per-setting values are our inference from that load and bend. At initiation the load is nearly body weight at every setting, so gentle 1 against moderate 2 reflects the knee depth, not the load

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the stance leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the load, sharing the work with the hamstrings and adductor magnus
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared with the hamstrings and adductor magnus. Scaled like the vasti, with the load and the depth of the fold; the per-setting values are inference. At initiation gentle 1 against moderate 2, at almost the same load, reflects the depth of the fold

activations.role: Holds up the inside half of the pelvis, unsupported from the transition to the set-down, hikes it further as the edge builds, and lets it down as the other ski comes down
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the one-leg pelvic hold follows from mechanics and single-leg exercise data. Unlike stork turns the pelvis has no support from before the edge change, through a one-foot edge change on blue to gentle black terrain, so moderate and dynamic reach 3 from initiation; gentle stays 2, near body weight on easier pitch. All values per setting are inference

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to steer and edge the one ski through its edge change, then brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the steering role is mechanics of the bent leg

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee, shares the hip extension moment, and checks the trunk's forward pitch on one ski
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance; modelled hip extension share. A one-legged racer's biceps femoris was much more active in the first half of the turn on his harder side, so it matters on one ski. Scaled with the load like adductor magnus

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the hip joint and brake the thigh's inward turn
activations.basis: The hip rotation moment is small and its sign depends on whether the ski carves or brushes; extrapolated from a model of a carved GS turn. Their action also shifts with hip flexion

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the foot back into the new turn; once the turn loads, only co-contracts, as the net ankle moment is plantarflexion
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where it is highly active; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the flexed ankle against the rising load to the fall line, sharing the plantarflexion moment with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus, not the gastrocnemius, does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the one ski from its little-toe edge onto its big-toe edge, build the edge into late shaping, make the constant small balance corrections on one edge, then ease it
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; balancing on one ski adds continuous co-contraction, and here the whole edge change is made by this foot. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment

activations.role: Holds the ski on its little-toe edge as it takes the weight, lets it roll to flat for the edge change, then holds the arch and co-contracts with the peroneals for balance on the big-toe edge
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of a one-foot edge change; until the ski is flat the snow force acts on its outer edge, an inversion moment. Not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the stance hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The stance hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Lifts the inside thigh and the whole ski before the edge change and holds them up to the set-down
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow, and only rectus femoris has been measured as an inside-leg hip flexor. Holding up the leg, boot and ski, about 16 kg, with nothing on the snow is about 0.6 Nm/kg of hip flexion moment (our estimate), a moderate hip-flexor effort held through the whole turn; the load factor adds 6-22 % at the fall line, too little to move a level

activations.role: Works as a hip flexor on the inside leg, not as a knee extensor
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns; here it holds the whole ski up all turn. Changes little with intensity

activations.role: Idle while the leg is lifted; take the load again as the ski is set down to become the next stance ski
activations.basis: Measured low on the inside leg in normal turns; lower still with the leg off the snow

activations.role: Bends the knee to lift the ski, then holds the heel up so the ski stays level; its short head is a pure knee bender
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics. Holding the lower leg, boot and ski with the shank hanging close to the balance axis is a light effort, about a tenth of maximum by our estimate

activations.role: Help bend the knee and hold the ski up
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Bends the knee and keeps the lifted leg at hip width
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Flexes the hip, turns the thigh out and bends the knee together, which is the lifted-leg posture
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps hold the thigh up
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Keep the lifted thigh at hip width; pectineus also lifts it
activations.basis: Modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Turn the lifted thigh out so the ski stays parallel to the stance ski
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. With the hip deeply flexed their external rotation moment arm shrinks, and piriformis flips to an internal rotator, so gluteus maximus and sartorius share the work

activations.role: Helps turn the lifted thigh out so the ski stays parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the free thigh from falling inward
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns; its role here is mechanics

activations.role: Keeps the shin on the tongue and the lifted ski level against its forebody's weight, tips it onto its little-toe edge, and keeps the ankle closed as it is set down
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns. The forebody's pitch moment is a few newton-metres, a small share of the dorsiflexors' strength, and the cuff carries part of it; low by mechanics

activations.role: Tips the lifted ski onto its little-toe edge, holds it there, and holds that edge as the ski is set down and loaded
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. The loaded moment on the little-toe edge at set-down is brief, and the boot shell carries most of it

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it at the finish; the pelvic hike itself is the outside hip abductors' work
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The side bend grows with the edge angle, so its effort rises with intensity by inference; held through the finish because the inside ski stays up until its end

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the counter against the stance leg's turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics, and a light one

activations.role: Steadies the trunk's side bend by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Balances the back extensors and the outside hip flexors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the skier stays off the tail
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the low back carries a large combined load. Rises when dynamic, with the deeper fold and the higher load from the fall line on

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid, so lifting the ski does not shift the upper body
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. The task's teaching cues ask for a core that keeps the upper body still as a ski lifts

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes steady while the chest counters
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Swings the pole for the touch and keeps the inside hand up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Brings the pole tip down for the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Works with latissimus dorsi in the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles and flick the tip for the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier falls back and the one ski catches its inner edge while the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries; with no inside ski to catch the fall, a backward lean loads this knee alone
Loaded if the lifted ski is set down wide or tip out and catches, so the leg re-engages in a wedge and the knee twists inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Our inference from the same wedge catch, which the sources describe without naming this ligament; the knee caving in opens its inner side
Pulled hard through long quadriceps holds at a deep knee bend on one leg, more so at higher intensity
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load

thousand-steps-turn.name: Turn made of continuous small steps from ski to ski

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the feet are drawn back and the shin presses into the tongue while the body crosses over; re-closed each time the foot is placed, so every step lands centred
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and land each step on the middle of the foot

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load through every step, then opens a little as the foot starts forward
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion while loaded, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue through every step

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves toward the heel
finish.cue: Let the foot slide ahead as the turn ends, without stepping onto the tail

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes with the outside ankle, shin into the tongue, and stays closed as the foot is lifted and placed
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, every step

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, so the lifted ski stays level and lands centred
shaping.cue: Lift the ski level, not tip down

finish.action: Held flexed as the steps carry on into the transition, where this leg becomes the outside one
finish.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue into the next turn

initiation.action: Everts in the boot as the skis change edges, so each step of this foot lands on the big-toe edge; the stepping carries on through the edge change
initiation.cue: Step onto the big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping and holds the edge under each stance; each step is placed on the edge, never flat, so the track stays narrow
shaping.moment: Eversion while loaded
shaping.cue: Place every step on its edge; the edge angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Eases toward flat as the turn ends, while the steps continue into the edge change
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends, still stepping

initiation.action: Inverts so the inside ski lands on its little-toe edge with each step, leading the edge change
initiation.cue: Step onto the little-toe edge

shaping.action: Tilt held; for the moment the inside foot carries the whole load, the snow force on its little-toe edge needs an inversion moment, and the boot shell takes most of it
shaping.moment: Inversion while loaded
shaping.cue: Short, light steps on the inside ski

finish.action: Tilt held, then rolls toward flat as the edges change and this ski becomes the outside one
finish.cue: Let the little-toe edge go into the next turn

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the whole load at each step
initiation.cue: Land on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under each loaded step
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held under each brief loaded step on the little-toe edge
initiation.cue: Spread the pressure over the sole

shaping.action: Arch held under each brief loaded step
shaping.cue: Spread the pressure over the sole

finish.action: Arch held under each brief loaded step
finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the sole

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the new turn loads. Under that, each step is caught with a small yield and pushed off with a small extension, and the leg is lifted for a moment between its steps
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn, stepping all the time

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, under each stance; deeper the harder the turn, about 58° gentle, 62° moderate, 67° dynamic (our inference). Small yields and pushes ride on top as the weight moves foot to foot
shaping.moment: Extension while loaded
shaping.cue: Flex and extend each leg on its own to move the weight across

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 66° gentle, 70° moderate, 76° dynamic (our inference), still stepping
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends; keep stepping

initiation.action: More bent than the outside knee. Cycles with each step; the hamstrings lift the ski a little, then the knee extensors catch the brief load when it is placed, which is the heavier part
initiation.moment: Extension while loaded, a small flexion moment while lifted
initiation.cue: Short leg, light quick steps

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee while it keeps lifting and catching brief steps
shaping.cue: Step the inside ski as quickly as the outside one

finish.action: Keeps stepping; lengthens toward the outside knee's bend as the leg becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Let the inside leg lengthen into the next turn

initiation.cue: Step the ski with the thigh, not by twisting the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites at each landing
shaping.cue: Land each step with the knee and foot pointing the same way

finish.cue: Knee and foot point the same way

initiation.cue: Knee and foot point the same way

shaping.cue: Knee and foot point the same way

finish.cue: Knee and foot point the same way

initiation.cue: Land each step with the knee over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites at each landing
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot as it takes the step

finish.cue: Knee over the foot

initiation.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

shaping.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Place each step without the knee caving in

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens; between its steps the hip flexors lift the ski a little
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip, about 46° gentle, 51° moderate, 57° dynamic (our inference); the extensors hold it under each stance
shaping.moment: Extension while loaded
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the transition, about 58° gentle, 64° moderate, 71° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to finish

initiation.action: More flexed than the outside hip. The hip flexors lift the leg at each step; when the ski is placed, the hip extensors catch the brief load, the heavier part
initiation.moment: Extension while loaded, flexion while lifted
initiation.cue: Lift from the hip, ski level

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip while it keeps lifting and catching steps
shaping.cue: Keep the inside leg short and quick

finish.action: Keeps stepping; opens toward the outside hip's fold as the leg becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Let the inside leg lengthen into the next turn

initiation.action: The pelvis tips over the stance thigh as the legs tilt in; while the inside foot is up, the outside abductors hold the inside half of the pelvis, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up as you step

shaping.action: Angulation builds with the edge; under each stance the outside hip holds the pelvis level against the balance axis, catching a small drop as the step lands
shaping.moment: Abduction while loaded
shaping.cue: Move the weight with the legs, not by swaying the hips

finish.action: Holds, then releases as the legs come upright for the edge change
finish.cue: Level the hips as the turn ends

initiation.action: When the inside foot takes its step, the inside abductors hold the other half of the pelvis up for that moment; between steps the leg is kept at hip width
initiation.cue: Steps at hip width, narrow tracks

shaping.action: Repeated brief single-leg pelvic holds on the inside ski, the foot placed at hip width
shaping.cue: Steps at hip width, not wide

finish.action: Repeated brief pelvic holds, longer as this leg becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Steps at hip width

initiation.action: Turns inward a little, the thigh rotating under the pelvis to steer and tip the ski; after the first diverging step the skis stay nearly parallel
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh in the hip socket

shaping.action: Held turned in as the ski turns; each step lands pointing along the arc
shaping.moment: Small
shaping.cue: Land each step pointing along the arc

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the release
finish.cue: Let the thigh unwind with the release

initiation.action: Turns outward with the turn, so each step of the inside ski lands parallel to the outside ski, not diverging
initiation.cue: Step the skis parallel, not in a fan

shaping.action: Held turned out
shaping.moment: Internal rotation while loaded, as in a normal turn (modelled)
shaping.cue: Inside ski parallel to the outside ski

finish.action: Held, then unwinds as this leg becomes the outside leg
finish.cue: Keep the skis parallel

initiation.action: Comes up from the transition's deep hip hinge as the legs lengthen, moving with the thighs; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open, never standing tall, and steady while the legs step under it. Tilting it further forward than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half rises with the edge as the legs tilt in; on top of that it hikes and drops a little with each step, held by whichever hip is standing
initiation.cue: Inside hip up; small, quiet weight shifts

shaping.action: Held at the turn's list, a small hike and drop at each step
shaping.cue: The legs step; the pelvis stays nearly level to the balance axis

finish.action: Lowers toward level for the edge change, still shifting a little with each step
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Quiet in space while the femurs rotate under it
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

activations.role: Carry the outside leg's stances through the turn's flex pattern; each step adds a small eccentric catch and a small concentric push-off
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns. Each stance carries the whole load, about 1.0-1.2 times body weight at these speeds, but only for part of each cycle, so the mean stays at 2; dynamic's 2 at initiation reflects a deeper bend. Inference from the loads and the step pattern

activations.role: Works with the vasti under each stance, and as a hip flexor when the outside ski is lifted between steps
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg and a hip flexor on the inside leg in normal turns; here it does both in turn

activations.role: Holds the folded hip under each stance and helps catch each step
activations.basis: Hip extension moment modelled in carved turns; scaled like the vasti for part-time loading. Inference

activations.role: Holds the pelvis over the outside leg each time the inside foot lifts, catching a small drop at every step, and hikes the inside half as the edge builds
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; repeated single-leg pelvic holds match off-snow single-leg exercise data. A balance and support effort that changes little with these modest loads

activations.role: Shares the repeated pelvic holds with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to steer, then co-contract with the abductors so each step lands at hip width
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; lower here, with little steering in a large turn

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment under each stance
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps at each landing, and bends the knee to lift the outside ski between its steps
activations.basis: Hamstring co-contraction measured in normal turns and on landing; the lift is mechanics. Scaled with the load by inference

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in at each landing
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the hip joint and control the thigh's inward turn
activations.basis: Extrapolated from a model of a carved GS turn and cadaver moment arms

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the foot back into the new turn and re-centres it at each step; once the turn loads, co-contracts, as the net ankle moment under a stance is plantarflexion
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where it is highly active; active ankle flexion is a book technique point

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Shares the plantarflexion moment with the boot shaft under each stance, then opens the ankle through the finish
activations.basis: Modelled ankle moments in carving; with the knee bent the soleus does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Place each outside step on the big-toe edge, build the edge, and make the balance corrections of every single-leg stance
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; every step is a fresh landing on one edge. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals at each landing
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of single-leg balance; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of single-leg balance; not measured on snow

activations.role: Lifts the outside ski a little between its steps
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. Short, low lifts of a leg, boot and ski

activations.role: Lifts the inside leg at every step, the ski level; placing it again is a short eccentric lowering
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. Repeated lifts of the leg, boot and ski, about 16 kg, at about 0.6 Nm/kg of hip flexion moment while up (our estimate), with short rests while the foot stands

activations.role: Works as a hip flexor lifting the inside leg at each step
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the inside leg in normal turns

activations.role: Catch each brief step on the inside ski at its deeper knee bend, then push off it
activations.basis: Measured lower on the inside leg in normal turns; here it carries the whole load only for short steps. Rises in the finish as the leg becomes the outside one

activations.role: Bends the knee to lift the inside ski at each step and co-contracts at each landing
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics

activations.role: Help bend the knee to lift the ski
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Catches each brief step on the inside ski at its deeper hip fold, and helps turn the thigh out
activations.basis: The loaded inside leg needs hip extension moments like the outside one (modelled); brief here

activations.role: Holds the pelvis for the brief moments the inside foot stands alone
activations.basis: Measured on the inside leg in normal turns; repeated single-leg pelvic holds match off-snow data. Brief, so lower than the outside side; rises as this leg becomes the outside one

activations.role: Shares the brief pelvic holds with gluteus medius
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh out so each step lands parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep each inside step at hip width and hold the thigh against the internal-rotation moment of a loaded inside leg
activations.basis: Modelled inside adductor longus in normal turns

activations.role: Helps lift the thigh
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps lift the thigh and bend the knee
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Keeps the shin on the tongue and the lifted ski level, and tips the inside ski onto its little-toe edge
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns

activations.role: Holds the inside ski on its little-toe edge under each brief step
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of a load on the little-toe edge; the boot shell takes most of it

activations.role: Controls the trunk's slight bend toward the outside ski and keeps it from swaying with the steps
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side so the trunk stays quiet as the weight moves foot to foot
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the slight counter, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; a large turn needs little counter

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend
activations.basis: Mechanics; internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving

activations.role: Steadies the trunk by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk, quiet and steady over the stepping legs
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the loads here change little between settings

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk so the legs can step under a still torso
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. The task asks for a stable torso while the legs step

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes ahead while the body steps
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the arms forward with the hands in view
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles

structures.mechanism: Loaded if a step lands back on the tail with the knee straight and the ski catches its inner edge; the boot-induced and slip-catch mechanisms seen in racing injuries
Loaded if an inside step lands diverging, tip out, and catches, so the knee twists inward in a wedge; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Squeezed by forward flexion and side bend under the turn load; swaying the trunk with each step adds repeated side bending

extension-transition-turn.name: Carved turns linked by an extension transition, the body rising over the skis

initiation.action: Closes as the feet are drawn back while the body rises and moves forward over the skis, so the extension goes up and forward, not up and back
initiation.cue: Rise forward over the feet, shins on the tongues

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load, a little more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens a little as the foot slides forward under the body and pressure moves toward the heel, still flexed past upright
finish.cue: Let the feet come forward a little as the turn ends

initiation.action: Stays closed while the old outside leg pushes, then the foot is drawn back as it becomes the inside foot
initiation.cue: Both shins forward as you rise

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue; the inside dorsiflexors work harder after the fall line
shaping.cue: Keep the inside shin on the tongue

finish.action: Held closed while the outside foot comes forward, ready to push as the new turn starts
finish.cue: Inside ankle stays bent

initiation.action: Everts inside the boot as the skis go light at the top of the rise, rolling the ski onto its big-toe edge above the fall line
initiation.cue: Roll onto the new big-toe edge as you rise

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line

finish.action: Holds, then releases toward flat as the turn ends
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends

initiation.action: Inverts to roll the new inside ski onto its little-toe edge as it unweights after the push
initiation.cue: Tip the inside foot toward its little toe

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the outside ski's edge
shaping.cue: Keep both skis tipped the same way

finish.action: Releases toward flat with the outside ski
finish.cue: Flatten both skis together

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the new load after the light switch
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under the peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

shaping.action: Arch held under a lighter load

finish.action: Arch held under a lighter load

initiation.action: Extends through the switch, lifting the body up and across onto the new edges; the skis go light at the top of the rise, then the leg meets the new turn long

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load peaks; less bent than with a flexion transition

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, ready for the next push

finish.action: Held, then eases toward neutral as the edges flatten

activations.role: Extend the knee through the switch to lift the body over the skis, hold it at the peak and let it flex as the turn ends
activations.basis: Vastus medialis and lateralis averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns (hintermeister-1997), the same carved pattern. Outside vastus lateralis ran lower with an extension transition than with a flexion one (seifert-2023, in mV), because the knee works less bent; the push at the switch is a short concentric burst (L&S Fig 5.4b). Per-setting values are our inference from the load and the push

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor in the push and the hold
activations.basis: Outside rectus femoris was much lower in the transition with an extension transition than with a flexion one (seifert-2023, in mV). Levels are our inference

activations.role: Extends the hip in the push through the switch, then holds the folded hip against the load
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns (hintermeister-1997); the knee and hip extensors drive the extension through the switch (biomechanics.md D17). Per-setting values are inference from the load and the push

activations.role: Keeps the inside half of the pelvis up as the legs tip and the hip angulates
activations.basis: Measured on both legs on snow with both transition styles (seifert-2023); the inside ski shares the pelvic hold. Rises with the angulation at speed by inference

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Never measured on snow; off-snow EMG puts it with gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to tip and steer the light skis, then stiffen the hip against the abductors
activations.basis: The adductors averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns as a group; the carved turn needs little steering, so they sit lower here by inference

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured apart from the adductor group

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and brakes the thigh's inward turn as the ski carves

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the body rises up and back instead of forward, so the new turn starts back-seated with the boot pushing the shin forward against a hard quadriceps pull; a late edge set from there adds the slip-catch
Squeezed by flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load; arching the low back to stand up at the switch adds extension under load

flexion-transition-turn.name: Carved turns linked by a flexion transition, the legs retracted under a low body

initiation.action: Held closed through the low switch, shin pressed into the tongue, so the deep knee and hip bend does not tip the body back; then the feet are drawn further back as the new edges engage

initiation.action: Closes as the foot is pulled up and back under the body during the retraction; the shin stays on the tongue

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue; the inside dorsiflexors work harder after the fall line

finish.action: Held closed while the outside foot comes forward, ready to become the new outside foot low and flexed

initiation.action: Everts inside the boot as the legs cross under, rolling the ski onto its big-toe edge early, above the fall line
initiation.cue: Roll onto the new big-toe edge while you are still low

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski

shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line

finish.action: Holds, then releases toward flat as the legs begin to retract

initiation.action: Inverts to roll the retracting inside ski onto its little-toe edge, leading the outside ski
initiation.cue: Tip the folded foot toward its little toe

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the outside ski's edge

finish.action: Releases toward flat with the outside ski

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the new load after the light switch

shaping.action: Arch held up under the peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held as the folded foot takes little load

shaping.action: Arch held under a lighter load
shaping.cue: A quiet inside foot

finish.action: Arch held under a lighter load

initiation.action: Starts from its deepest bend in the switch, near 90°, and lengthens only gradually, out to the side rather than up, as the new turn loads; the body stays low

initiation.cue: Stay low and let the leg reach out to the side

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load peaks; deeper than in an extension transition, which costs the vasti more
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Strong and steady on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, on into the deep bend of the next switch

initiation.action: The old outside leg is pulled up through the switch, knee folding actively so the skis cross under the body; the skis go light at once

initiation.cue: Pull the old outside foot up and under you

shaping.action: Held short and more bent than the outside knee as it takes its share of the load again
shaping.moment: Extension, about as large as the outside knee's, because it is more bent
shaping.cue: Short inside leg, long outside leg

finish.action: Held bent while the outside knee folds to match it, so both are low and level at the switch

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

initiation.cue: Folded knee points where its ski points

shaping.cue: Inside knee points where its ski points

finish.cue: Inside knee points where its ski points

shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot and does not cave in

shaping.moment: Small abduction moment
shaping.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Opens slowly from its deep fold in the switch, near 90°, as the leg reaches out to the side; the hips stay low

initiation.cue: Stay folded at the hips as the leg reaches out

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip with the pelvis slightly countered
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the deep fold of the next switch
finish.cue: Keep folding at the hips as the turn ends

initiation.action: The old outside thigh is pulled up toward the chest through the switch, iliopsoas and rectus femoris lifting it, so the leg shortens without the body rising

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip as it takes its share of the load

finish.action: Held flexed while the outside hip folds to match it

shaping.action: Hip angulation builds with the edge to its most in late shaping, then holds

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases as the legs fold and come back under the body
finish.cue: Let the hips come back over the skis as you fold

initiation.action: The folded inside knee tips toward the new turn with its ski, leading the edge change
initiation.cue: Inside knee leads the tipping

shaping.action: Held, the inside thigh drawn toward the turn at hip width
shaping.moment: Adduction, the adductor longus the main contributor in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Feet hip width apart

finish.action: Held, then eases toward neutral as the edges flatten
finish.cue: Keep the feet hip width apart

initiation.action: Turns inward a little as the light skis are tipped and pointed into the new turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Held turned in as the ski carves
shaping.moment: External in a modelled carved turn, the external rotators braking the inward turn
shaping.cue: Keep the knee over the foot as the ski turns

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the release

initiation.action: Turns outward as the folded leg steers the inside ski into the new turn
initiation.cue: Steer the folded inside ski too

shaping.action: Held turned out, about 10-26° in a modelled carved turn
shaping.moment: Internal, so the internal rotators hold the femur against further outward turn
shaping.cue: Inside ski parallel

finish.action: Held until the release
finish.cue: Inside ski parallel

initiation.action: Deeply hinged at the hips through the low switch, the trunk forward about 40-50°, and comes up only a little as the legs reach out; the low back stays slightly flattened, never rounded to make the fold
initiation.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist; chest over the knees

shaping.action: Hinge held over the long outside leg, more tilted the harder the turn
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs fold toward the switch

initiation.action: The inside half stays up as the legs tip under the low body, held by the outside hip abductors

finish.action: Levels as the edges release

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load
shaping.moment: Extension, the largest moment in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing as the fold deepens
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski as the legs tip under; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out; more as speed builds

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the edges release
finish.cue: Straighten up over the skis as you fold

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

initiation.action: Chest low and well forward through the switch, but the upper back not rounded; it rises a little as the legs reach out

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Chest lowers with the fold toward the switch
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Returns toward straight through the finish

initiation.action: Quiet in space with the pelvis while the femurs turn under
initiation.cue: Chest a little toward the outside of the turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the legs turn

finish.action: Squares to the skis as they release

initiation.action: Shoulder blades forward and level with the hands reaching ahead through the low switch

shaping.action: Hand held forward, leading

finish.action: Hand held forward

shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

Outside vastus lateralis ran higher with a flexion transition than with an extension one, in steering and transition alike, with more desaturation and higher perceived exertion (seifert-2023, in mV). The per-setting values are our inference from the load and the deeper bend

activations.role: Holds the deep knee bend through the switch and helps lengthen it, its activity there much higher than in an extension transition
activations.basis: Outside rectus femoris was much higher in the transition with a flexion transition (seifert-2023, in mV, so ranked, not scaled). Levels are our inference

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and brakes the thigh's inward turn as the ski carves

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the new big-toe edge while the body is still low, build it into late shaping, then let it go

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals

activations.role: Helps fold the knee while the leg is light

activations.role: Hold the inside thigh drawn toward the turn and, with the hip flexed, hold it against further outward turn

activations.role: Flexes the hip, turns the thigh out and bends the knee together, the shape of the retraction

activations.role: Helps the folded knee tip toward the new turn and steadies the inside hip

activations.role: Pulls the retracting foot up and back, tips the inside ski first, and keeps the shin on the tongue, rising after the fall line
activations.basis: The second most active inside-leg muscle in an EMG-validated model of a carved turn, rising after the fall line; scaled by inference

activations.role: Pull the inside foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Rolls the inside ski onto its little-toe edge and lets it go
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Shares the inside ankle's plantarflexion moment with the boot once the leg is loaded again
activations.basis: The modelled inside ankle moment was about 45 % lower than the outside one

activations.role: Spread the lighter load over the inside sole
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the deeply folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened, so the retraction comes from the hips and knees, not a rounded back
activations.basis: Measured in turns; the lumbar extension moment was the largest joint moment in a modelled carved turn. The trunk is folded further through the switch than in an extension transition, so the hold is longer; levels are inference

activations.role: Balances the back extensors and helps the hip flexors pull the legs up, without rounding the back
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in turns; LeMaster names the abdominals with iliopsoas as active flexors

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The side bend grows with the edge angle, so its effort rises with speed by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the slight counter against the legs' turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Internal oblique was a primary trunk muscle in a model of carving; external oblique measured higher in GS than in slalom

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured in turns, higher in GS than in slalom

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski
activations.basis: Mechanics of the side bend

activations.role: Steadies the trunk by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Keep the head up and the eyes ahead while the chest drops low
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Swings the pole for the touch and keeps the inside hand up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level

activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles and flick the tip for the touch
