structures.mechanism: Loaded if the deep fold drops the hips behind the feet, so the skier lands the new turn back-seated with the boot pushing the shin forward against a hard quadriceps pull; the backward-fall mechanism
Pulled hard by the quadriceps holding the knee near 90° through the switch, deeper than in an extension transition
Squeezed by the deep forward fold at the switch and by flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load; worse if the fold is made by rounding the back

short-radius-turn.name: Short-radius turns, legs turning under a pelvis that faces down the hill

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the feet are drawn back under the body after the release, so the shin meets the tongue and the new tips bite
initiation.cue: Pull the feet back as the edges change

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load, shin on the tongue, a little more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue

finish.action: Opens a little as the foot slides forward and pressure moves toward the heel at the edge set, still flexed past upright
finish.cue: Let the feet come forward a little as you set the edges

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes with the outside ankle as the feet are drawn back; the inside shin meets its tongue too
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue; the inside dorsiflexors work harder after the fall line
shaping.cue: Keep the inside shin on the tongue

finish.action: Held closed while the outside foot comes forward, so the inside foot is ready to become the new outside foot
finish.cue: Inside ankle stays bent

initiation.action: Everts quickly inside the boot right after the release, rolling the ski onto its big-toe edge early, above the fall line
initiation.cue: Roll quickly onto the new big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line

finish.action: Sets the edge briefly, then lets it go early toward flat, ready for the next release
finish.cue: Set, then let the edge go

initiation.action: Inverts to roll the inside ski onto its little-toe edge, leading the outside ski
initiation.cue: Tip the inside foot first, toward its little toe

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the outside ski's edge
shaping.cue: Keep both skis tipped the same way

finish.action: Releases toward flat with the outside ski
finish.cue: Flatten both skis together

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the new load
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under the peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held through the edge set as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held under a lighter load
initiation.cue: A quiet inside foot

shaping.action: Arch held under a lighter load
shaping.cue: A quiet inside foot

finish.action: Arch held as the inside foot takes more load at the edge set
finish.cue: A quiet inside foot

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the new turn loads; quicker and shorter than in long turns
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, through a short window as the load builds past the fall line; never straight
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Strong and steady over the fall line

finish.action: Flexes quickly under the edge set, absorbing the peak load, into its deepest bend in the transition, then the rebound starts the next turn
finish.cue: Flex to set the edges, then let the rebound carry you

initiation.action: Shortens under its own load as the skis tip, so the inside leg is more bent than the outside one
initiation.moment: Extension, about as large as the outside knee's, because it is more bent
initiation.cue: Let the inside leg fold so the skis can tip

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee
shaping.cue: Short inside leg, long outside leg

finish.action: Held bent under the extra load the inside foot takes at the edge set, while the outside knee flexes to match it, so both are level at the edge change
finish.cue: Both knees bent together at the edge set

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

finish.moment: Resisting the twist of the edge set
finish.cue: Turn the thigh not the knee

initiation.cue: Inside knee points where its ski points

shaping.cue: Inside knee points where its ski points

finish.cue: Inside knee points where its ski points

initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot and does not cave in

finish.moment: Resisting valgus at the edge set
finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot through the edge set

initiation.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

shaping.moment: Small abduction moment
shaping.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens into the new turn
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip with the pelvis facing down the hill
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further with the knee under the edge set, into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to set the edges

initiation.action: Flexes under its own load with the knee as the inside leg shortens; its femur ends more flexed than the outside one, which brings the inside foot slightly ahead
initiation.cue: Inside hip folds a little more

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip
shaping.moment: Extension, similar to the outside hip because it is more flexed
shaping.cue: Inside leg short, inside foot slightly ahead

finish.action: Held flexed while the outside hip folds to match it at the edge set
finish.cue: Both hips folded at the edge set

initiation.action: The knee moves toward the turn as the leg tips the ski, then the pelvis tips over the loaded thigh so the inside half stays up; the outside abductors hold it, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up as you tip in

shaping.action: Hip angulation builds quickly to its most in late shaping, then holds; smaller than in long turns, coming mostly from the legs winding under the pelvis
shaping.moment: Changes sign within the turn; abductors and adductors co-contract
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders over the outside ski

finish.action: Holds through the edge set, then releases early as the legs come back under the body
finish.cue: Let the hips come back over the skis to release

initiation.action: The inside knee tips toward the turn with its ski, leading the edge change
initiation.cue: Inside knee leads the tipping

shaping.action: Held, the inside thigh drawn toward the turn at hip width
shaping.moment: Adduction, the adductor longus the main contributor in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Inside knee stays out of the way of the outside knee

finish.action: Held, then eases back toward neutral as the edges flatten
finish.cue: Keep the feet hip width apart

initiation.action: Turns inward from the outward rotation it held as the old inside leg, through neutral, as the released skis swing toward the fall line under a pelvis already facing it; the stretched rotators recoil and the internal rotators drive
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet upper body

shaping.action: Keeps turning inward as the skis come across the fall line under the still pelvis
shaping.moment: Internal when the skis are brushed; when they carve, sidecut turns them and the external rotators brake instead
shaping.cue: Keep turning the thigh in the hip socket

finish.action: At its most turned in, about 30-40° of counter, held through the edge set; this stretch winds up the next turn
finish.cue: Skis across, belly button down the hill

initiation.action: Turns outward from the inward rotation it held as the old outside leg, through neutral, so the inside ski turns with the outside one
initiation.cue: Turn both legs together

shaping.action: Keeps turning outward as the skis come across the fall line
shaping.moment: Internal in a modelled carved turn, so the external rotators drive only when the skis are brushed
shaping.cue: Steer the inside ski too

finish.action: Held turned out through the edge set
finish.cue: Inside ski parallel at the edge set

initiation.action: Comes up a little from the transition's hip hinge as the legs lengthen; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held over the legs, less forward than in long turns
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the edge set
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half stays up as the legs tip, held by the outside hip abductors with some support from the inside ski
initiation.cue: Inside hip up

shaping.action: Kept up, a little more as the edge builds to late shaping
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop

finish.action: Levels as the edges release
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Faces down the fall line in space while the skis turn under it, so its counter to the skis unwinds from the last turn's 30-40° through square
initiation.cue: Belly button down the hill

shaping.action: Still facing down the hill; counter to the skis grows to about 25° as they turn across
shaping.moment: Resisting the reaction torque of the turning legs
shaping.cue: Upper body quiet, legs turning

finish.action: Counter at its most, about 30-40°, held against the edge set's twist
finish.cue: Stay facing down the hill as you set the edges

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing through the edge set
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Bend builds a little to late shaping, then holds; less than in long turns
shaping.cue: Upper body over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the edges release
finish.cue: Straighten up over the skis

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets not the low back

initiation.action: Chest slightly forward and held
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Chest slightly forward and held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Chest slightly forward and held through the edge set
finish.cue: Don't sit up as you set the edges

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

shaping.action: Bend held to late shaping
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the edges release
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Chest faces down the fall line with the pelvis while the legs swing under
initiation.cue: Chest down the hill

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill against the legs' turning, a little more countered than the pelvis
shaping.cue: Chest down the hill

finish.action: Held facing down the hill against the edge set's twist, blocked by the pole plant
finish.cue: Plant and stay facing down the hill

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Begins to swing forward, ready for the next plant
shaping.cue: Swing the next pole early

finish.action: Swings forward and down the hill to plant at the edge change
finish.cue: Reach the pole down the hill

initiation.action: Plants the pole down the hill at the release, tip ahead of the hand, then the arm braces as the body moves past it; the plant blocks the upper body from turning with the legs
initiation.cue: Plant and move past it

shaping.action: Hand comes forward again once the pole leaves the snow
shaping.cue: Hand back in view after the plant

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides with the hands wide
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the planting arm braces against the pole
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held while the next pole swings
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip; the planting wrist flicks the tip down the hill
initiation.cue: Plant with the wrist and forearm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip; the swinging wrist brings the next tip forward
finish.cue: Tip forward with the wrist

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes down the corridor
initiation.cue: Eyes down the hill

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady through the edge set
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level or tipped slightly toward the outside with the shoulders
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.cue: Head faces down the hill with the chest

shaping.cue: Head faces down the hill with the chest

finish.cue: Head faces down the hill with the chest

activations.role: Lengthens the knee into the turn, holds it through the short peak and brakes it through the edge set
activations.basis: Vastus medialis and lateralis averaged above 50 % MVC, with peaks above 150 %, in short-radius parallel turns; the electrodes were on one leg through both turns, so the outside-leg share is higher still. That is the dynamic setting; gentle and moderate are scaled down by our inference from the load (about 0.7-1.1 W on this leg at the finish). The finish carries the edge set's brief spike

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the loaded leg
activations.basis: Rectus femoris averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius turns, recorded on one leg through both turns; in instructors' slalom it peaked at the start of the cycle in the inside position (panizzolo-2013), so its outside-leg share is set below the vasti

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the load and brakes the fold through the edge set; brakes the thigh's inward turn when the skis carve
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius parallel turns (one leg through both turns). Lower settings scaled down by inference from the load

activations.role: Keeps the inside half of the pelvis up as the legs tip, and with its front fibres turns the bent thigh inward to steer
activations.basis: Measured on both legs on snow in normal turns. The inside ski shares some of the pelvic hold, so it stays below stork-turn levels; the steering role at a flexed hip is moment-arm anatomy

activations.role: Turns the bent thigh inward with gluteus medius's front fibres and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Never measured on snow; its internal-rotation moment arm grows with hip flexion (delp-1999) and off-snow EMG puts it with gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps turn the thigh inward and hold the pelvis
activations.basis: Inferred from moment arms and exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to steer and edge, the strongest rotators of a flexed leg, and stiffen the hip against the abductors
activations.basis: The adductors averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius turns, recorded as a group on one leg through both turns; that they drive the steering is mechanics of the bent leg. Lower settings by inference

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured apart from the adductor group

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and protect the ACL, more than in any other turn type, and shares the hip extension moment
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius parallel turns (one leg through both turns); short turns had the lowest quadriceps-to-hamstrings ratio of the recreational tasks. Lower settings by inference

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in, most at the edge set
activations.basis: Medial hamstrings averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius turns (one leg through both turns); semitendinosus 6-15 % MVC in a simulated edged stance. Set a step below biceps femoris

activations.role: Steady the hip joint and brake the thigh's inward turn when the skis carve
activations.basis: The hip rotation moment's sign depends on whether the skis carve or are brushed; extrapolated from a model of a carved GS turn. With the hip flexed their external-rotation moment arms shrink

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the feet back at every edge change, many times a minute, then co-contracts to keep the shin on the tongue
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in short-radius parallel turns (one leg through both turns). The quick rhythm repeats the pull every second or so; the shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction. Lower settings by inference

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the ankle against the rising load with the boot shaft, then opens it as the foot comes forward at the edge set
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus, not the gastrocnemius, does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the foot quickly onto the new big-toe edge, build it into late shaping, then let it go
activations.basis: Peroneus longus is highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment. The quick edge changes repeat this every turn

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the loaded hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; never measured on snow. The loaded hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Let the inside knee fold under its own load, hold it bent, and take the extra load the inside foot carries at the edge set
activations.basis: Inside vastus lateralis ran about 54 % below the outside leg in recreational turns, so it sits a step lower; inside load rises at the end of a short turn (bon-2021). Slalom is more symmetric between legs than other events (cross-raschner-2023 p 12)

activations.role: Switches between knee extensor and hip flexor on the inside leg, helping it stay short
activations.basis: Measured on the inside leg in normal turns, where it matched the outside leg while the inside vasti dropped

activations.role: Holds the more-flexed inside hip against its load and helps turn the thigh outward
activations.basis: The inside hip carries an extension moment similar to the outside one in a modelled turn, at a deeper fold; scaled with the inside load by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts to steady the bent inside knee
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in turns

activations.role: Co-contract to steady the bent inside knee
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in turns

activations.role: Hold the inside thigh drawn toward the turn at hip width
activations.basis: Adductor longus ranked among the most active inside-leg muscles in an EMG-validated model of a carved turn

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh outward so the inside ski steers with the outside one
activations.basis: Anatomy; never measured on snow. With the hip deeply flexed their moment arms shrink, so gluteus maximus and sartorius share the work

activations.role: Helps flex and turn the inside thigh outward
activations.basis: Anatomy and hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps the inside knee tip toward the turn and steadies the inside hip
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius was active on snow through steering and the transition

activations.role: Pulls the inside foot back, tips the inside ski first, and keeps the shin on the tongue, rising after the fall line
activations.basis: The second most active inside-leg muscle in an EMG-validated model of a carved turn, rising after the fall line; scaled by inference

activations.role: Pull the inside foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Rolls the inside ski onto its little-toe edge and lets it go
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Shares the inside ankle's plantarflexion moment with the boot
activations.basis: The modelled inside ankle moment was about 45 % lower than the outside one

activations.role: Spread the lighter load over the inside sole
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the pelvis and chest facing down the hill against the legs' turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Internal oblique was a primary trunk muscle in a model of carving; external oblique was measured in turns, lower in slalom than in GS. The counter is larger here than in long turns, so the hold works every turn

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured in turns, lower in slalom than in GS (hintermeister-1995); the pairing is anatomy

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Mechanics of the side bend; a light role at slalom's small bend

activations.role: Steadies the trunk by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics, light at slalom's small bend

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in turns

activations.role: Hold the hinged trunk with the low back slightly flattened, quiet but not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in slalom and in turns; the trunk is less folded than in long turns, so a step below the long-turn hold

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against the twist the legs send up
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes down the corridor while the legs swing under
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Brings the planting hand forward and keeps the inside hand up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Drives the pole tip into the snow and braces the arm against the blocking plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; a forceful plant adds latissimus and triceps. Not measured on snow

activations.role: Works with latissimus dorsi in the plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the elbow against the blocking plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints through the swing and plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles and flick the tips forward for the swing and plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier is behind the feet at the edge set and the outside ski catches its inner edge while the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries; a hard set from the back seat adds the boot's push on the shin
Pulled hard by the quadriceps braking the edge set at a deep knee bend, many times a run
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under load; the legs' turning torque passes up through a trunk held facing down the hill

long-radius-carved-turn.name: Long-radius carved turn, arc to arc on both skis

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the feet are drawn back and the shins move into the tongues while the body crosses over the skis, so the new turn starts on the shovels
initiation.cue: Pull the feet back and the toes up as the edges change

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load and the boot's flex to the fall line, then opens a little as the foot starts forward; more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, up to about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves from the ball of the foot toward the heel
finish.cue: Let the feet run ahead a little as the turn ends

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes with the outside ankle, the inside foot drawn back so it does not run far ahead as the inside leg shortens
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the shin on the tongue; the inside foot leads a little because its hip and knee are more flexed and the boot fixes the ankle
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, smaller than outside, up to about 0.47 Nm/kg in the muscles in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Inside shin on the tongue too

finish.action: Still held closed, the shin pressing the tongue more after the fall line, ready to become the new outside ankle
finish.cue: Keep the inside shin forward through the end of the turn

initiation.action: Rolls from flat onto the big-toe edge inside the boot as soon as the edges change, so the ski grips and bends above the fall line
initiation.cue: Roll onto the big-toe edge early, not hard

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building with the edge angle to its most in late shaping, below the fall line, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion; most of it carried by the boot shell
shaping.cue: Keep tipping as the turn builds; the edge grows with speed and pitch

finish.action: Holds, then lets the edge go progressively toward flat through the finish into the transition
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends

initiation.action: Inverts onto the little-toe edge, leading the edge change with the outside foot
initiation.cue: Tip the inside foot onto its little-toe edge first

shaping.action: Tilt built and held with the outside ski, both skis at similar high edge angles
shaping.cue: Keep both skis tipping together

finish.action: Rolls back toward flat with the outside ski at the release
finish.cue: Release both edges together

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes most of the load
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under peak load, pressure spread along the inside of the foot
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held under a light load on the outer border of the foot
initiation.cue: Feel the whole little-toe side of the foot

shaping.action: Arch held under a light load
shaping.cue: Feel the whole little-toe side of the foot

finish.action: Arch held as the foot loads up to become the outside foot
finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the whole foot

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the new turn loads
initiation.cue: Grow into the new turn

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds; deeper the harder the turn, about 55° gentle, 60° moderate, 65° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension, up to about 1.02 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Long, strong and steady on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 65° gentle, 72° moderate, 80° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends

initiation.action: Flexes as the skis tip, shortening the inside leg under its own share of the load so both skis can tilt together; the flexion transition starts this leg already short
initiation.cue: Shorten the inside leg as the skis tip

shaping.action: Held well more bent than the outside knee, the difference growing with the edge angle, about 70° gentle, 85° moderate, 100° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 81-114°)
shaping.moment: Extension, up to about 0.96 Nm/kg, nearly as much as the outside knee because it is more bent
shaping.cue: Short inside leg, long outside leg

finish.action: Lengthens toward the outside knee's bend as the edges come down, ready to become the new outside leg
finish.cue: Let the inside leg grow as the edges flatten

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Small and changing sign, up to about 0.22 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

shaping.moment: Mostly internal rotation, up to about 0.28 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites, up to about 0.23 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

shaping.moment: Abduction, up to about 0.31 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Opens from its deepest fold in the transition as the leg lengthens into the new turn
initiation.cue: Rise a little into the turn

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip with the pelvis slightly countered, about 45° gentle, 52° moderate, 60° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Extension, up to about 1.27 Nm/kg in the modelled turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist; deeper with speed and pitch

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the transition, about 58° gentle, 68° moderate, 78° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex to finish

initiation.action: Flexes more than the outside hip as the inside leg shortens, partly yielding under its load and partly drawn up by the hip flexors; this sets the inside foot's lead
initiation.cue: Draw the inside thigh up a little as the skis tip

shaping.action: Held well more flexed than the outside hip, about 65° gentle, 80° moderate, 95° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 70-117°)
shaping.moment: Extension, up to about 1.05 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Inside thigh up, inside half of the body strong and a little forward

finish.action: Opens toward the outside hip's angle as the edges come down and the leg lengthens
finish.cue: Let the inside leg lengthen with the release

initiation.action: The outside knee moves toward the turn (adduction of the flexed thigh), then the pelvis tips over the stance thigh as the legs tilt and the inside half rises, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up as the legs tip

shaping.action: Hip angulation keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held; the adductors yield as the angle builds while the abductors co-contract and hold the pelvis
shaping.moment: Mostly adduction, up to about 0.52 Nm/kg, in one model; abduction from gluteus maximus in the other, so the sign changes within the turn and between skiers
shaping.cue: Stay strong over the outside hip; the angle builds with speed and pitch

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases toward neutral as the legs come back under the body
finish.moment: A brief abduction moment, up to about 0.39 Nm/kg, as it releases
finish.cue: Let the hips come level as the edges release

initiation.action: The inside knee moves toward the turn with the tipping (abduction of the flexed thigh), then the thigh settles adducted as the skis tilt
initiation.cue: Move the inside knee into the turn with the skis

shaping.action: Held adducted at hip width, the inside thigh drawn toward the turn under its share of the load
shaping.moment: Adduction, up to about 0.45 Nm/kg in the modelled turn; adductor longus the main contributor
shaping.cue: Inside boot at hip width, not pushed out

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral as the edges release
finish.cue: Keep the stance width as the edges change

initiation.action: Turns inward a little as the knee moves toward the turn, tipping the ski rather than pivoting it; in a carved turn the sidecut turns the ski
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh in the hip socket to tip, not to twist the ski

shaping.action: Held turned in while the ski carves; the snow and boot push the femur further in and the external rotators hold and brake it
shaping.moment: External rotation, up to about 0.17 Nm/kg, from the lateral hamstrings, gluteus maximus and quadratus femoris
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot as the ski bends

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the release
finish.cue: Let the thigh unwind with the release

initiation.action: Turns outward with the tipping so the inside ski tracks with the outside ski
initiation.cue: Turn the inside thigh with the outside one

shaping.action: Held turned out about 10-26° while the hip's internal rotators hold it against an internal rotation moment
shaping.moment: Internal rotation, up to about 0.23 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Keep the inside ski parallel, tip slightly ahead

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral as the edges release
finish.cue: Keep the skis parallel through the release

initiation.action: Comes up from the transition's deep hip hinge as the outside leg lengthens, moving with the thighs and forward with the body; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise and move forward with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open over the long outside leg, more tilted the harder the turn, never standing tall; the pelvis carries most of the forward fold
shaping.moment: Hip and low-back extension, the largest moments in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: The inside half rises against the balance axis as the legs tilt, hiked by the outside hip abductors with the light inside foot helping
initiation.cue: Inside hip up as the skis tip

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, the inside half up and a little forward ("strong inside half"); about 15-33° of list in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Held up under the late load, then lowers toward level as the edges release
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Slight counter set by the end of the transition, the pelvis facing a little toward the outside of the new turn while the femurs turn under it
initiation.cue: Belt buckle a little toward the outside of the new turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held; it stays small in carving, and the upper body may turn a little with the turn
shaping.cue: Quiet pelvis, slightly countered

finish.action: Square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under the turn load, never arched or slumped; a harder turn folds more at the hips, not the low back
shaping.moment: Extension, up to about 1.88 Nm/kg, the largest joint moment in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under the peak load, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski as the legs tilt; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Tip the upper body over the outside ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking; about 11° in GS racing
shaping.moment: Lateral bending, up to about 0.75 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out; more as speed and pitch build

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Straighten up as the turn ends

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.moment: Small, up to about 0.16 Nm/kg in the modelled turn
shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-35° from vertical through the turn, more the harder the turn; it moves forward and rises a little with the hips as the outside leg lengthens
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees, moving forward into the new turn

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held under the turn load, not rounded
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski; more as the edge builds

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight through the finish
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Quiet in space with the pelvis while the femurs turn under; aimed toward the apex of the coming turn
initiation.cue: Chest toward the apex of the new turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the skis carve

finish.action: Square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under
finish.cue: Chest and pelvis square to the skis as they release; the new counter forms as the legs turn under

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward, the hand level with the slope
shaping.cue: Keep the outside hand ready

finish.action: Swings forward to ready the next pole touch
finish.cue: Swing the next pole forward

initiation.action: Swings the pole forward for a light touch as the edges change; a timing touch, not a plant
initiation.cue: Light touch at the edge change

shaping.action: Hand held forward and up, leading with the inside half of the body
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward, not dropped

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides, hands wide for balance
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the touching arm reaches forward from the shoulder
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip; the touching wrist flicks the pole tip forward
initiation.cue: Touch with the wrist, not the arm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes ahead along the path
initiation.cue: Eyes on the next turn

shaping.action: Head held steady against the turn load
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level, or tipped slightly toward the outside with the shoulders
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level with the slope as the body inclines
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head turns toward the coming apex so the eyes lead the turn
initiation.cue: Look where the turn is going

shaping.action: Held toward the path against the slight counter
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Lengthen the knee into the turn, hold it near its longest against the building load, then let it flex under the late load
activations.basis: Vastus medialis and lateralis averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns, with peaks above 150 %, and vastus lateralis ranked first on the outside leg in a model of a carved turn. Dynamic is that turn; gentle and moderate carry about 0.7-1.0 BW on the outside foot at a shallower bend, so their values are our inference. The eccentric share is shorter and lighter than once thought; most of the work is a near-isometric hold

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the outside leg
activations.basis: Measured as an outside-leg knee extensor in recreational turns and at 43 % MVC in instructors' slalom; not reported in GS. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the turn load, brakes the femur's inward turn and helps hold the pelvis up over the deeply flexed hip
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns and ranked second on the outside leg in a model of a carved turn, where it was the main abductor of the deeply flexed hip. Gentle and moderate values are our inference from the lower load

activations.role: Hikes the inside half of the pelvis from the stance hip as the edge builds, helped by the lightly loaded inside foot, and lets it down at the release
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in carved turns, but in mV, which ranks rather than sets a level. The inside ski carries part of the pelvis, so the demand is below a one-ski drill's, and the hip's frontal moment changes sign within the turn

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Not measured in skiing; its role is the pelvic hold that single-leg exercise data rank it high for, here shared with the inside foot

activations.role: Helps tip the thigh inward at initiation and hold the pelvis
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Move the bent thigh's knee toward the turn to tip the ski, then carry the stance hip's adduction moment, yielding as the angulation builds
activations.basis: Adductors averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns. The hip's frontal moment was mostly adduction in one model, so they are a working part of the hold, not just co-contraction. Gentle and moderate values are our inference

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; the GS EMG does not separate it from the other adductors

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and guard the ACL, shares the hip extension moment and brakes the femur's inward turn
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns; a model of a carved turn credited the lateral hamstrings with the hip's external rotation moment. Gentle and moderate values are our inference

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in under the edged load
activations.basis: Ranked among the top outside-leg muscles in a model of a carved turn; semitendinosus 6-15 % MVC in a simulated edged stance

activations.role: Brake and hold the femur's inward turn while the ski carves, and steady the hip joint
activations.basis: Quadratus femoris added to the hip's external rotation moment in a model of a carved turn; model only, and their action shifts with hip flexion

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the feet back and the shins into the tongues as the edges change, then keeps the shin forward against the boot's spring and the load
activations.basis: Averaged above 50 % MVC in GS and parallel turns, read as fore-aft and edge control. How that splits by phase is our inference; the modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction against the calf

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the flexed ankle against the load with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: The modelled ankle moment put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus keeps its length where the gastrocnemius does not. Not measured by EMG in skiing

activations.role: Stiffens the ankle against the boot under load and co-contracts across the bent knee
activations.basis: The medial head averaged above 50 % MVC in GS turns. With the knee bent much of its pull is lost to knee flexion, so it stiffens rather than drives the ankle; gentle and moderate values are our inference

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the big-toe edge early, keep building the edge into late shaping, then let it go
activations.basis: Peroneus longus is reported highly active in racing turns and was recorded on snow, though its activity tracked posture more than measured torsion; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment. On two skis the one-edge balance work is lighter than in a one-ski drill

activations.role: Holds the arch up under the outside foot's load
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole as it moves from ball to heel
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the stance hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The stance hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Let the inside knee bend under its share of the load as the leg shortens, hold the deep bend, then lengthen it into the next turn
activations.basis: Inside vastus lateralis was the most active inside-leg muscle in a model of a carved turn, because the more bent knee needs nearly the outside knee's extension moment on less force; recreational skiers' inside vastus lateralis ran about 54 % below the outside one

activations.role: Draws the inside thigh up as a hip flexor to shorten the inside leg, then holds it
activations.basis: Inside rectus femoris was as active as the outside one in recreational turns while inside vastus lateralis was not, read as a hip-flexor role on the inside leg

activations.role: Helps draw the inside thigh up so the inside leg shortens rather than pushing the skier off the outside ski
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The loaded inside hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only add to what the extensors let go

activations.role: Lets the loaded inside hip fold as the leg shortens, holds it against the hip extension moment, and helps turn the thigh out
activations.basis: The inside hip's extension moment reached about 1.05 Nm/kg in the modelled turn; its share among the extensors is our inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside vasti at the deep bend
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in GS-type turns

activations.role: Co-contract at the deep bend and resist the inside knee's internal rotation moment
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in GS-type turns

activations.role: Hold the inside thigh adducted at hip width against the inside hip's adduction moment, and help hold it against further outward rotation
activations.basis: Adductor longus was the third most active inside-leg muscle and the main inside adductor in a model of a carved turn

activations.role: Its anterior fibres hold the turned-out inside thigh against the internal rotation moment, and it steadies the inside hip
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius was active through steering and the transition on snow; the rotation role is the measured inside-hip moment with moment arms

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh out as the skis tip; once held, the net moment is internal, so they only co-contract to steady the hip
activations.basis: Anatomy and the measured inside-hip moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Flexes the hip and turns the thigh out with the shortening inside leg
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Pulls the inside foot back and tips it onto its little-toe edge first, then presses the shin into the tongue, more after the fall line
activations.basis: The second most active inside-leg muscle in a model of a carved turn, rising after the fall line

activations.role: Help pull the inside foot back and the toes up
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Tips the inside foot onto its little-toe edge with tibialis anterior and builds it with the outside ski
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Shares the inside ankle's smaller plantarflexion moment with the boot
activations.basis: The modelled inside ankle moment was about 45 % below the outside one, carried by muscles and boot

activations.role: Steady the inside foot on its outer border
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the hinged trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, against the largest moment in the turn; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Reached full model activation in a carved turn, where the low-back extension moment was the largest joint moment, and measured in racing turns; no %MVC in GS. Highest from late shaping into the finish with the peak load

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against bending and twist under load
activations.basis: A small lumbar multifidus went with back overuse in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the skier stays off the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in GS and parallel turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the slight counter against the legs' turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Internal oblique was a primary trunk muscle in a model of a carved turn; external oblique ran higher in GS than in parallel or wedge turns. Counter stays small in carving, so the anti-rotation work is lighter than in short turns

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: External oblique ran higher in GS than in parallel or wedge turns

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's growing bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics

activations.role: Steadies the trunk's side bend and twist by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Controls the low back's growing bend toward the outside ski from the lengthened side, then straightens it at the finish; the pelvic hike itself is the outside hip abductors' work
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. Lateral bending reached about 11° in GS, more with the edge angle, so its effort rises with intensity by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Keep the head level against the turn load and turn the eyes toward the next apex
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Swings the pole for the touch and keeps the inside hand up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level with the slope
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles and flick the tip for the touch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier falls back and inward, the outside ski loses its grip, and its inner edge catches as the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries. In a balanced carved turn the knee stays past 60° with the hamstrings co-contracting, which kept the modelled ACL force low
Loaded if the skier banks onto an inside ski that then catches, or if a light inside ski re-engages in a wedge, twisting the knee inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Pulled hard through long quadriceps holds at a deep knee bend, more so at higher intensity and in a flexion transition
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load, about 2.9 BW at the low back in GS; longer turns hold that load longer

one-footed-railroad-track-turn.name: One-footed railroad-track turn, rolled on the outside ski with the inside ski held up

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the foot is drawn back and the shin moves into the tongue at the edge change, pressure toward the ball of the foot so the shovel bites
initiation.cue: Shin to the cuff; more pressure on the ball of the foot

shaping.action: Held flexed with three points of contact in the boot (shin, heel, ball of the foot), with constant small fore-aft corrections
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, small, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Shin to the cuff, some heel, more ball of the foot

finish.action: Opens a little as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright
finish.cue: Let the foot run a little ahead as the arc ends

initiation.action: Lifted; the shin stays forward in the boot so the ski hangs level with the slope
initiation.cue: Lifted ski parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Held with the shin forward
shaping.cue: Lifted ski parallel to the snow

finish.action: Held with the shin forward
finish.cue: Lifted ski parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Rolls from flat onto the big-toe edge inside the boot; the whole drill is this roll on one foot
initiation.cue: Roll onto the big-toe edge from the ankle, not by leaning

shaping.action: The small edge builds to its most at the fall line and holds, with constant small corrections on the one edge

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the edges are set abruptly with the skier back, so the downhill ski catches while the knee straightens and turns in; the slip-catch seen in racing injuries. Our inference for this drill
Pulled hard by the quadriceps braking at a deep knee bend, more so the shorter and faster the stop
Squeezed when the braking load meets a trunk bent forward and sideways and held against twist; our inference from the racers' pattern

finish.action: Flexes a little with the downhill hip to absorb the edge set

initiation.action: The hips drift out over the feet a little to release the edges, so the downhill hip's angulation eases; the abductors let the pelvis tip back a little, pelvis on femur

shaping.action: Held angulated so the body stays plumb over nearly flat skis; the steeper the slope, the more angulation, the uphill half of the pelvis held up over the downhill femur

shaping.cue: Stand tall over the downhill ski; don't lean into the hill

finish.action: The hips move in toward the hill as the edges set, increasing the angulation over the downhill ski

initiation.action: Uphill thigh drawn in, adducted under a pelvis tipped toward the downhill ski; held

shaping.action: Held adducted as the angulation holds

finish.action: Adducts a little more as the angulation grows with the edge set

initiation.action: Turned in under a pelvis facing downhill, the downhill femur internally rotated relative to the pelvis; held as the skis release

shaping.action: Held turned in; in the diagonal version small rotation keeps the skis on a steady line, more turned the more the tips lead
shaping.moment: Small
shaping.cue: Steer the line with the thighs, not the shoulders

finish.action: Held turned in as the edges set
finish.cue: Keep the skis across, the body facing down the hill

initiation.action: Turned out under the downhill-facing pelvis, the uphill femur externally rotated relative to it; held

shaping.action: Held turned out; small adjustments with the downhill femur keep the line in the diagonal version

finish.action: Held turned out as the edges set

initiation.action: Tilted forward with the hip fold, the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held, a little less folded than in a turn
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts a little further forward as the hips fold into the stop, then holds

initiation.action: The uphill half eases down a little as the hips move out over the feet to release
initiation.cue: Let the hips move over the feet

shaping.action: Uphill half held slightly up and forward, carried by the downhill hip's abductors
shaping.cue: Uphill hip slightly up and forward

finish.action: Uphill half rises a little more as the hips move into the hill with the edge set

initiation.action: Faces down the hill, turned about 70-90° from the skis' direction toward the downhill side, mostly from the hip sockets

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill; in the diagonal version it faces the direction of travel more

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; the fold is made at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened under a steady load

finish.action: Held slightly flattened as the braking pitches the trunk forward

initiation.action: The bend toward the downhill ski eases a little as the hips move out over the feet

shaping.action: Bent toward the downhill ski, keeping the shoulders over it while the legs tilt into the hill; more on a steeper slope
shaping.cue: Shoulders over the downhill ski; don't lean into the hill

finish.action: Bends further toward the downhill ski as the edges set and the hips move in

initiation.cue: The facing comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: The facing comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: The facing comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward a little, upper back slightly flexed and quiet

shaping.action: Held

finish.action: Held as the braking pitches it forward

shaping.action: Tipped toward the downhill ski a little more than the pelvis, keeping the shoulders level with the slope's tilt
shaping.cue: Downhill shoulder over the downhill ski

finish.action: Tips further toward the downhill ski with the edge set
finish.cue: Shoulders out over the downhill ski as you stop

initiation.action: Faces down the hill with the pelvis
initiation.cue: Chest down the fall line

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill, quiet

finish.action: Held facing down the hill against the edge set's twist

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level

shaping.action: Arms held forward
shaping.cue: Hands forward and quiet

finish.action: Arms held forward through the stop

shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the hill

activations.role: Hold the flexed downhill knee under most of the skier's weight, then absorb the edge set
activations.basis: Measured as the main load-bearing muscle in normal turns, not in sideslips. Here the load is about body weight, mostly on the downhill leg, below a normal turn's; the edge set's braking adds to it, about 1.4 times body weight when dynamic by Lind & Sanders eq 4.7. Per-setting values are our inference from that load and the deeper stance on steeper pitches

activations.role: Works with the vasti on the downhill knee
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; scaled with the load by inference

activations.role: Holds the hip fold over the downhill ski and brakes it in the edge set
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the hip extension moment here is smaller than in a turn, rising with the edge set. Per-setting values are our inference

activations.role: Holds the angulation over the downhill ski, the uphill half of the pelvis up; eases it to release and adds to it in the edge set. Its front fibres help hold the downhill thigh turned in
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the pelvic hold is mechanics and single-leg exercise data. The angulation needed to stand plumb over nearly flat skis grows with the pitch, so the effort rises with intensity by inference

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and helps hold the downhill thigh turned in
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data and moment arms in hip flexion; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps hold the downhill thigh turned in under the downhill-facing pelvis, and the pelvis level
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the bent downhill thigh turned in and brace against the abductors, more so as the edge bites
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; with the hip bent they are the strongest internal rotators, so they carry much of the turned-in hold, by mechanics

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment in turns; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the downhill knee, more as the edge set loads it
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting and caving in as the edge bites
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; the edge set adds a twisting load by mechanics

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shin on the tongue and makes the small fore-aft adjustments that keep the slip straight
activations.basis: Highly active in normal turns; a light, continuous holding role here, by inference

activations.role: Help tibialis anterior keep the ankle closed
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the ankle against the boot, and holds the shin as the edge set's braking pitches the body forward
activations.basis: Mechanics of braking at the feet; the ankle moment is shared with the boot shaft, as modelled in turns

activations.role: Let the downhill ski flatten to release, hold its few degrees of edge with constant small corrections, then roll it back onto the edge to stop
activations.basis: Recorded on snow, where activity followed posture; edge control in the boot is the drill's main job, but the boot shell carries most of the edging moment. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Holds the arch and co-contracts with the peroneals for fine edge control
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole of the downhill foot
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the more bent uphill knee under its lighter load, and share the edge set
activations.basis: Measured lower on the inside leg in normal turns; here the uphill leg carries perhaps a quarter to a third of the load, our inference

activations.role: Helps hold the uphill thigh turned out under the downhill-facing pelvis, and the hip fold
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the uphill thigh turned out and steady the hip joint
activations.basis: Anatomy; with the hip bent their external rotation moment arm shrinks, so gluteus maximus shares the work

activations.role: Hold the uphill thigh drawn in under the tipped pelvis, and bring the knee into the hill with the edge set
activations.basis: Inside adductor longus is active in a modelled turn; its role here is mechanics

activations.role: Co-contract to steady the bent uphill knee
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; low here by mechanics

activations.role: Keeps the uphill shin on the tongue
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns; light here

activations.role: Lets the uphill ski flatten off its little-toe edge, holds it, then rolls it back to stop
activations.basis: Anatomy and the edge mechanics; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contract with tibialis posterior for fine edge control on the uphill ski
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the uphill ankle against the boot
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the downhill ski, easing it for the release and letting it deepen for the edge set
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The bend grows with the pitch, so its effort rises with intensity by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the uphill side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the trunk facing down the hill, paired with the uphill external oblique; more against the edge set's twist
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; the twisting load in a steady slip is small, rising with the edge set, by inference

activations.role: Pairs with the downhill internal oblique to hold the trunk facing down the hill
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; rising with the edge set by inference

activations.role: Helps the uphill quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the downhill ski
activations.basis: Mechanics; a light role

activations.role: Steadies the side bend by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the hip-hinged trunk with the low back slightly flattened, and stop the braking folding it forward
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the load here is lower than in a turn and the trunk less folded, rising with the edge set's braking, by inference

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist while the legs face across the hill
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured on snow

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes down the hill
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the arms forward
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles
