structures.mechanism: Loaded if the edge set is abrupt with the skier sitting back, so the downhill ski catches while the knee straightens and turns in; the slip-catch seen in racing injuries. Our inference for this drill

carved-j-turn.name: One carved arc on both skis from the fall line to a stop

initiation.action: Closes a little more from the straight run, shin pressed into the tongue, so the forebody engages as the ski tips
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up; shins on the tongues before you tip

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load, a little more the harder the arc; the ski bends from its centre
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the arc loads

finish.action: Opens a little as the foot slides ahead and pressure moves toward the heel, still flexed past upright, shin still touching the tongue
finish.cue: Let the pressure roll back to the heel without leaving the tongue

initiation.action: Closes with the outside ankle, shin into the tongue, so both ankles match
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the downhill one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the shin on the tongue while the inside leg shortens; the boot carries less of the ankle moment than outside
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Matching ankle angles, both shins on the tongues

finish.action: Opens a little with the outside ankle as pressure moves back, shin still on the tongue
finish.cue: Both feet slide ahead together

initiation.action: Everts inside the boot, rolling the ski from flat onto its big-toe edge, early and progressive, with the knee
initiation.cue: Roll the ankles and knees into the turn

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building with the edge to its most around across the hill, holding the edge against the snow force that would flatten it
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep tipping; the edge angle sets the arc

finish.action: Held while the arc tightens, then let back toward flat as the skier comes to rest
finish.cue: Hold the edge to the stop, then let it go

initiation.action: Inverts inside the boot, rolling the uphill ski onto its little-toe edge at the same time and rate as the downhill ski, if anything first
initiation.cue: Tip the uphill foot onto its little-toe edge with the downhill one

shaping.action: Tilt held, building with the outside ski's edge so the two tracks stay parallel
shaping.cue: Two clean lines, the same distance apart

finish.action: Held, then let back toward flat as the skier stops
finish.cue: Release both edges together

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes most of the load
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under the peak load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch held under a lighter load
initiation.cue: Feel all three contact points in the uphill boot too

shaping.action: Arch held under a lighter load
shaping.cue: Feel the uphill foot on the snow

finish.action: Arch held under a lighter load
finish.cue: Feel the uphill foot on the snow

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from the straight-run stance as the edges engage and the CoM moves inside, the long leg of the pair
initiation.cue: Long outside leg, short inside leg

shaping.action: Held quasi-isometric while the load builds to across the hill; about 50° gentle, 55° moderate, 62° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension, building to its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long and steady on the downhill leg

finish.action: Flexes a little under the falling load as the arc tightens and the skier settles to a stop; about 55°, 60°, 66° (our inference)
finish.cue: Settle into the stop, don't stand up

initiation.action: Flexes under its own load as the skis tip, shortening the inside leg so both skis can edge together
initiation.cue: Let the uphill knee bend as you tip

shaping.action: Held more bent than the outside knee, still carrying about a quarter to a third of the load
shaping.moment: Extension, about as large as outside despite the smaller load, because the knee is more bent
shaping.cue: Short uphill leg, still on the snow

finish.action: Lengthens back toward the outside leg as the tilt falls and the skier comes to rest on both feet
finish.cue: Come to rest on two feet

initiation.cue: Roll the knee in by turning the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Uphill knee points where its ski points

shaping.moment: Mostly internal rotation, small
shaping.cue: Uphill knee points where its ski points

finish.cue: Uphill knee points where its ski points

initiation.cue: Knee over the foot as it rolls in

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Uphill knee in line with the foot

shaping.moment: Abduction, small
shaping.cue: Uphill knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Uphill knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Opens a little with the knee as the leg lengthens; the fold stays at the hips
initiation.cue: Grow a little into the arc

shaping.action: Held folded forward at the hip with the pelvis slightly countered, about 45° gentle, 50° moderate, 57° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg at its peak in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus; less at drill speed
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds a little further with the knee as the skier settles to a stop
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as you settle

initiation.action: Flexes under load with the knee, shortening the leg, so the uphill foot drifts a little ahead (lead)
initiation.cue: Uphill knee up and a little forward

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip
shaping.moment: Extension, about as large as outside in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Uphill leg short, uphill foot a little ahead

finish.action: Opens back toward the outside hip as the tilt falls
finish.cue: Even the legs out as you stop

initiation.action: The flexed thigh turns and draws in a little to roll the knee into the turn, then the pelvis tips over the femur as the legs tilt, so the inside half rises; the outside abductors hike it, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Knees in, inside hip up

shaping.action: Hip angulation builds with the edge, the outside hip carrying the inside half of the pelvis with help from the loaded inside foot
shaping.moment: Abduction and adduction both work; its sign varies through a carved turn, so the two co-contract
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out; more as the arc builds

finish.action: Held, angulation growing a little as speed and tilt fall while the edge is kept, then let go as the skier stops
finish.cue: Keep the angle as you slow; level the hips at the stop

initiation.action: The flexed thigh opens and turns out a little so the uphill knee tips into the turn with the downhill one
initiation.cue: Roll both knees, not just the downhill one

shaping.action: Held near neutral beside the outside thigh under a small adduction moment, the boots hip width apart
shaping.moment: Adduction, small, mostly adductor longus in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Feet hip width, no wider

finish.action: Held, then back to neutral as the skier stops
finish.cue: Hip width to the stop

initiation.action: Turns inward a little as the knee rolls in to tip the ski; with the ski carving, it tips, it does not steer
initiation.cue: Roll the knee in from the hip; don't twist the ski

shaping.action: Held turned in while the sidecut turns the ski; the snow pushes the thigh further in, and the external rotators hold it
shaping.moment: External rotation, small, in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Let the ski's shape do the turning

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the stop
finish.cue: Keep the knee over the foot to the end

initiation.action: Turns outward a little as the uphill knee tips into the turn, keeping the skis parallel
initiation.cue: Keep the tips parallel

shaping.action: Held turned out against an internal-rotation moment, so the uphill ski tracks its own line
shaping.moment: Internal rotation, up to about 0.23 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Two clean parallel lines

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral at the stop
finish.cue: Skis parallel to the stop

initiation.action: Comes up a little with the lengthening outside leg; the hinge stays at the hips, the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: The hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hip hinge held, more tilted the harder the arc; tilting further than balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward a little with the hinge as the legs settle; the hips do not drop back behind the feet
finish.cue: Settle, don't sit

initiation.action: The inside half rises against the balance axis as the legs tilt in, hiked by the outside hip abductors
initiation.cue: Uphill hip up

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge, then held; the loaded inside foot supports part of that half
shaping.cue: Don't let the uphill hip drop into the hill

finish.action: Held while the tilt falls and the edge is kept, then levels as the skier stops
finish.cue: Uphill hip up until you stop

initiation.action: Square to the skis in the fall line and quiet while the knees roll
initiation.cue: A quiet pelvis while the knees roll

shaping.action: A slight counter forms as the skis carve away under a pelvis that turns less than they do
shaping.cue: Belt buckle a little down the hill of the skis

finish.action: Counter at its most as the skis come across and up the hill, the pelvis still facing partly down it
finish.cue: Face a little down the hill as the skis climb

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load; a harder arc folds more at the hips, not the low back
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened; fold at the hips

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Starts to bend toward the outside ski as the legs tip; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Tip the legs, keep the upper body over the downhill ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking into the hill
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out

finish.action: Held, a little more as speed falls and the tilt with it, then straightens as the skier stops
finish.cue: Don't lean into the hill as you slow

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-30° from vertical, a little more the harder the arc
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held; the chest does not lift as the skier slows
finish.cue: Don't sit up to stop

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis does; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Keeps building with the edge, then held
shaping.cue: Downhill shoulder over the downhill ski

finish.action: Held as speed falls, then straightens at the stop
finish.cue: Shoulders stay level with the slope to the stop

initiation.action: Quiet with the pelvis, facing down the fall line

activations.role: Lengthen the downhill knee a little as the edges engage, hold it through the carve, then let it settle into the stop
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. Here the downhill leg carries about 0.7 body weight gentle, 0.8 moderate and 1.0 dynamic at the peak, and less as speed bleeds off; the per-setting values are our inference from that load and the knee depth

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the downhill leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded hip against the load with the hamstrings and adductor magnus, and helps hold the thigh's inward turn
activations.basis: The modelled hip extension moment in a carved turn is shared with the hamstrings and adductor magnus, and gluteus maximus also brakes the femur's inward turn there. Scaled like the vasti; the per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Hikes the inside half of the pelvis from the downhill hip as the angulation builds, and holds it while the angulation grows into the slow end of the arc
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the pelvic hold follows from mechanics and single-leg exercise data. Lower than in one-ski drills because the loaded uphill foot supports part of the pelvis; holds up into the finish because angulation grows there as the tilt falls

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius, turns the flexed thigh inward to roll the knee in, and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data and moment arms; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis and turn the thigh inward
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn and draw the bent thigh in to roll the knee and the ski onto its edge, then brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the edging role is mechanics of the bent leg (knee angulation by femoral rotation). Light here, as the arc is carved, not steered

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee, shares the hip extension moment and brakes the thigh's inward turn; guards the knee as pressure moves back at the stop
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance; modelled hip extension and external rotation shares. Scaled with the load

activations.role: Resist the knee twisting outward and caving in
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Let the thigh turn in as the knee rolls, then hold it against the snow while the ski carves, and steady the hip as the pelvis counters
activations.basis: A carved turn's outside hip carries a small external-rotation moment in a model of a GS turn; extrapolated. Their action shifts with hip flexion

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Closes the ankle and pulls the shin onto the tongue as the ski tips, then co-contracts while the net ankle moment is plantarflexion, and lets the ankle open under control at the stop
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where it is highly active; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, holds the flexed ankle against the load with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle a little as pressure moves to the heel
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put a large share in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus, not the gastrocnemius, does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the big-toe edge and keep building the edge to across the hill, then let it go at the stop
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control. The boot shell carries most of the edging moment, so it changes little with intensity; lower at the stop as the edge is let go

activations.role: Holds the arch up under the load and co-contracts with the peroneals
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball as it moves from front to back
activations.basis: Anatomy and the three-point stance cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the downhill hip, a minor role
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The downhill hip carries an extension moment, so the hip flexors only co-contract

activations.role: Let the uphill knee bend under its load as the leg shortens, hold it bent through the carve, then lengthen it back at the stop
activations.basis: Inside vastus lateralis was the most active inside muscle in a modelled carved turn, though about half the outside's EMG in recreational turns; the deeper bend keeps the moment up despite the smaller load

activations.role: Helps hold the uphill thigh up and a little forward while the leg shortens under load; a two-joint muscle whose length the knee and hip change in opposite ways
activations.basis: Measured on the inside leg in recreational turns at the outside leg's level, read as a hip flexor unloading the inside leg

activations.role: Holds the deeply flexed uphill hip under its load and turns the thigh out with the deep rotators
activations.basis: The inside hip carries an extension moment about as large as the outside's in a modelled carved turn; anatomy for the rotation

activations.role: Opens the flexed uphill thigh so the knee tips into the turn, then steadies it against the adductors
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius was measured active through steering in normal turns; its roles here are mechanics

activations.role: With TFL and the adductors, holds the uphill thigh against the internal-rotation moment so it stays turned out
activations.basis: Measured-moment inference; the inside hip carries an internal-rotation moment while it sits turned out, so the internal rotators hold

activations.role: Helps hold the uphill thigh's rotation and flexion
activations.basis: Moment-arm inference; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the uphill thigh beside the downhill one against the adduction moment, mostly adductor longus
activations.basis: Inside adductor longus was a main inside muscle in a modelled carved turn

activations.role: Turn the uphill thigh out as its knee tips into the turn, keeping the skis parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy; with the hip deeply flexed their external rotation moment arm shrinks, so gluteus maximus shares the work

activations.role: Co-contracts with the vasti to steady the deeply bent uphill knee
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the uphill knee against twist and the inward collapse
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Closes the uphill ankle onto the tongue and tips the uphill ski onto its little-toe edge with the downhill one, then holds the shin forward
activations.basis: Inside tibialis anterior was the second most active inside muscle in a modelled carved turn, rising after the fall line

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Tips the uphill ski onto its little-toe edge and holds it there
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Shares the uphill ankle's smaller plantarflexion moment with the boot
activations.basis: The modelled inside ankle moment is about half the outside's

activations.role: Co-contract with the inverters to steady the uphill ski's edge
activations.basis: Mechanics of holding an edge from both sides; not measured on the inside leg

activations.role: Spread the lighter load over the uphill sole
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the downhill ski as angulation builds, and holds it while angulation grows into the slow end of the arc
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The bend grows with the edge and stays up as the tilt falls, so its effort holds into the finish by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the uphill side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the slight counter while the skis carve away underneath, paired with the uphill external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; light here, as the skis are not steered against the trunk

activations.role: Pairs with the downhill internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Helps the uphill quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the downhill ski
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics

activations.role: Steadies the trunk's side bend by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and keeps the hips from dropping back at the stop
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where the low back carries the largest modelled joint moment. Scaled with the load, which peaks around across the hill

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes on the arc while the chest counters
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arms forward, the hands in view
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms held forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles lightly
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier sits back as the arc slows and the downhill ski's inside edge catches while the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries; a back-weighted stop pushes the shin forward through the boot
Our inference; loaded if the uphill ski catches its edge and is forced out into a wedge, twisting the knee inward, as in the dynamic snowplow seen in racing
The uphill knee is held deeply bent under load through the carve, which pulls hard on the tendon for its load
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load, the side bend and counter largest near the stop

crab-wedge-turn.name: Wedge turn carved on the outside ski, inside ski brushing

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the ski is tipped up and takes the weight, the shin pressed into the tongue so the forebody engages
initiation.cue: Shin to the tongue as the ski tips up

shaping.action: Held flexed against the load so the pressure stays over the middle of the foot while the ski bends
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue; three contact points in the boot

finish.action: Stays closed, shin on the tongue, as the edge is released; the wedge never sits back on the heels
finish.cue: Stay over the middle of the foot as the edge lets go

initiation.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, as the ski lightens and flattens
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed while the ski brushes under a lighter load
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, small
shaping.cue: Shin on the tongue while the inside ski brushes

finish.action: Presses further into the tongue as the ski is tipped up and takes the weight for the next turn
finish.cue: Shin forward as this ski becomes the outside ski

initiation.action: Everts inside the boot, rolling the ski up from the low wedge edge onto a higher big-toe edge, with the femur turning in
initiation.cue: Roll the outside ankle in; tip the ski with the lower leg

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion, mostly carried by the boot shell
shaping.cue: Keep tipping the outside ski until it bends and carves

finish.action: Lets the edge back down to the low wedge edge as the other ski tips up; the ski never goes flat or onto its other edge
finish.cue: Let the outside edge soften; stay in the wedge

initiation.action: Lets the old outside ski's edge down toward flat, still on its big-toe edge, so it can brush
initiation.moment: Eversion, falling
initiation.cue: Flatten the inside ski; don't lift it onto its little-toe edge

shaping.action: Held low on its big-toe edge, with small inversion and eversion corrections so it brushes without catching
shaping.cue: Inside ski light and flat enough to brush

finish.action: Begins to evert and tip up for the next turn as the outside ski releases
finish.cue: Start tipping the inside ski up as the outside one softens

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes most of the load and the ankle rolls in
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under the peak load on the big-toe edge
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing as you tip

finish.action: Arch held as the load moves to the other foot
finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the whole foot

initiation.action: Arch held under a falling load
initiation.cue: A quiet inside foot

shaping.action: Arch held under a light load while the ski brushes
shaping.cue: A quiet inside foot

finish.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the load again
finish.cue: Stand on the whole foot as it takes over

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from the hand-over as the leg takes most of the weight; a small range, the wedge never rises tall
initiation.cue: Stand a little taller on the outside ski as it tips up

shaping.action: Held quasi-isometric while the ski carves, about 35-45° of flexion, a little deeper at the dynamic setting (our inference)
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Steady outside leg while the ski bends

finish.action: Flexes a little as the edge releases and the weight moves to the other ski
finish.cue: Soften the outside leg as the other ski takes over

initiation.action: Flexes a little as the weight leaves it, so the inside leg is the shorter one while the pelvis moves over the outside ski
initiation.moment: Extension, falling
initiation.cue: Let the inside leg soften as the outside ski takes the weight

shaping.action: Held a little more bent than the outside knee, still loaded while the ski brushes
shaping.moment: Extension, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Inside leg a little shorter, still on the snow

finish.action: Lengthens as it takes the weight and becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Grow onto the next outside ski

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the edged ski invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Inside knee points along its ski

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist of the brushing ski
shaping.cue: Inside knee points along its ski

finish.cue: Inside knee points along its ski

initiation.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the wedge invites
initiation.cue: Knee over the big toe, not caving inside it

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee over the big toe, not caving inside it

finish.cue: Knee over the foot

initiation.cue: Inside knee over its foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse if the brushing edge bites
shaping.cue: Inside knee over its foot, not falling in

finish.cue: Inside knee over its foot

initiation.action: Opens a little with the knee as the leg takes the weight; the hinge stays at the hips
initiation.cue: Rise a little over the outside ski

shaping.action: Held flexed about 35-45° (our inference), folded at the hip over the carving ski
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds a little with the knee as the weight leaves it
finish.cue: Soften at the hips as the other ski takes over

initiation.action: Folds a little more than the outside hip as the leg lightens and shortens
initiation.moment: Extension, falling
initiation.cue: Inside hip folds, not drops

shaping.action: Held a little more flexed than the outside hip, still loaded
shaping.moment: Extension, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Inside leg a little shorter

finish.action: Opens as the leg takes the weight for the next turn
finish.cue: Grow onto the next outside leg

initiation.action: The pelvis moves across over the outside ski and the knee moves in, so the hip goes from the wedge's abduction toward neutral; the abductors lengthen under control while the adductors brace
initiation.moment: Abduction, holding the pelvis over the stance hip
initiation.cue: Move the hips over the outside ski, inside hip up

shaping.action: Held, the outside hip carrying most of the pelvis with the inside ski as a light second support; abductors and adductors co-contract
shaping.moment: Abduction, with adductor co-contraction keeping the wedge size
shaping.cue: Stay over the outside hip; keep the wedge the same size

finish.action: The pelvis moves back toward the middle of the wedge and the hip returns to its abducted wedge position
finish.cue: Move back to the middle as the other ski takes over

initiation.action: Abducts a little further as the pelvis moves away over the outside ski while the inside foot stays wide; adductors keep the wedge from opening
initiation.cue: Keep the wedge size as you move over the outside ski

shaping.action: Held abducted in the wedge, adductors and abductors co-contracting
shaping.cue: Wedge the same size, tip to tail

finish.action: Comes back toward the wedge's middle as the pelvis moves over this foot
finish.cue: Move over this foot as it takes over

initiation.action: Turns inward a little beyond the wedge's internal rotation, moving the knee in so the ski rolls up its edge; the adductors and anterior gluteals drive it at this hip flexion
initiation.cue: Turn the outside thigh in to tip the ski

shaping.action: Held turned in, holding the edge against the snow's torque that would flatten the ski and push the knee out
shaping.moment: Internal rotation, small
shaping.cue: Keep the thigh turned in while the ski carves

finish.action: Lets the thigh turn back out to the wedge position as the edge releases
finish.cue: Let the thigh unwind as the edge softens

initiation.action: Held turned in at the wedge angle, tip toward the other tip, as the ski flattens
initiation.cue: Keep the inside tip in its place

shaping.action: Held turned in against the brushing ski, whose drag would swing its tip outward
shaping.moment: Internal rotation, small
shaping.cue: Inside ski steady; don't let it wander

finish.action: Turns in a little further as this ski is tipped up for the next turn
finish.cue: Turn this thigh in as it becomes the outside leg

initiation.action: Hip hinge kept as the pelvis moves across, the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Hinge at the hips over the outside ski

shaping.action: Hinge held, a little more at the dynamic setting; tilting further forward than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Hinge held as the weight moves to the other ski
finish.cue: Stay hinged; don't sit back in the wedge

initiation.action: As the pelvis moves over the outside ski its inside half rises a little against the balance axis, held by the outside abductors with the inside ski's help
initiation.cue: Inside hip up a little as you move over the outside ski

shaping.action: Held a little up while the edge peaks; small, because the inside ski still supports it
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop

finish.action: Levels as the pelvis returns to the middle of the wedge
finish.cue: Level the hips for the hand-over

initiation.action: Quiet, facing along the path, while the outside thigh turns in under it
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Held quiet, a touch toward the outside ski
shaping.cue: Belt buckle along the path, a touch toward the outside ski

finish.action: Held quiet through the hand-over
finish.cue: Quiet hips

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load, never arched or slumped
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends a little toward the outside ski as the upper body aligns over it; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Upper body over the outside ski

shaping.action: Small bend held while the edge peaks, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than leaning into the turn
shaping.cue: Hips over the outside ski, shoulders level with the slope

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the weight moves to the middle
finish.cue: Straighten up for the hand-over

initiation.cue: The legs turn in the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: The legs turn in the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: The legs turn in the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward about 15-25° from vertical (our inference), over the knees
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up in the wedge

initiation.action: Tips a little toward the outside ski with the low back; the inside obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Small bend held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight
finish.cue: Shoulders level for the hand-over

initiation.action: Quiet with the pelvis while the thighs turn under
initiation.cue: A quiet upper body

shaping.action: Held quiet, facing along the path

activations.role: Lengthen the outside knee a little as it takes the weight, hold it while the ski carves, then let it soften as the other ski takes over
activations.basis: Measured high in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract) and low in the plough in recreational women (hermann-2023). Here the outside leg carries about 70-85 % of about body weight at a modest bend; the per-setting values are our inference from load and depth

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the stance leg
activations.basis: Measured as an outside-leg knee extensor in normal turns; low at wedge loads by inference

activations.role: Holds the folded outside hip against the load and helps hold the pelvis over it
activations.basis: Measured more active in wedge than in parallel turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract); scaled with load and fold by inference

activations.role: Controls the pelvis moving across over the outside ski, holds its inside half up while the edge peaks, and its front fibres help turn the thigh in
activations.basis: Measured on snow in normal turns and in single-leg stance off snow; the inside ski still shares the pelvic support, so it stays at 2 at every setting

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold and, in hip flexion, turns the thigh in
activations.basis: Off-snow single-leg EMG and moment arms; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps turn the thigh in and hold the pelvis
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise EMG; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh in to tip the ski and hold the edge, and brace against the abductors so the wedge keeps its size
activations.basis: Adductors averaged above 50 % MVC in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract); the edging role is the mechanics of the flexed leg (LeMaster). Placed at 2 because this wedge is small and slow

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment and braces the wedge
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee
activations.basis: Measured high in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997) but with the least hamstring co-contraction of any task in the plough (hermann-2023); placed low

activations.role: Resist the knee caving in and twisting under the tipped ski
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low hamstring co-contraction in the plough

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the outside foot in to tip the ski up its edge and keep building it into late shaping, then let it back down
activations.basis: Tipping from the lower leg is the drill's point (psia-c-crab-wedge); peroneus longus is highly active in turns, attributed to edge control. A balance and edging effort, so it changes little with intensity; the boot shell carries most of the moment

activations.role: Pulls the shin to the tongue as the ski tips up, then co-contracts to keep it there
activations.basis: Measured high in turns including wedge turns; the modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, then shares the plantarflexion moment with the boot
activations.basis: Modelled ankle moments in carving; low at wedge loads by inference

activations.role: Holds the arch up as the ankle rolls in
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole on the big-toe edge
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Let the inside knee soften as the weight leaves it, hold it lightly loaded, then lengthen it as it takes over
activations.basis: Inside vasti were about half the outside value in normal turns (kroll-2010); the hand-over in the finish raises it by inference

activations.role: Controls the inside hip folding as it lightens, then opens it as it takes over
activations.basis: Inferred from the inside leg's extension moment in a modelled turn

activations.role: Keep the wedge from opening as the pelvis moves away, and help hold the brushing ski's tip in
activations.basis: Adductors were high in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract); this side's role is wedge geometry

activations.role: Co-contracts with the adductors to set the wedge, its front fibres holding the thigh turned in; takes the pelvis again at the hand-over
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns (seifert-2023); this role is mechanics

activations.role: Helps hold the inside thigh turned in, then turns it in further for the next turn
activations.basis: Moment arms and exercise EMG; not measured on snow

activations.role: Let the inside ski's edge down toward flat, keep it brushing, then tip it up for the next turn
activations.basis: Mechanics of the edge release and re-engagement; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the peroneals so the brushing ski stays steady and doesn't catch
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the inside shin on the tongue, then pulls it in as this ski becomes the outside ski
activations.basis: Inside tibialis anterior was the second most active inside muscle in a modelled carved turn (heinrich-2023)

activations.role: Steadies the lightly loaded inside knee
activations.basis: Low hamstring co-contraction in the plough (hermann-2023)

activations.role: Resist the inside knee falling in if the brushing edge bites
activations.basis: Mechanics of the wedge catch; not measured

activations.role: Controls the low back's small bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it

activations.role: Co-contracts to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps control the trunk's small bend toward the outside ski
activations.basis: Mechanics; not measured in this movement

activations.role: Keep the upper body quiet while the outside thigh turns in
activations.basis: External oblique was lower in wedge than in parallel or GS turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract)

activations.role: Pairs with the external obliques to keep the trunk quiet
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing; little twist to resist in a wedge

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the skier stays off the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in turns

activations.role: Hold the hinged trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Measured in turns, lower in the wedge than in parallel turns; the fold is shallow at wedge speeds

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back
activations.basis: Not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the brushing inside ski's edge catches in the wedge, so the ski is pulled outward and the knee is twisted inward and falls in; the wedge catch that Lind & Sanders describe and the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Our inference from the same wedge catch; the knee falling in opens its inner side

Loaded if the knee is pushed in over the foot to tip the ski (valgus with internal rotation) instead of turning the thigh, and more so if the skier sits back; caught edges in that position are the slip-catch pattern

dolphin-turn.name: Turn that loads the tails at the finish, lifts the tips and retracts the legs into the next turn

initiation.action: Closes hard out of the transition, toes pulled up and the feet drawn back under the hips so the tips point down, then the shin meets the tongue as the tips land and the forebody engages; flexed about as far as it goes in the turn
initiation.moment: Dorsiflexion in the air, unloaded; plantarflexion once the tips land and the load comes on, shared with the boot shaft
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and point the tips down

shaping.action: Held flexed with the shin on the tongue against the rising load to the fall line, a little more flexed the harder the turn
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens deliberately, the feet sliding forward under the hips until the shin leaves the tongue and rests toward the spoiler; still dorsiflexed in the shell, about 8-12° (inference), never pointed. Pressure goes through the heel to the tail
finish.moment: Plantarflexion while the feet are pushed forward, then dorsiflexion once the load point is behind the heel, held by the rear spoiler with tibialis anterior
finish.cue: Let the feet run ahead; feel the heels and the tails

initiation.action: Closes with the outside ankle in the retraction, toes up, tip pointed down, the shin on the tongue as the ski lands
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, more lightly loaded than the outside
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Inside shin on the tongue too

finish.action: Opens with the outside ankle as both feet slide forward and both tails load; the inside foot leads a little
finish.cue: Both feet forward together

initiation.action: Everts as the tips land, putting the new outside ski on its big-toe edge from the first contact
initiation.cue: Land on the big-toe edge

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to its most in late shaping, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep rolling onto the big-toe edge past the fall line

finish.action: Releases toward flat as the pressure moves aft; the tails still grip enough to bend
finish.cue: Let the edge go as you move back

initiation.action: Inverts as the ski lands, onto its little-toe edge with the outside ski, leading the tip-over
initiation.cue: Land on the little-toe edge

shaping.action: Inversion held, building with the outside edge
shaping.cue: Keep the inside ski tipped with the outside

finish.action: Releases toward flat with the outside foot
finish.cue: Flatten both skis together

initiation.action: Arch held as the landing loads the forefoot
initiation.cue: Land on the ball of the foot with the heel in contact

shaping.action: Arch held under peak load, pressure spread
shaping.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

finish.action: Arch held as the pressure runs back along the inside of the foot to the heel
finish.cue: Ball, arch, heel

initiation.cue: A quiet inside foot

shaping.cue: A quiet inside foot

finish.cue: A quiet inside foot

initiation.action: Pulled up in the retraction, about 90-100° at its deepest (inference), then catches the landing as the tips touch and lengthens a little as the new turn loads
initiation.moment: Flexion in the air; extension once the tips land, briefly up to about 2 times body weight in the reference catch (L&S Fig 5.4a)
initiation.cue: Land soft on the tips, then grow into the turn

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds; about 62° gentle, 68° moderate, 74° dynamic (our inference)
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long and steady on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the late load while the feet slide forward; with the load point behind the heel the knee extension moment climbs, about 75° gentle, 80° moderate, 86° dynamic at the end (our inference)
finish.moment: Extension, rising as the pressure moves back
finish.cue: Flex as the tails load, hips stay above the knees

initiation.action: Pulled up in the retraction with the outside knee, the old outside leg shortening most, then catches the landing
initiation.cue: Pull both feet up under you

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside knee and loaded, so the inside leg is shorter and both skis tip together
shaping.moment: Extension, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Inside leg short, outside leg long

finish.action: Flexes with the outside knee as both tails load, the inside foot a little ahead
finish.cue: Both legs absorb

initiation.moment: Resisting the twist of the landing
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Knee points where the ski points

shaping.cue: Knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Knee points where the ski points

initiation.moment: Resisting the inward collapse a landing on edge invites
initiation.cue: Land with the knee over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot

initiation.cue: Land with the knee over the foot

shaping.cue: Knee over the foot

finish.cue: Knee over the foot

initiation.action: Flexes hard in the retraction, drawing the knee up and forward over the boot so the tip drops, about 85-95° (inference); then opens a little as the leg lengthens into the turn
initiation.moment: Flexion in the air, from the hip flexors; extension once loaded
initiation.cue: Knees up and forward, tips down

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded at the hip with the pelvis countered, about 52° gentle, 58° moderate, 65° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further as the feet run ahead and the hips drop back toward the heels; the chest stays forward so the hips do not sink below the knees
finish.moment: Extension, rising with the load behind the heel
finish.cue: Hips back for a moment, chest still forward

initiation.action: Flexes in the retraction, the old outside leg pulled up most, knee forward so the tip drops, then catches the landing
initiation.cue: Pull the old outside foot up and back

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip and loaded; the inside leg stays short
shaping.moment: Extension, like the outside hip
shaping.cue: Inside knee up and forward

finish.action: Folds with the outside hip as both tails load
finish.cue: Fold at both hips

initiation.action: Moves toward abduction, pelvis on femur, as the legs tip in on landing and the outside ski takes the load
initiation.cue: Keep the inside hip up as you land

shaping.action: Hip angulation builds with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.moment: Changes sign within the turn in models of carving; abductors and adductors co-contract
shaping.cue: Strong over the outside hip

finish.action: Releases toward neutral as the edges flatten and the pressure moves aft
finish.cue: Level out as you move back

initiation.action: The inside knee tips toward the turn with the ski as it lands; the thigh is drawn a little toward the outside leg
initiation.cue: Tip the inside knee in with the ski

shaping.action: Adducted and held beside the outside leg
shaping.moment: Adduction (adductor longus in a modelled carved turn)
shaping.cue: Keep the knees in step

finish.action: Held, then returns toward neutral as the edges release
finish.cue: Feet hip-width

initiation.action: Turns inward as the skis land and the legs steer them into the new turn, with the skis light for the instant after landing
initiation.cue: Steer from the thighs as you land

shaping.action: Held turned in, the rotation spread through the turn rather than rushed
shaping.moment: Small; internal when steering, external if carved
shaping.cue: Smooth, steady leg rotation

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral as the edges release
finish.cue: Let the thighs unwind with the release

initiation.action: Turns outward with the turn as the ski lands, keeping it parallel
initiation.cue: Turn the inside thigh out with the turn

shaping.action: Held turned out against a small internal moment
shaping.moment: Internal (modelled), so the internal rotators hold
shaping.cue: Keep the skis parallel

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral
finish.cue: Skis parallel as they release

initiation.action: Tilted forward with the hip fold in the retraction, the abdominals and hip flexors drawing the legs up; comes up a little with the hips as the legs lengthen after the landing. Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Pull the knees up, don't round the back

shaping.action: Hinge held, more tilted the harder the turn; never standing tall, never arched
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened

finish.action: Tilts forward further as the hips drop back toward the heels, so the chest stays over the knees and the low back does not arch to compensate
finish.cue: Hips back, chest forward

initiation.action: The inside half rises as the legs tip in on landing, held by the outside hip abductors
initiation.cue: Inside hip up as you land

shaping.action: Inside half held up, building with the edge; the loaded inside foot gives some support
shaping.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop

finish.action: Levels as the edges release
finish.cue: Level the hips for the edge change

initiation.action: Quiet while the legs, light after the landing, turn under it; the pole plant steadies it
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Slight counter held, a by-product of the legs turning
shaping.cue: Belt buckle a little toward the outside of the turn

finish.action: Counter held as the legs flex; it squares as the skis release
finish.cue: Upper body calm as the feet run ahead

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; the retraction folds the hips, not the spine
initiation.moment: Extension, small in the air, rising with the landing
initiation.cue: Fold at the hips to pull the knees up, not the back

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened under load
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened as the hips move back; arching it to keep the chest up is the fault
finish.cue: Don't arch as you move back

initiation.action: Bends toward the outside ski as the skis land on edge; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Upper body over the outside ski

shaping.action: Builds with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the edges release
finish.cue: Straighten up as the skis flatten

initiation.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Counter comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward over the knees through the retraction and landing, so the CoM is over the forebody when the tips touch
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees as the tips land

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Kept forward while the hips go back; sitting up here is what turns a moment aft into the back seat
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the tails load

initiation.action: Tips toward the outside ski as the skis land on edge; the inside obliques lengthen
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Builds with the edge, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight with the release
finish.cue: Shoulders come level

initiation.action: Quiet, facing a little down the hill, steadied by the pole plant while the legs turn under
initiation.cue: Chest a little toward the outside of the turn

shaping.action: Slight counter held against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the legs turn

finish.action: Held facing down the hill as the legs flex; squares as the skis release
finish.cue: Chest stays down the hill

initiation.action: Shoulder blades forward and level; the planting side reaches
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Held forward; reaching the hands forward helps keep the chest forward as the hips go back
finish.cue: Reach forward as you move back

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward
shaping.cue: Keep the outside hand ready

finish.action: Swings forward to ready the next plant
finish.cue: Swing the next pole early

initiation.action: Plants the pole as the tips leave the snow, tip ahead of the hand, then the arm passes it and stays forward
initiation.moment: Extension at the plant, small
initiation.cue: Plant as the tips come up

shaping.action: Hand held forward, leading
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the planting arm braces against the pole as it meets the snow
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Grip firms for the plant; the planting wrist sets the pole tip ahead
initiation.cue: Plant with the wrist and forearm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held; the next pole tip swings forward
finish.cue: Ready the next pole

initiation.action: Head up, eyes ahead down the hill, steady through the retraction and landing
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead, not on the tips

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held up as the hips go back
finish.cue: Head up, chest forward

initiation.action: Head kept level
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head turned against the countered chest so the eyes stay on the path
initiation.cue: Look where you are going

shaping.action: Held against the counter
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Catches the landing and lengthens the knee into the turn, holds it through shaping, then absorbs the late load as the feet run ahead and the load point moves behind the heel
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. The drill adds two things by mechanics, both our inference. In the finish the load point behind the heel raises the knee extension moment the vasti must hold, the back-seat mechanism, so the finish rises above the stork's. At initiation the landing catch, at most about 2 times body weight briefly in the reference cycle, comes after a near-zero-load retraction, so the phase averages lower than its peak

activations.role: Pulls the thigh up in the retraction, then works with the vasti as a knee extensor once the ski is loaded
activations.basis: Rectus femoris was much higher in flexion transitions than in extension transitions in instructors on snow (seifert-2023, mV, used to rank only); its knee-extensor role on the outside leg is measured in normal turns

activations.role: Pulls the leg up and the knee forward in the retraction so the tip drops; afterwards co-contracts to steady the pelvis
activations.basis: Inference; iliopsoas has never been measured on snow. Active retraction is hip-flexor work by mechanics (LeMaster pp 97-98, L&S p 120); its share at deep hip flexion comes from off-snow EMG

activations.role: Catches the hip fold on landing, holds the folded hip against the turn load, then controls the deeper fold as the hips move back over the heels
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn; measured above 50 % MVC in normal turns. The deeper finish fold with the load aft raises it, our inference

activations.role: Holds the inside half of the pelvis up as the skis land on edge and the angulation builds, then lets it level as the edges release
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the pelvic hold is pelvis-on-femur mechanics backed by single-leg exercise data. The loaded inside ski shares the pelvis, so it stays below the stork's one-leg hold

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the femoral head on landing
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps flex the hip in the retraction and turn the thigh inward as the skis land
activations.basis: Exercise EMG for hip flexion and abduction; not measured on snow

activations.role: Turn the bent thigh inward to steer and edge the landed ski, then brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the steering role is mechanics of the bent leg

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings, more so in the deep finish fold
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the foot up and back in the retraction; through the turn co-contracts with the quadriceps, and in the finish guards the knee against the forward pull of the tibia when the load is aft
activations.basis: Hamstrings measured in normal turns; the retraction is knee-flexor work by mechanics. Co-contraction protects the ACL with the knee bent and the hips above the knees (heinrich-2023, LeMaster p 62); the boot-and-quadriceps drawer when aft is the back-seat mechanism (bere-2011). Finish values are our inference

activations.role: Help pull the foot up in the retraction; resist the knee caving in and twisting, and the anterior drawer when the load is aft
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns. Retraction and aft roles are mechanics

activations.role: Steady the hip joint and brake the thigh's inward turn when the ski grips
activations.basis: Extrapolated from a model of a carved turn; the sign depends on carving or brushing

activations.role: Pulls the toes up and the foot back to point the tip down before it lands; co-contracts through shaping; in the finish lets the ankle open under control and, with the rear spoiler, holds the shin once the load point is behind the heel
activations.basis: Highly active in normal turns; the drill makes its closing the cue that lands the tips first. The finish role follows from the force line behind the ankle (L&S p 54, pp 192-193), our inference. Dynamic needs a faster, bigger closing after a higher tip lift

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior to point the tip down
activations.basis: Anatomy and the coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin meets the tongue on landing, holds the flexed ankle with the boot shaft, then pushes the feet forward to open the ankle at the finish
activations.basis: Modelled ankle moments put the muscles' share near the boot's; with the knee bent the soleus does the ankle work. Pushing the feet forward is plantarflexion (LeMaster p 81); its size in a boot is small, our inference

activations.role: Helps flex the knee in the retraction; adds a little ankle stiffness, slack with the knee bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Put the landing ski on its big-toe edge, build the edge into late shaping, then let it go
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment

activations.role: Holds the arch as the pressure runs from the ball to the heel
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole as it moves from forefoot to heel
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Catch the landing and hold the short, loaded inside leg; absorb with the outside leg as both tails load
activations.basis: Inside vastus lateralis measured about half the outside in normal turns (kroll-2010); the inside knee still needs an extension moment because it is more flexed (heinrich-2022). The aft finish raises it, our inference

activations.role: Pulls the old outside leg up hardest in the retraction, then holds the inside leg short as a hip flexor
activations.basis: Inside rectus femoris was higher in flexion transitions in instructors (seifert-2023) and works as a hip flexor on the inside leg in normal turns (kroll-2010). Dynamic retracts further from a bigger tail load, our inference

activations.role: Pulls the inside thigh up in the retraction and helps keep the inside leg short
activations.basis: Inference from off-snow hip-flexor EMG; never measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the inside foot up and back under the hips in the retraction, then co-contracts
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the retraction is mechanics

activations.role: Help pull the inside foot up and steady the knee
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Holds the deeply flexed, loaded inside hip and helps turn the thigh out
activations.basis: The inside hip needs an extension moment close to the outside's in a modelled carved turn because it is more flexed (heinrich-2022)

activations.role: Hold the inside thigh beside the outside leg; adductor longus carries the inside hip's adduction moment
activations.basis: Modelled in a carved turn (heinrich-2023)

activations.role: Its front fibres hold the inside thigh against further outward rotation
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius active in normal turns (seifert-2023); the rotation-holding role is the modelled internal moment (heinrich-2022)

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh out with the turn as the ski lands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Points the inside tip down with the outside one and tips the ski onto its little-toe edge; holds the shin on the tongue
activations.basis: Inside tibialis anterior was the second most active inside muscle in a modelled carved turn (heinrich-2023); the tip-pointing is the drill's cue

activations.role: Pull the toes up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Tips the inside ski onto its little-toe edge and holds it
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the inside ankle against the lighter load, then pushes the foot forward with the outside one
activations.basis: Modelled inside ankle moment about half the outside's (heinrich-2022)

activations.role: Helps pull the legs up in the retraction with the hip flexors, then balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened and the skier does not sit back
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns; LeMaster names the abdominals with iliopsoas as the active flexors of a retraction (pp 97-98). The retraction level is our inference

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened, through the landing, the turn and the deeper fold as the hips move back
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the lumbar extension moment is the largest in a modelled carved turn. Rises when dynamic with the deeper fold and higher load

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back through the landing
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk for the landing without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the upper body quiet against the legs' turning as the light skis are steered after the landing, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the counter
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it at the release
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's side bend
activations.basis: Mechanics of the side bend

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes ahead through the landing
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow
