structures.mechanism: Loaded if the moment aft becomes a position, the trunk behind the knees, and the skier lands or recovers on the tails; the rear spoiler pushes the tibia forward while the quadriceps contract hard, the back-weighted landing seen in racing injuries
Loaded if a tip lands on its inside edge with the knee straight and turned in, so the ski catches; the slip-catch pattern
Pulled hard in the landing catch at a deep knee bend and in the aft finish, where the knee extension moment climbs
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist under the turn load and the landing; worse if the retraction folds the back instead of the hips

one-ski-straight-run.name: Straight run on one flat ski, inside tail held up

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the weight moves onto the stance foot, shin pressed lightly into the tongue so the CoM sits over the middle of the foot
initiation.cue: Shin on the tongue as the weight arrives

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin lightly on the tongue, with small fore-aft corrections; friction at the snow pitches the skier forward, so the reaction sits a little ahead of the CoM
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, small, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Light, steady shin pressure; balance over the whole foot

finish.action: Held flexed as the other ski's tail is set down; the shin stays on the tongue
finish.cue: Keep the shin forward as the other foot comes down

initiation.action: Flexed, shin on the tongue, as the tail lifts so the ski pitches tip down with the tip resting on the snow
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the stance one

shaping.action: Held flexed with the tip resting; the ski's heavier forebody and the snow under the tip balance it, so little ankle effort is needed
shaping.cue: Tip resting on the snow, not pressed

finish.action: Stays closed, shin on the tongue, as the tail comes down to take weight
finish.cue: Set the ski down with the shin already forward

initiation.action: Ski kept flat as the whole weight arrives on one foot; inverters and evertors stiffen the foot in the boot
initiation.cue: Flat ski, weight across heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Held flat by constant small inversion and eversion corrections inside the boot; the edge is offset from the ankle, so any tilt makes a roll moment the foot must answer at once
shaping.moment: Near zero, alternating
shaping.cue: Keep the ski flat; let it neither roll in nor out

finish.action: Held flat as the other ski is set down beside it
finish.cue: Both skis flat as they meet the snow

initiation.action: The lifted ski is held flat, parallel to the stance ski, by light inversion and eversion inside the boot
initiation.cue: Lift the tail level, not tilted

shaping.action: Held flat and parallel
shaping.cue: Lifted ski parallel to the stance ski

finish.action: Held flat so the ski lands on its base, not an edge
finish.cue: Land the ski flat, at hip width

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the whole weight
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up; pressure spread to keep the ski flat
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as the weight starts to share
finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the whole foot

initiation.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

shaping.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

finish.cue: A quiet foot as it lands

initiation.action: Settles a little deeper as the whole weight arrives on one leg
initiation.cue: Sink a little onto the stance leg

shaping.action: Held in a centred stance, about 35-45° flexed (our inference), quasi-isometric with small flex and extend corrections over ripples; a little deeper the faster the run
shaping.moment: Extension, about body weight on one leg
shaping.cue: Steady, supple stance leg; soak up the bumps

finish.action: Lengthens a little as the other foot takes back its share
finish.cue: Rise slightly as both skis carry you

initiation.action: Flexes to raise the tail once the weight is over the stance ski; the tip stays on the snow
initiation.cue: Weight over, then lift the heel toward your seat

shaping.action: Held more bent than the stance knee, the tail at a steady height
shaping.cue: Keep the tail at the same height

finish.action: Lengthens with the hip to set the tail down
finish.cue: Lower the tail, don't drop it

initiation.cue: Knee and ski point down the run

shaping.moment: Small, from the ski wandering off line
shaping.cue: Knee and ski point down the run

finish.cue: Knee and ski point down the run

initiation.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

shaping.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Set the ski down straight

initiation.cue: Knee over the foot as the weight arrives

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse single-leg stance invites
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee over the foot

initiation.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

shaping.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Set the ski down without the knee caving in

initiation.action: Folds a little with the knee as the weight arrives, the hinge at the hip
initiation.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

shaping.action: Held about 35-45° flexed (our inference), hinged so the CoM stays over the middle of the foot; extensors hold the trunk against the forward pitch from snow friction
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Hips over the middle of the foot, chest a little forward

finish.action: Opens a little with the knee as the weight is shared again
finish.cue: Rise slightly with the knee

initiation.action: Flexes to hold the thigh up while the knee lifts the tail; hip flexion shortens the leg as a whole
initiation.cue: Bring the thigh up a little; the tip stays on the snow

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the stance hip, the hip flexors holding the leg, boot and ski up
shaping.cue: Thigh held up, tip resting

finish.action: Lowered to set the tail down
finish.cue: Lower the leg under control

initiation.action: As the other foot unweights, the stance hip's abductors hold up the lifted side of the pelvis, pelvis on femur, while the pelvis shifts over the stance foot
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted-side hip up

shaping.action: Held, the lifted side of the pelvis level or a touch up, with small corrections that move the CoM over the flat ski
shaping.moment: Abduction
shaping.cue: Hips level; stand tall over the stance hip

finish.action: Lets the lifted side down as the other foot is set down
finish.cue: Level the hips as both skis meet the snow

initiation.action: Kept at hip width as the tail lifts, neither drawn in nor out
initiation.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

shaping.action: Held at hip width beside the stance leg
shaping.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

finish.action: Held, then the foot is set down at hip width
finish.cue: Set the foot down at hip width, not wide

initiation.cue: Thigh and ski face down the run

shaping.moment: Small, alternating, as rotary corrections keep a flat ski tracking straight
shaping.cue: Keep the ski running straight without steering it

finish.cue: Thigh and ski face down the run

initiation.cue: Lifted ski parallel to the stance ski

shaping.moment: Small, against the resting tip's drag
shaping.cue: Lifted ski parallel, tips level

finish.cue: Set it down parallel

initiation.action: Tilts forward a little with the hip hinge as the stance leg settles; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Hinge at the hips as you settle

shaping.action: Hinge held, moving with the thighs; tilting further than balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Comes up a little with the hips as the legs lengthen
finish.cue: Rise with the legs

initiation.action: The lifted side rises to level or a touch above as that foot unweights, hiked by the stance hip's abductors
initiation.cue: Lifted-side hip up

shaping.action: Held level or a touch up on the lifted side, with no support from the lifted ski
shaping.cue: Don't let the lifted-side hip drop

finish.action: Lowers to level as the other ski takes weight
finish.cue: Level hips over both feet

initiation.cue: Belt buckle down the run

shaping.cue: Belt buckle down the run

finish.cue: Belt buckle down the run

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, quiet but not rigid, so the trunk can ride the ripples
shaping.moment: Extension, small, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Quiet core, not braced stiff

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.cue: Move the whole body over the stance foot; don't lean the trunk over the hip

shaping.moment: Small, alternating
shaping.cue: Trunk upright over the stance foot

finish.cue: Trunk upright

initiation.cue: Upper body faces down the run

shaping.cue: Upper body faces down the run

finish.cue: Upper body faces down the run

initiation.action: Chest a little forward, about 15-25° from vertical (our inference), with the hip hinge
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held, not rounded
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the ski comes down

initiation.cue: Shoulders level

shaping.cue: Shoulders level

finish.cue: Shoulders level

initiation.cue: Chest faces down the run

shaping.cue: Chest faces down the run

finish.cue: Chest faces down the run

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arms held forward, hands in view
initiation.cue: Elbows ahead of the body

shaping.action: Arms held forward; no pole touch
shaping.cue: Elbows ahead of the body

finish.action: Arms held forward
finish.cue: Hands forward as the ski comes down

initiation.action: Arms out from the sides, hands wide, which raises the upper body's inertia and slows a sideways topple
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide, making small balance corrections
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75° and held
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip, pole tips trailing clear of the snow
initiation.cue: Hold the poles lightly

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up, eyes ahead down the run
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead, not on the ski

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.cue: Level head; don't tip it to balance

shaping.cue: Level head

finish.cue: Level head

initiation.cue: Look down the run

shaping.cue: Look down the run

activations.role: Settle the stance knee as the whole weight arrives, hold it supple under body weight on one leg, and soak up the ripples
activations.basis: Body weight on one leg at a moderate knee bend is a single-leg stance or quarter-squat load, measured off snow; the vasti are measured highly active in turns, at higher loads. The load swing over ripples grows from about ±0.05 to ±0.25 body weight with speed, and the stance is a little deeper at speed; the per-setting values are our inference

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the stance leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the loaded leg in normal turns; light here by inference

activations.role: Holds the hip hinge against the forward pitch that snow friction gives the body, and helps hold the pelvis over the stance hip
activations.basis: Measured in single-leg stance and squat exercises; the hip extension moment here is small because the hinge is shallow. Rises a step at dynamic with the deeper, more absorbing stance; our inference

activations.role: Holds up the lifted side of the pelvis, pelvis on femur, and makes the small side-to-side corrections that keep the CoM over a flat ski
activations.basis: Single-leg stance and the hip hitch rank top for gluteus medius in off-snow EMG; the job here is the same action. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps hold the pelvis level over the stance hip
activations.basis: Inferred from hip-hike exercise EMG; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contract with the abductors so the stance hip is stiff side to side, and make small rotary corrections
activations.basis: Mechanics of single-leg balance; adductors are measured highly active in turns, at far higher loads

activations.role: Shares the small hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee and checks the forward pitch of the trunk
activations.basis: Measured in a simulated edged single-leg stance at 12-35 % of maximum, rising on wider skis; here the ski is flat and the load lower

activations.role: Resist the stance knee caving in or twisting
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged single-leg stance; lower with a flat ski by inference

activations.role: Steady the femoral head and make the small rotary corrections that keep the flat ski running straight
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the shin onto the tongue as the weight arrives, then keeps it there and answers every roll toward the big-toe edge
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, where it holds the shin forward; here it also inverts against a ski that tips onto its big-toe edge, a continuous balance job that changes little with intensity

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Answer every roll toward the little-toe edge so the ski stays flat; co-contract with the inverters
activations.basis: Peroneus longus is measured highly active in turns and in balancing; on one flat ski the corrections never stop. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Holds the arch up and co-contracts with the peroneals to keep the ski flat
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin moves to the tongue, then holds the small plantarflexion moment that keeps the reaction just ahead of the CoM, shared with the boot shaft
activations.basis: The net ankle moment under a loaded, flexed ankle is plantarflexion shared with the boot in a modelled turn; here it is small, set by snow friction

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with gluteus maximus and the abdominals to steady the pelvis on the stance hip
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow

activations.role: Holds the thigh up while the knee lifts the tail, for the whole glide
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. Holding up the leg, boot and ski, about 16 kg, is a moderate hip-flexor effort even with the tip resting, and it lasts the whole run

activations.role: Works as a hip flexor on the lifted leg, not as a knee extensor
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns; changes little with intensity

activations.role: Let go as the leg unloads; take the load again at set-down
activations.basis: Measured low on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns; idle with no load

activations.role: Bends the knee to raise the tail, then holds it; its short head is a pure knee bender
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics. With the tip resting, holding the lower leg and tail up is light

activations.role: Help bend the knee and hold the tail up
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Bends the knee and keeps the lifted leg at hip width
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Flexes the hip and the knee together to hold the leg up
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps hold the thigh up
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Keep the lifted thigh at hip width; pectineus also helps lift it
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the free thigh from falling inward toward the stance leg
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns; its role here is mechanics

activations.role: Keep the lifted ski parallel against the drag on the resting tip
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shin on the tongue and the lifted ski level side to side; light, because the resting tip balances the ski
activations.basis: Modelled on the inside leg in normal turns; low here by mechanics

activations.role: Pair with tibialis anterior so the lifted ski stays flat, not tilted onto its little-toe edge
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps hike the lifted side of the pelvis, as in a hip hitch, and keeps the low back from bending sideways
activations.basis: Recorded off snow in hip-hike and pelvic-drop exercises; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts with the other side to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Keep the trunk quiet and square against small twists and sideways tips
activations.basis: Obliques are measured in normal turns, where they hold a counter; here only light stabilising is needed

activations.role: Pair with the internal obliques to keep the trunk quiet
activations.basis: External obliques are measured in normal turns, lowest in the wedge; light here by inference

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the slightly forward trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns at higher loads; here the fold is shallow and the load about body weight. Rises a step at dynamic with the deeper stance and the larger swing over ripples; our inference

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in skiing

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes steady down the run
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arms forward
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulders with the arms forward and wide, making small balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level

activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow
