structures.mechanism: Loaded if the skier drifts back on the one ski and is thrown onto the tail, the boot and the quadriceps pushing the shin forward; the backward-fall mechanism, at low speed here
Our inference; if the flat ski rolls onto its big-toe edge and catches, it twists the stance knee inward
Loaded if the lifted ski is set down wide and angled, catches and is forced into a wedge, twisting the knee inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries

tic-tac-turn.name: Short turn with a stepped edge change, each ski lifted and set on its new edge in turn

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the lifted foot is drawn back under the body, then the shin presses into the tongue as the ski is set down on its new edge, so the forebody grips first
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up as you lift; land with the shin on the tongue

shaping.action: Held flexed against the rising load to the fall line, then opens a little as the foot starts forward; a little more flexed the faster the tempo
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward and pressure moves toward the heel, still flexed past upright, ready to become the next stance foot
finish.cue: Let the feet come forward as the turn ends, not the hips back

initiation.action: Closed under load while this leg stands alone during the tic, then dorsiflexes again as the foot is lifted and drawn back for the tac, and is set down with the shin on the tongue
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, the lifted one too

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, the inside foot a little ahead because the inside leg is more flexed
shaping.moment: Small plantarflexion; the inside tibialis anterior rises after the fall line in a modelled carved turn
shaping.cue: Keep the inside shin forward too

finish.action: Held closed while the outside foot comes forward; this foot will be the next lifted (tic) foot
finish.cue: Keep the inside shin on the tongue

initiation.action: In the air the foot everts in the boot so the ski meets the snow already on its new big-toe edge, set a little away from the CoM; the edge grips at the placement
initiation.cue: Put the ski down on its big-toe edge, a little out from under you

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building with the edge angle to its most in late shaping, below the fall line, then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Keep tipping onto the big-toe edge past the fall line

finish.action: Holds, then releases toward flat through the finish; this ski is lifted next and changes edge in the air
finish.cue: Let the edge go as the turn ends

initiation.action: Lets go of the old big-toe edge as this foot is lifted, then inverts in the air so the ski is set down on its new little-toe edge, out from under the CoM rather than beneath it
initiation.cue: Roll the lifted foot to its little-toe edge before it lands

shaping.action: Inversion held, the edge building with the outside ski's
shaping.cue: Keep both skis tipped the same way

finish.action: Held, then rolls toward flat as the edges release; this ski becomes the next stance ski through the tic
finish.cue: Flatten both skis together

initiation.action: Arch braced as the foot lands and takes the whole load for a moment
initiation.cue: Land on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball together

shaping.action: Arch held up under the rising load
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing

finish.action: Arch held as pressure moves back
finish.cue: Spread the pressure as it moves to the heel

initiation.action: Arch braced while this foot carries the whole load during the tic, then quiet in the air
initiation.cue: Stand on the whole foot before you lift it

shaping.cue: A quiet foot on the little-toe edge

finish.action: Arch braced again as this foot takes more load, ready to carry the next tic
finish.cue: Feel the whole foot before the next lift

initiation.action: Flexes a little to lift the ski, then extends to stretch it down onto the snow and takes the load as the inside ski lifts; the leg lengthens from its deepest bend in the switch
initiation.moment: Extension once the ski is down; about 1-1.1 W gentle, 1.2-1.4 W moderate, 1.5-2 W dynamic at the placement (our inference)
initiation.cue: Lift, then reach the ski down and stand on it

shaping.action: Held near its longest, quasi-isometric, while the load builds with the inside ski helping; deeper the faster the tempo, about 55° gentle, 60° moderate, 65° dynamic (our inference)
shaping.moment: Extension, near its peak
shaping.cue: Stay long and strong on the outside leg

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line and eases, into the switch, about 70° gentle, 75° moderate, 80° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control to finish, ready to step

initiation.action: Holds the whole load at its old-turn bend while the tic ski is in the air, then flexes to lift the tac ski once the outside ski holds, and lengthens a little to set it down, ending shorter than the outside leg
initiation.moment: Extension while it stands alone; flexion (light) while lifted
initiation.cue: Stand, then lift the inside heel and set the ski down beside, not under, you

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside knee while it carries its smaller share; the shorter inside leg lets the legs tip in together
shaping.moment: Extension, similar to the outside knee because it is more flexed
shaping.cue: Short inside leg, still standing on it a little

finish.action: Flexes further with the outside leg as both absorb; it will be the stance leg through the next tic
finish.cue: Both legs flex together to finish

initiation.cue: Land with the knee pointing where the ski points

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Set the ski down straight, not twisted

shaping.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

finish.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

initiation.moment: Resisting the inward collapse a wide landing invites
initiation.cue: Land with the knee over the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot

initiation.cue: Set the ski down without the knee caving in

shaping.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

finish.cue: Inside knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Flexes a little to lift the thigh, then opens from the switch's deep fold as the leg is stretched down and takes the load
initiation.cue: Lift, reach, then rise a little onto the new edge

shaping.action: Held at its most open, folded forward at the hip, about 10° less than the knee (our inference)
shaping.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared by gluteus maximus, the hamstrings and adductor magnus
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the late load, into the switch
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: Held under load during the tic, then flexes to lift the thigh for the tac, and stays more flexed than the outside hip as the ski is set down; the shortening comes mostly from the hip
initiation.cue: Draw the inside thigh up, then set the ski down short

shaping.action: Held more flexed than the outside hip while loaded; the inside foot leads a little as a result
shaping.moment: Extension, similar to the outside hip because it is more flexed
shaping.cue: Inside hip folded, inside foot a little ahead

finish.action: Folds further with the outside hip as both absorb
finish.cue: Fold both hips to finish

initiation.action: The free thigh moves out to place the ski a little wide of the CoM; once the ski is down and the inside foot lifts, the outside abductors hold up the unsupported inside half of the pelvis, pelvis on femur
initiation.cue: Step the ski out a little, then stand tall over the outside hip

shaping.action: Hip angulation builds with the edge to its most in late shaping, then held, now with the inside ski sharing the support
shaping.moment: Abduction, varying; both abductors and adductors work
shaping.cue: Stay strong over the outside hip as the edge builds

finish.action: Holds under the late load, then releases as the legs come upright
finish.cue: Let the hips level as the turn ends

initiation.action: As the lone stance leg during the tic its abductors hold the other half of the pelvis up; then the free thigh is placed at hip width toward the turn's centre, out from under the CoM
initiation.cue: Stand tall on the inside leg, then set the inside ski down at hip width, not under you

shaping.action: Held a little adducted relative to the pelvis as the legs tilt in more than the trunk
shaping.moment: Adduction, held by adductor longus
shaping.cue: Keep the inside knee tipped in with the outside one

finish.action: Held, then back toward neutral as the edges release
finish.cue: Hip-width skis as the edges go flat

initiation.action: The free thigh turns inward a little so the ski lands pointing slightly into the new turn; the rotation is passive, set by the edge, not a twist of the ski
initiation.cue: Place the ski on its edge and let it point the way

shaping.action: Held turned in as the legs turn under a downhill-facing pelvis
shaping.moment: Small; internal (steering) in a brushed turn, external (braking) if carved, extrapolated from a modelled carved GS turn
shaping.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

finish.action: Turned further in as the skis come across under the downhill-facing pelvis, then unwinds with the release
finish.cue: Legs turn, chest stays downhill

initiation.action: The lifted thigh turns outward so the tac ski lands parallel to the outside ski
initiation.cue: Set the inside ski down parallel

shaping.action: Held turned out against an internal rotation moment
shaping.moment: Internal, about 0.23 Nm/kg at most in a modelled carved turn, so the internal rotators hold the femur
shaping.cue: Keep the skis parallel as they turn

finish.action: Held turned out as the skis come across, then unwinds with the release
finish.cue: Keep the skis parallel to the end

initiation.action: Comes up from the switch's deep hip hinge as the legs lengthen onto the new edges; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise a little with the legs; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held over the long legs, never standing tall; tilting further than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the legs flex into the switch
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the legs flex

initiation.action: Rocks side to side with each step; during the tic the outside half is held up by the inside (stance) hip's abductors, during the tac the inside half by the outside hip's, so it never drops toward the lifted foot
initiation.cue: Don't let the hip drop on the side of the lifted foot

shaping.action: Inside half held up as the edges build, with the inside ski sharing the support
shaping.cue: Inside hip up as the edge builds

finish.action: Lowers toward level as the edges release
finish.cue: Level the hips for the next step

initiation.action: Faces down the hill while the new skis are placed on edge; the separation from the old turn unwinds as the legs come under the body
initiation.cue: Belt buckle down the hill

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill as the legs turn under it, building counter toward the outside of the turn
shaping.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

finish.action: Counter at its most as the skis come across under a pelvis still facing down the hill
finish.cue: Skis across, pelvis down the hill

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the steps; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under load, never arched or slumped
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, while the hips fold
finish.cue: Fold at the hips, not the low back

initiation.action: Bends a little toward each stance foot in turn, then toward the outside ski once it holds; the lateral muscles on the lengthening side control it
initiation.cue: Keep the upper body over the stance foot, not swaying

shaping.action: Bend toward the outside ski builds with the edge, then held, keeping the trunk over the outside ski rather than banking
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight as the edges release
finish.cue: Straighten up as the turn ends

initiation.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-30° from vertical, more as the tempo rises; it rises a little with the hips as the legs lengthen
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held; sitting up here throws the next step back
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Shoulders kept level with the slope over each stance foot; no sway into the step
initiation.cue: Quiet shoulders while the feet step

shaping.action: Tips toward the outside ski a little more than the pelvis, building with the edge, then held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Holds, then returns toward straight
finish.cue: Let the shoulders come level

initiation.action: Faces down the hill with the pelvis while the skis are placed; the pole plant steadies it
initiation.cue: Chest down the hill, plant and step

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the legs turn

finish.action: Held facing down the hill as the skis come across, a little more countered than the pelvis
finish.cue: Chest stays down the hill

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arm held forward, hand in view, balancing the step
initiation.cue: Outside hand forward

shaping.action: Arm held forward, ready
shaping.cue: Keep the outside hand ready

finish.action: Swings forward and down the hill to ready the next plant
finish.cue: Swing the next pole early

initiation.action: The pole is planted down the hill just before the tic and the arm presses on it for a moment of support and timing, then the hand comes forward past it
initiation.cue: Plant, then step

shaping.action: Hand held forward, leading
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward, not dropped

finish.action: Hand held forward
finish.cue: Keep the inside hand up

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides for balance through the steps
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75°; the planting arm braces the elbow as it presses on the pole
initiation.cue: Firm arm on the plant

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Grip firms for the plant; the planting wrist sets the tip down the hill
initiation.cue: Plant with the wrist and forearm

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head held up with the eyes ahead down the hill, not on the feet
initiation.cue: Eyes ahead, not on your skis

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level through the steps
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Head faces down the hill with the chest
initiation.cue: Look down the hill

shaping.action: Held facing down the hill
shaping.cue: Look down the hill

finish.action: Eyes move to the next turn's spot
finish.cue: Look to the next plant

activations.role: Stretches the leg down onto the new edge and takes the whole load while the inside ski is lifted, holds it through shaping, then lets it flex under the late load
activations.basis: Measured as the main outside-leg muscle in normal turns. At initiation this leg carries the whole load for a moment, about body weight in a gentle step and up to 1.5-2 times it when the dynamic switch is airborne and caught on this ski first (Lind & Sanders unweighting relations); shaping and finish follow the arc load of 1.1-1.3 times body weight shared with the inside ski. Per-setting values are our inference

activations.role: Helps lift the thigh for the tic, then works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the loaded leg
activations.basis: Measured as a knee extensor on the outside leg and a hip flexor on an unloading leg in normal turns; here it does both in turn. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Opens the hip as the leg is stretched onto the edge and takes the load, holds the fold, then lets it close under the late load
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn, shared with the hamstrings and adductor magnus. Scaled like the vasti with the placement and arc loads; the per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Places the free thigh out and then holds up the unsupported inside half of the pelvis while the inside ski is in the air; shares the hold with the inside ski afterwards
activations.basis: Single-leg stance and the hip hitch rank highest for gluteus medius and minimus off snow; measured on both legs in normal turns. The single-leg moment is short but repeated every turn, and the landing load rises with tempo; with both skis on the snow in shaping it is a normal-turn hold

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and turns the flexed thigh inward as the ski is placed
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data and moment arms; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps place the thigh out and turned in, and helps hold the pelvis
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Brace the leg against the abductors at the landing, then turn the bent thigh inward as the skis come across under a downhill-facing pelvis
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the rotating role of the bent leg is mechanics, larger in short turns where the legs turn under the body

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment with gluteus maximus and the hamstrings
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Bends the knee to lift the tic ski, then co-contracts with the quadriceps at the landing and through the turn, sharing the hip extension moment
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns and a simulated edged stance; a landing with the trunk forward of the knee keeps it working. Scaled with the load by inference

activations.role: Resist the knee caving in and twisting outward at the landing and under the edged load
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns. Higher at a dynamic landing by inference

activations.role: Steady the femoral head at the landing and brake the thigh's inward turn as the skis come across
activations.basis: The rotation moment is small and its sign depends on how much the ski carves; model of a carved GS turn only

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Lifts the thigh for the tic, then co-contracts to steady the pelvis on the loaded hip
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. The lift is short and the leg light, so the effort is low

activations.role: Pulls the lifted foot back and up so the shin lands on the tongue; once the turn loads, only co-contracts
activations.basis: Measured as highly active in normal turns; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The modelled shaping moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction. Higher with a quicker tempo by inference

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin lands on the tongue, holds the flexed ankle with the boot shaft, then opens it to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving sit partly in the muscles and partly in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Helps bend the knee for the lift, then adds a little ankle stiffness
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the foot onto the new big-toe edge in the air and hold it at the landing, then build the edge into late shaping and let it go
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control. The landing on one edge is a balance effort that changes little with intensity; the shaping edge grows with speed and pitch

activations.role: Braces the arch at the landing and co-contracts with the peroneals for balance on the edge
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of landing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the landing pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the whole load on the old edge while the tic ski is in the air, then a smaller share on the shortened inside leg
activations.basis: Inside vastus lateralis measured about half the outside in normal turns; the single-leg stance during the tic briefly carries the whole load, more the quicker the tempo. Per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Lifts the thigh for the tac and keeps the inside leg short, a hip-flexor role
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the inside leg in normal turns, higher in flexion-led transitions; the lift is mechanics

activations.role: Lifts the thigh off the old edge for the tac and holds the inside hip folded
activations.basis: Inference; no study has measured iliopsoas on snow. Lifting leg, boot and ski quickly is a moderate hip-flexor effort; in shaping the inside leg is loaded, so only a hold

activations.role: Bends the knee to lift the tac ski; its short head is a pure knee bender. Then co-contracts on the loaded inside leg
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the lift is mechanics

activations.role: Help lift the ski, then guard the knee against caving in as the ski is set down wide
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns

activations.role: Helps bend the knee for the lift and steadies the knee's inner side at the set-down
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Flexes the hip, turns the thigh out and bends the knee together as the tac ski is lifted and set down parallel
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps bend the knee for the lift, then adds a little ankle stiffness
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the hip under the whole load during the tic and turns the lifted thigh out; then shares the inside leg's extension moment
activations.basis: The inside hip carries an extension moment similar to the outside in a modelled turn because it is more flexed; the single-leg moment adds to it briefly

activations.role: Holds up the other half of the pelvis while this leg stands alone during the tic, then places the free thigh at hip width
activations.basis: Single-leg stance ranks highest for gluteus medius off snow, and inside gluteus medius is active in normal turns; the moment is short but repeated each turn, and loaded harder at a quicker tempo

activations.role: Shares the single-leg pelvic hold with gluteus medius
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the inside thigh tipped in with the outside one once the ski is down
activations.basis: Adductor longus is the main inside-hip adductor in a modelled carved turn

activations.role: Turn the lifted thigh out so the tac ski lands parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. With the hip flexed their external rotation moment arm shrinks, so gluteus maximus and sartorius share the work

activations.role: Draws the lifted foot back with the shin on the tongue and tips the ski onto its little-toe edge
activations.basis: The second most active inside muscle in a modelled carved turn, rising after the fall line

activations.role: Inverts the lifted foot so the ski lands on its little-toe edge, holds it, then lets it flatten
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the old big-toe edge while this foot stands alone, then let it go as the foot lifts; co-contract afterwards
activations.basis: Edge-control role measured on the outside leg; inside role is mechanics

activations.role: Holds the closed ankle with the boot under the stance load during the tic and on the loaded inside leg
activations.basis: Inside ankle moment modelled about half the outside's

activations.role: Brace the arch during the single-leg moment and again before the next tic
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend toward the outside ski, then straightens it at the finish
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The bend grows with the edge angle

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to keep the low back steady as the pelvis rocks with each step
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Holds the trunk facing down the hill against the legs' turning, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; the counter is larger in short turns, where the legs turn under a downhill-facing trunk

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the trunk down the hill
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's bend toward the outside ski, then straighten it
activations.basis: Mechanics, a light role

activations.role: Steadies the trunk against the sway of each step by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the landing is not on the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk, low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, through each step and landing; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the low back carries a large combined load. Rises at the dynamic tempo with the landing and turn loads

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist while the legs turn under it
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk for each landing without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes down the hill through the steps
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arm forward, then swings the next pole early
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Swings the pole for the plant, then brings the hand forward past it and keeps it up
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Drives the pole tip into the snow and presses on it for a moment of support at the step
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow. A plant that supports the body (slow speed, steeper pitch) loads it more than a touch

activations.role: Works with latissimus dorsi in the plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Braces the elbow against the pole as the body leans on the plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level through the steps
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms forward and through the plant
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Grip the poles and set the planting tip
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the tic ski is landed with the trunk behind the knee, on the tail with the knee near straight, so the boot cuff and a hard quadriceps pull drive the shin forward; the back-weighted landing seen in racing injuries, likelier at the dynamic, airborne tempo
Loaded if the tac ski is set down wide, tip out, on its big-toe edge instead of its little-toe edge, so it catches in a wedge and twists the knee inward; the dynamic snowplow seen in racing injuries
Our inference from the same wide catch, which the sources describe without naming this ligament; the knee caving in opens its inner side
Pulled hard by the quadriceps at each landing and through the absorbing finish at a deep knee bend, many times a run, more so at the dynamic tempo
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under repeated landing and turn loads

wedge-turn.name: Linked turns in a gliding wedge, steered by both legs

initiation.action: Dorsiflexes as the CoM moves forward and toward the new outside ski; the shin presses into the tongue
initiation.cue: Shins forward into both tongues, toes up a little

shaping.action: Held flexed with the shin on the tongue while this ski carries most of the weight; a little more flexed the deeper the stance
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the turn loads

finish.action: Held, opening only a little as the pressure moves from the ball toward the middle of the foot; still flexed past upright
finish.cue: Stay over the middle of the foot; don't sit back as the turn slows you

initiation.action: Dorsiflexed with the outside ankle, the shin kept on the tongue as the ski lightens
initiation.cue: Both shins forward, not just the outside one

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, under a lighter load
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Both shins on the tongues

finish.action: Held flexed as this ski readies to take the weight of the next turn
finish.cue: Keep the inside shin forward too

initiation.action: Everts inside the boot so the ski's big-toe edge, already engaged in the wedge, edges a little more; the edge is never released, only built
initiation.moment: Eversion
initiation.cue: Roll a little more onto the big toe of the outside foot

shaping.action: Eversion keeps building to the turn's highest edge angle around and just below the fall line, about 10-20° from gentle to dynamic (our inference), then holds against the snow force that would flatten the ski
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Most edge on the outside ski as you pass the fall line

finish.action: Holds, then eases toward the wedge's resting edge as the weight returns to centre; it stays on the big-toe edge and becomes the flatter inside ski of the next turn
finish.cue: Ease the outside edge as the turn ends; don't let it go flat

initiation.action: Eversion eases so this ski, the old outside ski, flattens toward a low edge on its big-toe edge; this is the wedge's release, with no edge change
initiation.moment: Eversion, falling
initiation.cue: Let the new inside ski go flatter so it can turn

shaping.action: Held flatter than the outside ski, still on its big-toe edge, about 5-10° (our inference), with small corrections so it steers and brushes rather than grips
shaping.moment: Eversion, small
shaping.cue: Inside ski flatter, still in the wedge

finish.action: Held at its low edge, ready to edge more as it becomes the next outside ski
finish.cue: Keep the inside ski quiet and flat-ish

initiation.action: Arch held up as the foot takes more of the weight
initiation.cue: Stand on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball

shaping.action: Arch held up under the edged load along the inside of the foot
shaping.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing as you roll onto the big toe

finish.action: Arch held as the weight starts back toward centre
finish.cue: Spread the pressure over the whole foot

initiation.action: Arch held under a lighter load as weight leaves this foot
initiation.cue: Keep some weight on the inside foot too

shaping.action: Arch held under a light load
shaping.cue: A quiet inside foot

finish.action: Arch held as the foot readies to take the weight
finish.cue: Feel the whole inside foot

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from the even-weighted stance as weight moves onto this leg, never straight
initiation.cue: Grow a little tall on the new outside leg

shaping.action: Held flexed, quasi-isometric, while this leg takes most of the weight; about 35-45° gentle, 40-50° moderate, 45-55° dynamic (our inference)
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Steady on the outside leg; knees bent, not locked

finish.action: Flexes a little, absorbing the load that peaks below the fall line, as the turn slows the skier
finish.cue: Soften the outside leg as the turn finishes

initiation.action: Flexes a little as weight leaves it, so the inside leg becomes the shorter one and the pelvis can stay level over the outside ski
initiation.moment: Extension
initiation.cue: Soften the new inside leg

shaping.action: Held a little more flexed than the outside knee, still loaded
shaping.moment: Extension, smaller than outside
shaping.cue: Inside knee a little more bent

finish.action: Held flexed while the ski, now uphill of the outside ski, sits higher on the slope; it lengthens again only as it becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Keep the inside leg short until the next turn

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the outward twist the skidding ski puts on the shin
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist of the brushing ski
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.cue: Knee over the foot

shaping.moment: Small; the snow force runs from the edge toward the body's centre close to the knee, but a caught edge twists the knee in
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Knee over the foot, not caving in

initiation.cue: Inside knee over its foot

shaping.moment: Small, unless the inside ski catches its edge
shaping.cue: Inside knee over its foot, not caving in

finish.cue: Inside knee over its foot

initiation.action: Opens a little with the knee as this leg lengthens under the shifting weight
initiation.cue: Rise a little over the outside ski

shaping.action: Held flexed, about 35-50° (our inference), the trunk hinged forward at the hip
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist

finish.action: Folds a little more with the knee, absorbing the late load
finish.cue: Soften at the hips and knees together

initiation.action: Folds a little with the knee as weight leaves this leg
initiation.moment: Extension
initiation.cue: Soften the new inside leg at hip and knee

shaping.action: Held a little more flexed than the outside hip
shaping.moment: Extension
shaping.cue: Inside leg a little shorter

finish.action: Held flexed until it becomes the next outside leg
finish.cue: Keep the inside leg short

initiation.action: Held abducted, which keeps the tail out in the wedge, while the pelvis moves over this leg; abductors and adductors co-contract to keep the wedge width
initiation.moment: Small and changing sign with the wedge width; abductors and adductors co-contract
initiation.cue: Keep the wedge the same size as you move over the outside ski

shaping.action: Held abducted under most of the weight; the outside hip also holds the pelvis level over the femur so the inside half does not drop, helped by the still-loaded inside foot
shaping.moment: Abduction and adduction co-contraction
shaping.cue: Stand over the outside ski with level hips

finish.action: Held, then shares the pelvis again with the inside leg as the weight returns to centre
finish.cue: Keep the wedge width steady

initiation.action: Held abducted; the wedge width does not change as weight leaves this leg
initiation.cue: Keep the inside ski in the wedge

shaping.action: Held abducted, the adductors and abductors co-contracting so the inside ski neither drifts wide nor closes
shaping.cue: Same wedge, tips apart

finish.action: Held abducted
finish.cue: Same wedge width throughout

initiation.action: Turns inward in the hip socket, pivoting the ski about the foot to steer it into the new turn; the tail is not pushed out
initiation.moment: Internal rotation, against the snow's resistance to the skidding ski
initiation.cue: Turn the outside thigh and foot toward the turn

shaping.action: Keeps turning inward, spread evenly through the turn so the track is a C, not a V
shaping.moment: Internal rotation
shaping.cue: Keep steering the outside ski round

finish.action: Held, then eases back to the wedge's resting inward rotation as the next turn starts
finish.cue: Let the outside leg ease back to the wedge

initiation.action: Turns outward a little in the hip socket, steering the flatter inside ski toward the turn while it stays in the wedge
initiation.cue: Turn the inside foot the same way, a little

shaping.action: Held, still internally rotated relative to the pelvis to keep the tips together
shaping.moment: Internal rotation, holding the wedge
shaping.cue: Tips stay closer than tails

finish.action: Held; it will turn inward as the next outside leg
finish.cue: Keep the wedge shape

initiation.action: Hinged forward with the hips in an athletic stance; the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Hinge at the hips, chest over the knees

shaping.action: Hinge held, never standing tall or sitting back; tilting further forward than balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Hinge held as the legs flex a little
finish.cue: Don't sit back as the turn slows you

initiation.action: Kept level as the pelvis moves sideways toward the new outside ski, the inside half not allowed to drop
initiation.cue: Inside hip up, level hips

shaping.action: Held level relative to the balance axis, a little up on the inside, while the inside leg is shorter; the inside foot still supports it, so the hold is light
shaping.cue: Don't sag onto the inside ski

finish.action: Held level as the weight returns to centre
finish.cue: Level hips into the next turn

initiation.action: Quiet, facing between the skis, while both thighs turn under it
initiation.cue: Let the legs turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Faces along the turn's path, square to slightly countered toward the outside ski; it follows the turn slowly rather than leading it
shaping.cue: Belt buckle along the path, not ahead of it

finish.action: Held quiet while the legs ease back toward the even wedge
finish.cue: Quiet pelvis, legs do the turning

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened under a load close to body weight
shaping.moment: Extension, small
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened, never slumped as the skier slows
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

initiation.action: Bends a little toward the new outside ski as the upper body lines up over it; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Upper body a little over the outside ski

shaping.action: Small bend held, about 5° (biomechanics.md 2.0), so the weight stays over the outside ski without the shoulders tipping into the turn
shaping.cue: Shoulders level, weight over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight as the weight comes back to centre
finish.cue: Re-centre between the skis

initiation.cue: The legs turn in the hips; the low back stays untwisted

shaping.cue: The low back stays untwisted

finish.cue: The low back stays untwisted

initiation.action: Chest forward about 20° from vertical with the hip hinge, not rounded
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn slows you

initiation.action: Tips a little toward the outside ski with the lumbar bend; the inside obliques lengthen
initiation.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

shaping.action: Small bend held
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Returns toward straight
finish.cue: Re-centre the upper body

initiation.action: Quiet with the pelvis while the legs turn under
initiation.cue: Quiet upper body

shaping.action: Faces along the path with the pelvis, not turned into the turn ahead of the skis
shaping.cue: Don't steer with the shoulders

finish.action: Held quiet
finish.cue: Quiet upper body

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arms held forward, hands in view; no pole touch in this drill
initiation.cue: Hands forward like holding a tray

shaping.action: Arms held forward; the inside hand does not drop
shaping.cue: Keep the inside hand up

finish.action: Arms held forward
finish.cue: Hands forward

initiation.action: Arms a little out from the sides for balance
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75° and held
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent and held
shaping.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

finish.action: Bent and held
finish.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

initiation.action: Light grip on the poles, tips trailing
initiation.cue: Hold the poles lightly

shaping.action: Light grip held
shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

finish.action: Light grip held
finish.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.action: Head up, eyes ahead along the path, not down at the ski tips
initiation.cue: Look where you are going

shaping.action: Head held steady
shaping.cue: A steady head

finish.action: Head held steady
finish.cue: A steady head

initiation.action: Head kept level
initiation.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Level head

finish.action: Head kept level
finish.cue: Level head

initiation.action: Eyes turn toward the new turn's path a little ahead of the skis
initiation.cue: Look into the next turn

shaping.action: Eyes held on the path
shaping.cue: Look where you are going

finish.action: Eyes move ahead to the next turn's path
finish.cue: Look along the next turn

activations.role: Lengthen the outside knee as weight moves onto it, hold it flexed under most of the weight, then let it soften as the turn finishes
activations.basis: Measured above 50 % MVC in wedge turns, though lower than in parallel turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract only); the plough also had the highest quadriceps-to-hamstrings ratio of the tasks measured (hermann-2023). The load is near body weight at every setting, so the per-setting rise is our inference from the outside foot's growing share and the deeper stance

activations.role: Works with the vasti as a knee extensor on the more loaded leg
activations.basis: Whole-quadriceps EMG was measured in the plough (hermann-2023); rectus femoris's share is inferred from normal turns (kroll-2010)

activations.role: Holds the folded, abducted and inward-rotated hip under most of the weight, and steadies the femur as it steers
activations.basis: Measured above 50 % MVC in wedge turns and higher there than in parallel turns, the one muscle that was (hintermeister-1997, abstract only). The abducted, internally rotated wedge hip is the reason we infer; the per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Its front fibres turn the flexed thigh inward to steer; the whole muscle keeps the leg abducted in the wedge and the pelvis level over it
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns (seifert-2023); internal rotation in hip flexion is anatomy (delp-1999). Less pelvic work than a one-legged drill because the inside foot still supports the pelvis

activations.role: Turns the flexed thigh inward with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur
activations.basis: Anatomy and moment arms in hip flexion; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps turn the thigh inward and hold the wedge
activations.basis: Exercise EMG and anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the wedge width against the abductors and help turn the bent thigh inward to steer and edge
activations.basis: Measured above 50 % MVC in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract only); the steering role of the bent leg is LeMaster's mechanics (pp 108, 124-125). Per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment and the wedge-width hold
activations.basis: Anatomy; adductors as a group were measured in the wedge (hintermeister-1997), adductor magnus alone was not

activations.role: Co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the knee
activations.basis: The two wedge studies disagree. Biceps femoris averaged above 50 % MVC in wedge turns (hintermeister-1997, abstract), yet the plough had the least hamstring co-contraction of any task in older recreational women (hermann-2023, full text). We keep it low and rising only at the dynamic setting

activations.role: Resist the shin twisting outward under the skidding ski and the knee caving in
activations.basis: Mechanics of the skidding wedge ski (lind-sanders-2004 p 98); low hamstring activity in the plough (hermann-2023)

activations.role: Steady the femoral head and brake the thigh's inward turn so steering stays progressive
activations.basis: Anatomy; their rotation moment arms shrink and some flip with hip flexion (delp-1999)

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Pulls the shin forward into the tongue as weight moves onto this foot, then co-contracts to keep it there
activations.basis: Highly active in skiing turns (cross-raschner-2023 p 14); active ankle flexion is a book technique point (LeMaster p 81, IASI p 16). Beginners taught the plough load the rearfoot (kurpiers-2024), which this guards against

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Yields as the shin presses into the tongue, shares the held ankle with the boot shaft, then opens the ankle a little as pressure moves to the middle of the foot
activations.basis: The boot shaft carries much of the ankle moment in turns (heinrich-2022); at a load near body weight the soleus share is small

activations.role: Adds a little ankle stiffness; the knee is less bent than in a carved turn, so it is not slack
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Roll the outside ski further onto its big-toe edge as the turn builds, hold it, then ease it back to the wedge's resting edge
activations.basis: Peroneus longus is highly active in turns (cross-raschner-2023 p 14); the boot shell carries most of the edging moment (lind-sanders-2004 pp 54-55). Rises a little with the higher dynamic edge angle, by inference

activations.role: Holds the arch up under the edged foot
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Let the inside knee soften as weight leaves it, then hold it flexed under its smaller share
activations.basis: The wedge's vasti measurement does not split the legs (hintermeister-1997); inside vastus lateralis runs about half the outside value in normal turns (kroll-2010). The inside leg carries more here than in a parallel turn, by inference, so it reaches 2 when dynamic

activations.role: Helps hold the shorter, flexed inside leg
activations.basis: Active on the inside leg in normal turns (kroll-2010); plough quadriceps measured as a group (hermann-2023)

activations.role: Turns the inside thigh outward a little to steer the flatter ski, and holds the flexed hip under its share of the load
activations.basis: Measured high in the wedge without a side (hintermeister-1997); the inside share is smaller, so the effort is inference

activations.role: Keeps the inside leg abducted so the ski stays in the wedge
activations.basis: Inside gluteus medius is active through steering in normal turns (seifert-2023); its wedge role is mechanics

activations.role: Holds the inside thigh's inward rotation that keeps the tips together
activations.basis: Anatomy; internal rotators in hip flexion (delp-1999)

activations.role: Helps hold the inside thigh turned in and out to the side, the wedge shape
activations.basis: Anatomy and exercise EMG; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the inside ski from drifting wide, holding the wedge width with the abductors
activations.basis: Adductors measured above 50 % MVC in the wedge, side not given (hintermeister-1997); inside adductor longus is active in normal turns (heinrich-2023)

activations.role: Turn the inside thigh outward a little to steer the flatter ski, then steady it
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Co-contracts lightly to steady the inside knee
activations.basis: Low hamstring co-contraction in the plough (hermann-2023)

activations.role: Resist the inside knee caving in or twisting if the inside ski catches
activations.basis: Mechanics of the wedge catch (jordan-sporri-taylor-2023 p 122); not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the inside shin on its tongue too
activations.basis: Inside tibialis anterior is active in a modelled carved turn (heinrich-2023); in the wedge it is mechanics

activations.role: Shares the light ankle moment with the boot shaft
activations.basis: Smaller inside ankle moment in a modelled turn (heinrich-2022)

activations.role: Let the inside ski flatten while keeping it on its big-toe edge, then hold that low edge
activations.basis: Mechanics; the inside ski of a wedge is everted, not inverted, because it sits on its big-toe edge (psia-c-wedge-turn)

activations.role: Hold the hinged trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
activations.basis: Trunk muscles were less active in the wedge than in parallel turns (hintermeister-1997); the hinge is shallow and the load near body weight

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the pelvis stays neutral and the skier stays off the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in skiing turns (hintermeister-1997)

activations.role: Keep the upper body quiet while both legs turn under it
activations.basis: External oblique was lowest in the wedge of the three turn types measured (hintermeister-1997)

activations.role: Pair with the external obliques to steady the trunk against the legs' turning
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving (heinrich-2023); in the wedge the demand is small, by inference

activations.role: Controls the low back's small bend toward the outside ski from the lengthening side, then straightens it
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the side bend is small here

activations.role: Co-contracts to steady the low back
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk without bracing it rigid
activations.basis: Anatomy; IASI asks for an active but not tense core (p 60)

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes on the path
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the arms forward
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms forward and wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles lightly
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if a wedge ski catches its edge and the tip is pulled outward, twisting the knee inward with the ski as a long lever; the inward twist of a caught wedge, and the dynamic snowplow seen in racing, more likely sitting back in a wide wedge
Our inference from the same caught edge, which the sources describe as tearing knee ligaments without naming this one; the knee caving in opens its inner side
Pulled harder when the skier sits back in a wide wedge and holds the knees deeply bent on the quadriceps

whitepass-turn.name: Turn started on the inside ski's little-toe edge, finished on the outside ski alone

initiation.action: Held up with the ski about level to the snow, the shin kept on the tongue so the boot carries the ski's weight and the forebody does not drop
initiation.moment: Dorsiflexion, holding the lifted ski's forebody up
initiation.cue: Shin on the tongue, lifted ski level

shaping.action: The toes are pulled up and the foot drawn back as the ski is set down, so the forebody engages first; then held flexed against the load coming onto it
shaping.moment: Plantarflexion once the ski carries load, shared with the boot shaft
shaping.cue: Pull the foot back as the ski touches down

finish.action: Opens progressively as the foot slides forward under the body, still flexed past upright; pressure moves toward the heel and stays there into the transition
finish.cue: Let the foot slide ahead as the turn ends, shin still on the tongue

initiation.action: Closes from the transition, the foot drawn back so the one ski's forebody engages on its little-toe edge; held flexed as the load builds
initiation.moment: Plantarflexion as the load comes on, shared with the boot shaft
initiation.cue: Pull the toes up and the foot back on the stance ski

shaping.action: Held flexed, shin on the tongue, while the outside ski takes over the load
shaping.cue: Keep the shin on the tongue as the other ski lands

finish.action: Stays closed as the ski is lifted, the shin carrying the ski level through the boot
finish.moment: Dorsiflexion, holding the lifted ski's forebody up
finish.cue: Shin on the tongue as the ski comes up

initiation.action: In the air, the foot everts so the lifted ski tips onto its big-toe edge in step with the stance ski's tilt
initiation.cue: Tip the lifted ski the same way as the stance ski

shaping.action: Set down already on its big-toe edge near the body's tilt; eversion keeps building as the ski takes the load, to its most in late shaping
shaping.moment: Eversion
shaping.cue: Land on the big-toe edge and keep rolling onto it

finish.action: Held near its peak on one edge with constant small corrections, then released toward flat at the end of the finish, so the same ski can roll onto its other edge in the transition
finish.cue: Hold the edge, then let it go on the same ski

initiation.action: The stance foot inverts inside the boot so the one ski rolls from flat onto its little-toe edge, the edge building progressively as the body inclines into the turn
initiation.moment: Inversion, against a snow force on the lateral edge that would flatten the ski
initiation.cue: Roll the stance ski onto its little-toe edge early, from the foot

shaping.action: Edge held as the outside ski lands, then eased as that ski takes the load
shaping.cue: Keep the little-toe edge until the other ski has it

finish.action: The lifted ski stays tilted on its little-toe edge, in step with the stance ski, until it tips over in the transition
finish.cue: Keep the lifted ski tilted with the turn

initiation.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

shaping.action: Arch held up as the foot takes the load, pressure spread over heel and both balls of the foot
shaping.cue: Land on the whole foot, arch up

finish.action: Arch held up under the peak load on one ski, pressure moving to the heel
finish.cue: Keep the arch from collapsing as the load peaks

initiation.action: The foot balances the whole load on its outer border, which is not built for it; the arch and toes grip to spread the pressure toward the heel and little-toe ball
initiation.cue: Stand on the heel and the little-toe ball, toes quiet

shaping.action: Held as the load leaves the foot
shaping.cue: Keep the foot quiet as the other ski lands

finish.cue: A quiet foot in the lifted boot

initiation.action: Held bent, more than the stance knee, with the heel drawn up so the lifted ski stays level
initiation.moment: Flexion, holding the shank, boot and ski up
initiation.cue: Heel up, ski level

shaping.action: Extends to reach the snow near the fall line, then keeps lengthening against the load as the ski bends from its centre, to its longest in late shaping, about 58° gentle, 64° moderate, 70° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 56-80°)
shaping.moment: Extension once the ski carries load
shaping.cue: Extend the outside leg to put the ski down and stand on it

finish.action: Flexes, absorbing the load as it peaks below the fall line with no help from the other leg, into its deepest bend in the transition, about 66° gentle, 72° moderate, 79° dynamic (our inference)
finish.cue: Flex under control as the turn ends, still on one ski

initiation.action: Lengthens a little from its deepest bend in the transition as the body inclines, then held quasi-isometric on the one ski
initiation.moment: Extension
initiation.cue: Grow tall enough to balance on the little-toe edge

shaping.action: Yields and shortens as the outside ski lands and takes over, so the inside leg ends shorter than the outside one
shaping.moment: Extension, falling
shaping.cue: Let the inside leg shorten as you move onto the outside ski

finish.action: Flexes to lift the ski before the finish, then held bent with the heel drawn up
finish.moment: Flexion, holding the shank, boot and ski up
finish.cue: Lift the inside ski, heel toward your seat

initiation.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

shaping.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites as the ski lands
shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.moment: Resisting the twist the snow force invites
finish.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

initiation.moment: Resisting the twist the edged load invites
initiation.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

shaping.cue: Turn the thigh, not the knee

finish.cue: Lifted knee points where the ski points

initiation.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

shaping.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
shaping.cue: Land with the knee over the foot, not caving in

finish.moment: Resisting the inward collapse the edged load invites
finish.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not caving in

initiation.moment: Resisting the knee bowing outward, varus, that standing on the little-toe edge invites
initiation.cue: Knee stays over the foot, not bowing out

shaping.cue: Knee over the foot

finish.cue: Lifted knee in line with the foot

initiation.action: Held flexed, more than the stance hip, so the lifted ski rides level beside the stance boot with no tip support
initiation.moment: Flexion, holding the leg, boot and ski up
initiation.cue: Thigh up, ski level beside the other boot

shaping.action: Lowered to set the ski down, then opens as the leg lengthens under the load, to its most open in late shaping, about 50° gentle, 57° moderate, 64° dynamic (our inference; heinrich-2022 GS 50-81°)
shaping.moment: Flexion while lowering, extension once loaded
shaping.cue: Reach the outside ski to the snow and stand on it

finish.action: Folds further with the knee, absorbing the load on one leg, into the transition, about 60° gentle, 68° moderate, 76° dynamic (our inference)
finish.moment: Extension, about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn and more here with no inside support
finish.cue: Fold at the hips, not the waist, as the turn ends

initiation.action: Opens a little with the knee from the transition, then held, the hip hinge carrying the forward fold over the one ski
initiation.moment: Extension
initiation.cue: Fold at the hip over the stance ski

shaping.action: Flexes as the leg shortens and the outside ski takes over, more flexed than the outside hip
shaping.moment: Extension, falling
shaping.cue: Inside hip and knee bend as the outside ski lands

finish.action: Flexes to lift the thigh and ski before the finish, then held up through the finish
finish.moment: Flexion, holding the leg, boot and ski up
finish.cue: Lift the inside thigh, ski level

initiation.action: The lifted thigh held beside the stance leg at about hip width, neither crossing nor swinging wide; with the free leg off the snow the net moment is small
initiation.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

shaping.action: The ski is set down at hip width; as it loads, the pelvis tips over the new stance thigh so the inside half rises, the outside abductors hiking it, pelvis on femur; hip angulation builds with the edge to its most in late shaping
shaping.moment: Abduction
shaping.cue: Land at hip width and get over the outside hip

finish.action: Held under the peak load with the inside ski lifted, carrying the unsupported inside half of the pelvis, and held into the transition
finish.cue: Stay strong over the outside hip with the inside ski up

initiation.action: The stance femur tips into the turn under a pelvis kept closer to level, so the hip sits adducted while its abductors hold up the unsupported outside half of the pelvis, pelvis on femur
initiation.moment: Abduction
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted side of your hips up

shaping.action: Releases the pelvic hold as the outside ski lands and takes the load; the thigh then held adducted beside the outside leg
shaping.moment: Abduction, falling to small
shaping.cue: Hand the hips over to the outside leg

finish.action: The lifted thigh held beside the stance leg at about hip width
finish.cue: Lifted boot at hip width

initiation.action: Turns inward in the air with the stance ski so the lifted ski stays parallel and pointed along the new arc
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted ski parallel to the stance ski

shaping.action: Lands turned in under the pelvis and held as the ski carves
shaping.moment: Small and mostly external (braking) in a carved turn, extrapolated from a modelled GS turn
shaping.cue: Knee over the foot as the ski carves

finish.action: Turns further inward relative to the pelvis as the ski carves across under a quieter upper body, the turn braked by the external rotators
finish.cue: Let the ski turn under you; don't twist it

initiation.action: Starts turned in under a pelvis that still faces down the hill from the last turn, then turns outward as the carving ski comes round toward the fall line under it, the windup releasing
initiation.cue: Let the stance ski turn under a quiet pelvis

shaping.action: Held turned out as the outside ski takes over
shaping.moment: Internal, holding the femur against turning out further (modelled on the inside leg)
shaping.cue: Inside knee points where the ski points

finish.action: Held turned out so the lifted ski stays parallel; the tip must not drift onto the stance ski
finish.cue: Keep the lifted tip from crossing

initiation.action: Comes up a little from the transition's hip hinge with the stance leg, the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped
initiation.cue: Rise with the leg; the hinge stays at the hips

shaping.action: Hinge held at its most open over the lengthening outside leg, more tilted the harder the turn; tilting further than the balance needs, so the low back arches, is a fault
shaping.cue: Hinged at the hips, low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Tilts forward again with the hip hinge as the outside leg flexes into the transition
finish.cue: Fold at the hips as the leg flexes

initiation.action: Standing on the inside leg, the pelvis's outside half has no support; it is held up by the inside hip's abductors while the stance leg tips into the turn
initiation.cue: Keep the lifted side of your hips up

shaping.action: Passes through level as both skis are briefly on the snow, then the inside half rises over the outside hip as the outside ski takes the load
shaping.cue: Inside hip up as you move onto the outside ski

finish.action: Inside half held up with no support from the lifted inside ski, to the end of the finish and into the transition
finish.cue: Don't let the inside hip drop with the ski up

initiation.action: Faces down the hill from the last turn while the stance ski turns toward the fall line under it, so the angle between pelvis and ski closes
initiation.cue: Upper body faces the fall line; let the ski come round to it

shaping.action: Close to square with the skis at the fall line, then a slight counter forms as the outside ski carves on
shaping.cue: Belt buckle a little toward the outside of the turn

finish.action: Counter grows as the ski carves across under a pelvis that stays facing down the hill, ready for the next turn
finish.cue: Keep facing the fall line as the ski turns across

initiation.action: Low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and nearly constant through the turn; the fold is made at the hips
initiation.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped; fold at the hips

shaping.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under the load, never arched or slumped
shaping.moment: Extension, against the forward fold
shaping.cue: Low back slightly flattened, never arched or slumped

finish.action: Held slightly flattened from standing under the peak load on one leg, never arched or slumped; a harder turn folds more at the hips, not the low back
finish.cue: Low back slightly flattened; fold at the hips

initiation.action: The body inclines into the turn over the inside ski while the low back bends a little back toward the outside, counterbalancing over the one edge; the inside quadratus lumborum and obliques lengthen to control it
initiation.cue: Commit the hips inside; shoulders stay over the stance ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the outside ski's edge to its most in late shaping, angulation moving the pressure onto the outside ski
shaping.cue: Hips in, shoulders out, onto the outside ski

finish.action: Held through the finish on the one ski, then eases as the edge releases in the transition
finish.cue: Stay over the outside ski

initiation.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

shaping.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

finish.cue: Separation comes from the hip sockets, not the low back

initiation.action: Chest forward, about 20-33° from vertical through the turn, a little more the harder the turn; it rises a little with the hips as the stance leg lengthens
initiation.cue: Chest over the knees

shaping.action: Slight forward flexion held
shaping.cue: Chest over the knees

finish.action: Slight forward flexion held
finish.cue: Don't sit up as the turn ends

initiation.action: Tips back toward the outside a little more than the pelvis, the counterbalance that keeps the CoM over the inside ski's edge; too little and the skier falls inside, too much and the ski stands flat
initiation.cue: Counterbalance with the shoulders over the stance ski

shaping.action: Keeps building with the outside ski's edge to its most in late shaping
shaping.cue: Outside shoulder over the outside ski

finish.action: Held, then eases with the release in the transition
finish.cue: Shoulders level with the slope

initiation.action: Faces down the hill with the pelvis while the stance ski turns under them
initiation.cue: Chest to the fall line

shaping.action: Close to square at the fall line, then slight counter held against the legs' turning
shaping.cue: Quiet upper body while the skis turn

finish.action: Counter held and growing as the ski carves across, the chest still toward the fall line
finish.cue: Chest stays to the fall line

initiation.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
initiation.cue: Hands forward and in view

shaping.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
shaping.cue: Hands forward and in view

finish.action: Shoulder blades slightly forward and level
finish.cue: Hands forward and in view

initiation.action: Arms held forward, hands in view; no pole touch is needed and none is asked for
initiation.cue: Both hands forward

shaping.action: Arms held forward, the inside hand up, not dropped
shaping.cue: Inside hand up and forward

finish.action: Arms held forward
finish.cue: Hands forward

initiation.action: Hands wide for balance on one edge, raising the upper body's resistance to turning
initiation.cue: Hands wide and forward

shaping.action: Hands held wide
shaping.cue: Hands wide and forward

finish.action: Hands held wide
finish.cue: Hands wide and forward

initiation.action: Bent about 75° and held
initiation.cue: Forearms roughly parallel to the snow

shaping.action: Bent about 75° and held

finish.action: Bent about 75° and held

shaping.cue: Hold the poles lightly

initiation.cue: Eyes ahead

shaping.action: Head kept level
shaping.cue: Don't tip the head into the turn
