activations.role: Idle while the leg is held up; extend the knee to set the ski down and stand on it, then hold and absorb the whole load through the finish
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns, where activity peaks in the steering phase at a steady knee bend. Here one leg carries the whole load from late shaping, about 1.1-1.5 times body weight below the fall line by Lind & Sanders eq 4.9, at a deeper bend as the turn gets harder; the per-setting values are our inference

activations.role: Holds the lifted thigh up as a hip flexor, then works as a knee extensor once the ski is down
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg and a knee extensor on the outside leg in normal turns; this drill asks both of it in turn

activations.role: Holds the lifted leg, boot and ski level with no tip support, lowers it to the snow, then co-contracts on the stance hip
activations.basis: Inference; iliopsoas has not been measured on snow. Holding about 16 kg of leg, boot and ski level is a moderate hip-flexor effort, a little more than with a resting tip

activations.role: Opens the hip to set the ski down, then holds the folded hip under the whole load and brakes the thigh's inward turn as the ski carves
activations.basis: The hip extension moment is about 1.3 Nm/kg in a modelled carved turn with help from the inside leg; here none, so the finish is harder than a stork turn's. Per-setting values are inference

activations.role: Hikes the pelvis's inside half over the stance hip as the ski lands, then holds it up, unsupported, with the inside ski lifted
activations.basis: Measured on both legs in normal turns; the one-leg pelvic hold follows from mechanics and single-leg exercise data. Highest in the finish, where the load peaks and the inside ski is off the snow

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the head of the femur under the one-leg load
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow. Scaled as gluteus medius

activations.role: Helps hold the lifted thigh up, then the pelvis over the stance hip
activations.basis: Inferred from exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keep the lifted thigh beside the stance leg, then turn the bent thigh inward to edge the landed ski and brace against the abductors
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the edging role is mechanics of the bent leg

activations.role: Shares the hip extension moment once the leg is loaded
activations.basis: Anatomy and a modelled hip extension moment; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the lifted knee bent with the heel drawn up, then co-contracts with the quadriceps to steady the loaded knee and brake the thigh's inward turn
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity and outside-leg co-contraction are measured in normal turns; holding the shank, boot and ski up with no tip support is a moderate effort

activations.role: Help hold the lifted knee bent, then resist the loaded knee twisting outward and caving in
activations.basis: Semitendinosus at 6-15 % of maximum in a simulated edged stance; low in normal turns

activations.role: Steady the hip, then brake the thigh's inward turn as the ski carves across
activations.basis: The carved turn's outside hip rotation moment is small and external, extrapolated from a model of a GS turn

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the loaded bent knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the lifted ski level with the shin on the tongue, pulls the foot back as the ski lands so the forebody engages, then only co-contracts under the load
activations.basis: Highly active in normal turns; active ankle flexion is a book technique point. The loaded ankle's net moment is plantarflexion, so its later work is co-contraction

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Idle while the ski is up; yields as the shin presses into the tongue under the landing load, then opens the ankle to push the foot forward through the finish
activations.basis: Ankle moments modelled in carving put about 0.85 Nm/kg in the muscles and 1.16 Nm/kg in the boot shaft; with the knee bent the soleus does the ankle work. Scaled with load by inference

activations.role: Helps hold the lifted knee bent, then adds a little ankle stiffness
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Tip the lifted ski to its big-toe edge in the air, build the edge as it lands, make the constant small corrections on one edge, then let it go
activations.basis: Highly active in turns, attributed to edge control; balancing on one ski adds continuous co-contraction. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity; the boot shell carries most of the edging moment

activations.role: Holds the arch up under the landed load and co-contracts with the peroneals for balance on one edge
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Spread the pressure over the sole and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Lengthen the stance knee from the transition and hold it on the one ski, then let it shorten as the outside ski takes over; idle once the ski is lifted
activations.basis: Single-leg load at the top of the turn, about 1.0-1.1 times body weight, but on the weaker edge and through a deeper knee as the turn gets harder; measured as an outside-leg pattern in the one-legged racer's turns. Per-setting values are inference

activations.role: A knee extensor on the stance leg, then a hip flexor that lifts the ski before the finish
activations.basis: Measured as a hip flexor on the lightly loaded inside leg in normal turns

activations.role: Co-contracts on the stance hip, then lifts the thigh, boot and ski and holds them level
activations.basis: Inference; not measured on snow. The lift with no tip support is a moderate hip-flexor effort

activations.role: Holds the folded stance hip on one ski and turns the thigh out as the ski comes round, then keeps the lifted ski parallel
activations.basis: Hip extension on a single stance leg is mechanics; the share on the little-toe edge is inferred from the one-legged racer's outside-edge turns

activations.role: Holds up the unsupported outside half of the pelvis while the skier stands on the little-toe edge, then hands the hold to the outside hip and keeps the lifted thigh from falling in
activations.basis: The single-leg pelvic hold (hip hitch) ranks top for gluteus medius off snow; standing on the inside edge removes all support from the outside half. A balance-and-posture effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Shares the pelvic hold with gluteus medius and steadies the femoral head on the stance leg
activations.basis: Inferred from single-leg exercise data; not measured on snow

activations.role: Helps the pelvic hold on the stance leg, then helps hold the lifted thigh up
activations.basis: The hip hike drove TFL to about 47 % of maximum off snow; not measured on snow

activations.role: Brace the adducted stance hip against the abductors, then keep the lifted thigh beside the stance leg
activations.basis: Inside adductor longus was a main contributor in a modelled carved turn; the stance role is mechanics

activations.role: Shares the stance hip's extension moment
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls fore-aft and trunk pitch on the little-toe edge, then bends the knee to lift the ski; its short head is a pure knee bender
activations.basis: The one-legged racer's biceps femoris was much more active in the first half of his outside-edge turns, linked to forward trunk pitch, and hypertrophied; this is that edge. The lift is mechanics

activations.role: Co-contract on the stance knee, then help bend it to lift the ski
activations.basis: Inside-leg hamstring activity measured in normal turns; the stance share is inferred from the one-legged racer

activations.role: Adds ankle stiffness on the stance leg, then helps bend the knee to lift the ski
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the stance knee with the pes anserinus, then flexes the hip and knee and turns the thigh out to lift the ski
activations.basis: Hip-flexor EMG off snow

activations.role: Turn the stance thigh out as the ski comes round and steady the femoral head on one leg, then keep the lifted ski parallel
activations.basis: Anatomy; with the hip flexed their external rotation moment arm shrinks, so gluteus maximus shares the work

activations.role: Closes the stance ankle and helps invert the foot onto the little-toe edge, then keeps the lifted ski level with the shin on the tongue
activations.basis: Highly active in normal turns and the second most active inside-leg muscle in a modelled carved turn; here it also tips the ski onto the harder edge

activations.role: Pull the toes and foot up with tibialis anterior
activations.basis: Anatomy and coaching cue; not measured on snow

activations.role: Inverts the stance foot onto the little-toe edge and holds it against the snow force, then keeps the lifted ski tilted
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on the lateral edge, which the foot is not built for; not measured on snow. A balance effort, so it changes little with intensity

activations.role: Co-contract against the inverters for balance on the little-toe edge
activations.basis: Balancing on one edge needs both sides of the ankle; not measured on this edge

activations.role: Yields as the stance shin presses into the tongue and holds it with the boot shaft; idle once the ski is lifted, as pointing the foot would drop the tip
activations.basis: Modelled inside-ankle moments are about half the outside's in a normal turn; here the stance load is light, at the top of the turn

activations.role: Spread the pressure along the foot's outer border and make fine balance corrections
activations.basis: Anatomy and the mechanics of balancing on one ski; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shin's rotation under the loaded stance knee
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Controls the low back's bend back toward the outside, the counterbalance over each ski in turn
activations.basis: EMG off snow; the role here is mechanics. The bend grows with the edge angle, so the effort rises with intensity by inference

activations.role: Co-contracts with the inside side to steady the low back over the one edge
activations.basis: EMG off snow

activations.role: Helps the inside quadratus lumborum control the trunk's counterbalancing bend
activations.basis: Internal oblique ranks high in a model of carving; this side-bend role is mechanics

activations.role: Holds the upper body facing the fall line while the skis turn under it, paired with the inside external oblique
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns; the drill asks for the chest to stay to the fall line

activations.role: Pairs with the outside internal oblique to hold the upper body to the fall line
activations.basis: Measured and modelled in normal turns

activations.role: Steadies the trunk by co-contraction
activations.basis: Mechanics of the counter pairing

activations.role: Balances the back extensors so the low back stays slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped, and the skier stays off the tails
activations.basis: Measured at low levels in normal turns

activations.role: Hold the forward-folded trunk with the low back slightly flattened from standing, never arched or slumped; quiet, not rigid
activations.basis: Measured in normal turns; the low back carries a large combined load, highest here in the finish, where the load peaks

activations.role: Steadies each segment of the low back against twist
activations.basis: Linked to back complaints in racers; not measured in turns

activations.role: Stiffens the trunk so the upper body moves little when a ski is lifted
activations.basis: Anatomy; the association page asks for a torso stabilised by the core while a ski is lifted

activations.role: Keep the head level and the eyes steady as the body inclines
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the arms forward
activations.basis: Book technique point; not measured on snow

activations.role: Steadies the shoulder joints with the arms forward and the hands wide
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the shoulder blades forward with the hands
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Keeps the shoulders level
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Holds the elbows bent
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

activations.role: Hold the poles
activations.basis: Anatomy; not measured on snow

structures.mechanism: Loaded if the ski is set down with the leg straight and the skier behind it, or later the skier falls back on the one ski and its inner edge catches while the knee straightens and turns in, the slip-catch seen in racing injuries
Our inference from the dynamic snowplow, which the sources describe on a re-landing inside ski; here the outside ski lands wide, tip out, and catches, twisting the knee inward
Our inference from the same wide landing; the knee caving in opens its inner side
Pulled hard through the long single-leg hold at a deep knee bend, the drill's highest load, more so at higher intensity
Squeezed by forward flexion, side bend and twist combined under the turn load, with the side bend reversed in sense each time the stance changes ski

exercises.name: Banded ankle mobilisation, knee to wall
exercises.matches_on_snow: Room to flex the ankle so the shin can reach the tongue
exercises.easier: No band, foot closer to the wall
cautions: Pinching at the front of the ankle - ease off the range

ranges.note: The band sits low over the front of the ankle and pulls backward, gliding the ankle bone back while the knee drives forward over the toes, heel down. It mobilises; it never pulls the shin bone back.
ranges.basis: A racing book uses it as active recovery between squat sets in a sample block; its tables follow a general periodisation text, not a ski trial.

exercises.name: Banded standing march, hold at top
exercises.matches_on_snow: Holding the inside ski's tail up
cautions: Hip-flexor strain

ranges.note: Stand tall with the pelvis level; stop the set when the standing hip drops.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose. Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training.

ranges.note: Easy enough to breathe through the whole hold.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training. The rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

exercises.name: Copenhagen plank
cautions: Recent groin strain

ranges.note: Start with the knee on the bench; move to the foot only when the short lever is easy.
ranges.basis: A trial of the dynamic Copenhagen adduction found large adductor strength gains; this held version starts short because the groin is often sore at first.

ranges.note: Hips stay high and in line; end the set when they sag.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.matches_on_snow: A quiet trunk while the arms and legs move on their own
exercises.harder: Hold a light band or cable overhead
cautions: Low back arching off the floor - shorten the reach

exercises.name: Deep single-leg squat
exercises.matches_on_snow: Holding the knee over the foot on one bent leg, as on the stork's stance leg
cautions: Knee pain - reduce depth
Knee caving inward - stop the set

ranges.note: Lower slowly with the knee over the second toe; sit to a box until full depth is clean.
ranges.basis: An injury-prevention programme for young racers that cut injuries includes deep single-leg squats, done once a week; the book prints no sets or reps, so the counts are our conservative reading and the rest follows ACSM.

exercises.name: Hip airplane
exercises.matches_on_snow: The pelvis turning over a still stance thigh, as in counter, with the rotators braking
cautions: Hip impingement

ranges.note: Turn slowly, about 2-3 seconds each way, with the pelvis moving over a still stance leg.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

exercises.name: Isometric squat at two depths
exercises.matches_on_snow: The long, steady outside-leg hold at the peak of the turn
exercises.easier: Body weight against a wall, shallower bend
cautions: Knee pain - use the shallower depth
Hold your breath only briefly

ranges.note: Push hard against a fixed bar or a heavy load; split the sets between a shallow bend like skiing and a deeper one.
ranges.basis: A racing book's isometric guidance of short maximal holds adding to 30-50 seconds per muscle group, taken from a general periodisation text, not a ski trial; one national team tests isometric squats at two knee angles.

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl
exercises.matches_on_snow: Hamstring strength for the co-contraction that protects the ACL
cautions: Very sore at first - start with few reps

ranges.note: Lower as slowly as you can; begin at the low end, since soreness is heavy at first.
ranges.basis: Low volume to start, built up over weeks, as in progressive Nordic programmes; the rest follows ACSM's strength zone.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.matches_on_snow: A still upper body while the legs turn

ranges.note: Pause 2 seconds with the arms out; nothing rotates.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

ranges.note: Lighter band, short rest, same still trunk.
ranges.basis: Rep and rest ranges follow ACSM's endurance zone for healthy adults, kept at the conservative end.

exercises.name: Side plank with top-leg lift
cautions: Shoulder pain

ranges.note: Hips stacked and high; the top leg lifts without the pelvis rolling back.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

ranges.note: End the set when the hips sag or the shoulder complains.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance in an athletic stance
exercises.matches_on_snow: Balancing on one ski, where small corrections come from the foot and ankle
exercises.easier: Firm floor, eyes open, fingertip on a wall
exercises.harder: Stand on a balance pad, then close the eyes
cautions: Clear space around you before closing the eyes

ranges.note: Ankle, knee and hip bent as when skiing; progress to the pad only when the floor is steady, then to eyes closed.
ranges.basis: A racing book lists single-leg balance, made harder with the eyes closed, for off-snow proprioception and treats balance work as a supplement to strength work; the hold times are our own conservative reading.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
exercises.matches_on_snow: One-leg balance with a level pelvis
cautions: Acute low-back pain

ranges.note: Body weight, slow, pelvis level and square to the floor.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

ranges.note: A load you could lift one or two more times with clean form.
ranges.basis: Rep and rest ranges follow ACSM's strength zone for healthy adults, kept at the conservative end.

exercises.name: Lateral skater bound, stick the landing
exercises.matches_on_snow: Catching load on one leg without the knee caving in
cautions: Knee instability

ranges.note: Small hops; stick each landing for 2 seconds with the knee over the foot.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

ranges.note: Full rest between sets; stop when landings get loud or the knee caves in.
ranges.basis: Few reps with long rest, as in ACSM's power guidance.

exercises.name: Slow step-down
exercises.matches_on_snow: Eccentric knee control, lowering over 3-4 seconds
cautions: Knee pain - reduce depth

ranges.note: Lower over 3-4 seconds with the knee tracking over the second toe.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose; the rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

ranges.note: Higher step or added load, still lowering slowly.
ranges.basis: Rep and rest ranges follow ACSM's strength zone for healthy adults, kept at the conservative end.

exercises.name: Split-squat isometric hold
exercises.matches_on_snow: Holding the flexed stance at a ski-like knee bend
cautions: Knee pain

ranges.note: Held with load at a ski-like knee bend; hard by the end of the hold.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training. Isometric work gains strength mostly near the trained knee angle, so hold at the angle you ski.

ranges.note: Body weight; a steady burn, not a shake.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training.

exercises.name: Standing stork hold
exercises.matches_on_snow: The stork turn's shape - a bent stance leg, the free heel drawn up and the inside hip held up
exercises.easier: Fingertip on a wall, shorter hold
exercises.harder: Stand on a balance pad, or lean the trunk slightly toward the stance side as in a turn
cautions: Hamstring cramp - lower the heel and shorten the hold

ranges.note: Stance knee bent, free heel pulled up toward the seat with the thigh a little forward; end the hold when the free hip drops.
ranges.basis: Our own conservative reading for slow, form-first work, not a published dose. Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training.

ranges.note: Easy enough to breathe through the whole hold; the pelvis stays level.
ranges.basis: Body-weight holds sit well below a maximal effort, so the holds are longer than in maximal isometric training. The rest follows ACSM's general guidance.

exercises.name: Supine banded hip-flexor march
exercises.matches_on_snow: Drawing the inside thigh up with the hip already bent
exercises.harder: Pause with the thigh up, then lower slowly
cautions: Hip-flexor strain
Low back lifting off the floor - stop the set

exercises.name: Bent-knee calf raise and tibialis raise
exercises.matches_on_snow: Fore-aft balance in the boot, with the knee bent as when skiing
exercises.harder: Single leg, or a load held for the calf raise
cautions: Achilles pain - reduce range and load

ranges.note: Two legs, knees bent; lower each calf raise over about 3 seconds and hold each tibialis raise for 2 seconds at the top.
ranges.basis: Rep and rest ranges follow ACSM's endurance zone for healthy adults, kept at the conservative end.

ranges.note: Single leg or loaded, knee still bent; 3-second lowering on every calf raise.
ranges.basis: A racing book names tibialis anterior and soleus among the muscles to train and writes tempo as seconds of lowering; the rep and rest ranges follow ACSM's strength zone.

primitives.name: Stance-leg edge hold
primitives.summary: The outside leg holds the ski on edge under load, flexed at ankle, knee and hip.

primitives.name: Inside-leg shortening
primitives.summary: The inside leg flexes more than the outside one while it stays loaded, so both skis can tip together.

primitives.name: Ankle flexion into the tongue
primitives.summary: The shins move forward into the boot tongues, actively pulled by the muscles at the front of the shin.

primitives.name: Transition by extension
primitives.summary: The legs lengthen through the edge change.

primitives.name: Transition by flexion
primitives.summary: The legs shorten through the edge change and the body crosses over the skis.

primitives.name: Tipping and edge release
primitives.summary: The feet and lower legs roll the skis off one set of edges and onto the next.

primitives.name: Leg rotation
primitives.summary: The thighs turn in the hip sockets under a quiet pelvis to steer the skis.

primitives.name: Counter
primitives.summary: The pelvis and upper body face more toward the outside of the turn than the skis do.

primitives.name: Hip angulation
primitives.summary: The pelvis and spine tip toward the outside ski over the stance hip while the legs tilt in.

primitives.name: Inside-leg lift
primitives.summary: The unloaded inside leg is drawn up at hip and knee and held off the snow.

primitives.name: Edge set
primitives.summary: A sudden edge and flexion under a sharp rise in load, to brake or to rebound.

primitives.name: Pole swing and touch
primitives.summary: The inside arm swings the pole forward and touches it to time the turn.

fundamentals.name: Rotation
fundamentals.basis: Turning the legs in the hip sockets with a calm upper body

fundamentals.name: Edging
fundamentals.basis: Tilting the skis on and off their edges

fundamentals.name: Pressure control, ski to ski
fundamentals.basis: More pressure on the outside ski

fundamentals.name: Pressure control, fore/aft
fundamentals.basis: Pressure moved along the ski, tip to tail, through the ankle

fundamentals.name: Timing
fundamentals.basis: Timing has no single movement; the nearest are the pole touch and the timing of the transition

fundamentals.name: Fore-aft balance over the feet, with pressure along the ski
fundamentals.basis: Pressure moves along the ski mainly through the shin's angle in the boot

fundamentals.name: Pressure between the skis, mostly to the outside ski
fundamentals.basis: The outside leg takes the load while the inside leg shortens or lifts

fundamentals.name: Edge angle from leaning in and angulating
fundamentals.basis: Edges are tipped from the feet and held with angulation over the stance hip

fundamentals.name: Turning the skis with the legs, under a quiet upper body
fundamentals.basis: The legs turn in the hip sockets while the upper body faces outside the turn

fundamentals.name: How much pressure builds between ski and snow
fundamentals.basis: Pressure is managed by lengthening or shortening the legs, or by a sharp edge set
